field-theory.assignments-survive.lay: Choosing the spacetime volume element as the complex unit could in principle disturb the series' derivation of the particle content. It does not: the content, the charges and their consistency do not depend on the unit, and the only freedom is to conjugate all the particles together. Mixed choices are inconsistent, except for the neutral right-handed neutrino.

field-theory.boost-modes.formal: On a plane's mode operators the real-rapidity rotor acts by scaling, preserves the CAR, and is not a $*$-map; uniformly over many planes it has no bounded extension to the CAR algebra. The imaginary-rapidity rotor is unitary and acts by phases. So on the modes the series' geometric boost is the imaginary-time (KMS-strip) map, and the unitary real-time flow is the rotor at imaginary rapidity.
field-theory.boost-modes.technical: On a tower plane's mode operators the real-rapidity rotor acts by scaling $v$ and $v^*$ by inverse factors: it preserves the CAR but is not a $*$-map, and uniformly over many planes it has no bounded extension to the CAR algebra. The rotor at imaginary rapidity is unitary and acts by phases. So on the modes the series' geometric boost is the imaginary-time (KMS-strip) map, and the unitary real-time flow is the rotor at imaginary rapidity.
field-theory.boost-modes.lay: In the series a boost between observers is a rotation in a plane of the algebra. Acting on the tower's quantum modes, such a boost stretches and squeezes them rather than rotating them, so it is not a quantum symmetry in the usual sense. Its imaginary-angle counterpart is one, and the two are related as real and imaginary time are in thermal field theory.

field-theory.composite-gauge-bosons-what.formal: The GA current transforms as a vector, $J(Sf, Sg) = SJ(f,g)\tilde S$, for every element $S$ of definite parity; so a nonzero vector condensate breaks Lorentz invariance, and a massless composite photon as a Goldstone mode of one (Bjorken) conflicts with the exact Lorentz invariance of the series' exterior. Massless composites charged under a covariant current of the fermions are excluded by Weinberg and Witten. Massive composite vectors and gauge bosons of an emergent gauge symmetry are not addressed. The elementary route was taken because the author chose it, not because it is forced.

field-theory.composite-gauge-bosons-what.lay: One could try to build the photon out of pairs of fermions. Other composite routes are left open, so making the photon elementary was a choice, not a necessity.

field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-fiel.technical:
At mean-field level. The two-mode block $H = K(n_a + n_c) + \mu w_aw_c + \mu^*v_cv_a$ with $\mu \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ is self-adjoint, with $\operatorname{ad}_H^2 = K^2 + |\mu|^2$ on all four mode operators and block spectrum $\{K - E, K, K, K + E\}$, $E = \sqrt{K^2 + |\mu|^2}$; with $\mu = mB$ the dispersion is $E^2 = K^2 + m^2$. The tower element $H_4 = \sum_b K(n_a + n_c) - GP^*P$, $P = \sum_b w_aw_c$, is self-adjoint, conserves the axial number and has exact pair states of energy $2Kn - Gn(n_b - n + 1)$; pairs enter the ground state exactly when $G > 2K/n_b$, the threshold of the mean-field energy.

In the block ground state $\langle w_aw_c\rangle = -\mu^*/(2E)$, so the gap equation holds: the fermion mass is $G$ times the pair condensate. The axial phase is an inner unitary of the tower, $UH(\mu)U^* = H(\mu e^{-2\theta I_4})$, so the mean-field energy has an exactly flat phase direction.
field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-fiel.lay: A pair of fermion modes in the tower can bind into a scalar condensate that gives the fermions mass, the mechanism of Nambu and Jona-Lasinio. At mean-field level these exact computations reproduce its ingredients: the massive energy relation, the coupling above which pairs condense, the gap equation, and a direction in which the condensate's phase can turn at no cost.

field-theory.conserved-numbers-mass-bloc.formal: On the mass block of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(1) the quasi-particle annihilators $\gamma_a = \alpha w_a + \beta v_c$, $\gamma_c = \alpha'w_c + \beta'v_a$ satisfy $[H, \gamma] = -E\gamma$, and $H = E(N_a + N_c) + (K - E)$ exactly, with $N = \gamma^*\gamma/\{\gamma, \gamma^*\}$. A single rung number does not commute with $H$ when $\mu \neq 0$, and the massive vacuum has $\langle n_a\rangle = (E - K)/(2E)$. __notes__.note.field-theory.setting-gravitys-sourc: The series registers that gravity entangles two masses, each held in a superposition of two places, by the standard phase $\Phi = (Gm_Am_B/\hbar)\int(1/r_{11} + 1/r_{22} - 1/r_{12} - 1/r_{21})\,dt$, under the element reading, in which the geometry's coefficients lie in a commuting algebra of the matter's number operators. The masses are the field theory's fermions; gravity is not quantised here.
__notes__.note.field-theory.what-does-registration: Nothing. The registered phase and its wording stand: ``the commuting algebra of the rungs' number operators'' is right when read as the conserved ones, which the block charge supplies inside the rung algebra. A first version of the run proposed changing the wording to quasi-particle numbers; review showed the charge serves equally, and the proposal was withdrawn.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-open: (1) Pair creation, antiparticle modes and Compton scattering in the coupled system. (2) Gauge invariance beyond current conservation, and Lorentz covariance of the Coulomb-gauge construction beyond tree level. (3) Loops and renormalisation. (4) Non-abelian gauge fields, which bring the axial anomaly into play. (5) The composite scalar beyond mean field: the Goldstone pole, a covariant regularisation, the sigma mode, and whether the contact term of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.contact-interactions-tower} has an attractive scalar channel. (6) The map from the palatial ladder module's conformal-energy basis to the plane-wave Fock space, which would turn the analogy of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(1) into a construction. (7) The terminology conflict recorded in the first run: T03 calls the tower second quantisation and T09 calls the palatial storey second quantisation; on the attachment found here the palatial storey supplies the one-particle space and the tower's CAR over it is second quantisation, which is T03's usage. (8) Whether the Higgs is composite, which the tower supports at mean-field level, or elementary: a modelling decision. (9) The relative sign of the twistor's complex unit and the field's, which now carries T12's orientation, and a check of the conventions of T12's Fact on twistor charge and helicity against T09 and T07. (10) For the gravity prediction: retardation and the radiative sector, non-rigid bodies, and the shared spinor factor of two masses in one tower.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-what-series-ow: Three things. (i) Where the field theory's one-particle structure comes from: the palatial storey, not the tower (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}); the tower supplies the CAR and nothing about spacetime (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.ground-does-not-attach-modes}). (ii) Why the canonical commutation relations must be adjoined: the tower's own bosons are $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ quasi-spins (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}), the field-theory form of T09's statistics no-go. (iii) What one complex unit fixes: with $i = I_4$, positive frequency is positive helicity for every massless field, so the opposite helicities and chiralities enter conjugated in one stroke (Propositions \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(4), \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(3)). The dictionary of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes}, the boost on the modes as the KMS-strip map, is transport-convenient: its mathematics is that of any hyperbolic plane, its use the series'.
__notes__.note.field-theory.abstract: The tower of the series has the canonical anticommutation relations as its limit; this note asks whether that limit reaches a quantum field theory. It does, in one way. The palatial storey supplies a positive-energy one-particle space, the Penrose transform supplies the mode functions, and the tower's anticommutation relations are the second quantisation over that space. In real geometric algebra the construction needs one operator imaginary unit, and the pseudoscalar $I_4$ serves: it is Lorentz-invariant, and with it positive frequency is positive helicity for every massless field. A massive fermion is then two right-handed fields joined by the epsilon pairing; tower contact interactions give the textbook scattering laws; a tower pairing interaction condenses into a fermion mass; gauge bosons are adjoined as a bosonic Fock space; and the coupled system gives one-photon exchange exactly, for distinguishable and identical fermions. Pointed at the series' gravity prediction, the field theory is consistent with its matter premises and leaves the registered phase unchanged. Pointed at the Standard-Model paper, the assignments survive, and the paper's undetermined orientation is relocated into the relative sign of the twistor's complex unit and the field's. Almost every result is standard physics in the series' algebra; the series' own content is where the one-particle structure comes from, why the commutation relations must be adjoined, and what one complex unit fixes. Exact-arithmetic checks accompany every claim.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-introduction:
The relation of T16, $\{e_a, e_b\} = 2g_{ab}$, has two readings: a metric one in an orthogonal basis and the canonical anticommutation relations (CAR) in a Witt basis. The tower of T03 iterates the ascent and has the CAR algebra as its limit. That limit is many-fermion quantum mechanics. Whether it reaches a quantum field theory, with fields on spacetime that are local, covariant and of positive energy, is a different question, and the claim that general relativity and quantum theory are two faces of one object covers field theory only if the answer is yes.

This note collects the answer, built in eight exact-arithmetic runs on 15 and 16 October 2026, each with a preregistration, an independent adversarial review and its corrections. The answer is yes, in one way. The note is a consolidation: each result is stated at its level and cited to the run and check that establish it, and the runs' findings files carry the detail.

The plan. the section “Setting and imports” fixes the setting and the imports. the section “Attaching the modes to spacetime” attaches the modes to spacetime. the section “The imaginary units in real geometric algebra” identifies the imaginary units in real geometric algebra. the section “Second quantisation in one algebra” second-quantises multivector-valued fields in one algebra with $i = I_4$. the section “Mass and contact interactions” treats mass and contact interactions, the section “Bosons” the bosons, and the section “The photon's Fock space and the coupled system” the photon's Fock space and the coupled system. the section “Gravity's source: the registered prediction” and the section “The Standard-Model paper's chirality” point the result at two of the series' own claims: the registered gravity prediction and the Standard-Model paper's chirality. the section “The ledger” states what is the series' own, what is imported, and what is open.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-prior-art: Second quantisation, Coulomb-gauge quantum electrodynamics and old-fashioned perturbation theory are textbook (Sakurai; Weinberg, \emph{The Quantum Theory of Fields}, vol.~I). The spacetime algebra, its plane waves, its chirality and its photon polarisations are Hestenes' and Doran and Lasenby's; the geometric-algebra treatment of twistors with the conformal pseudoscalar as imaginary unit is Arcaute, Lasenby and Doran's. Two-component spinor technique is Dreiner, Haber and Martin's. The Nambu-Jona-Lasinio mechanism, Weinberg and Witten's theorem, Bjorken's composite photon and Anderson's quasi-spin are standard and credited where used. What the note claims for the series is the placement of these structures in the series' own algebra and storeys, and the consequences of using a single complex unit for all of them.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-setting-import: The ground is $\Cl(1,3)$ with signature $(+,-,-,-)$ and pseudoscalar $I_4 = \gamma_0\gamma_1\gamma_2\gamma_3$, $I_4^2 = -1$. Tower planes $(e_j, f_j)$ with $e_j^2 = 1$, $f_j^2 = -1$ are adjoined after the ground; $v_j = (e_j + f_j)/2$ creates and $w_j = (e_j - f_j)/2$ annihilates. T03's adjoint $*$ is the antiautomorphism with $x^* = x$ on generators of square $+1$ and $x^* = -x$ on generators of square $-1$; so $I_4^* = -I_4$ and $w_j^* = v_j$. Hestenes' unit $\IS = \gamma_2\gamma_1$ acts on the right. The chirality projectors on even elements are $\chi_\pm(\phi) = (\phi \mp I_4\phi\IS)/2$, so that $I_4\phi = \phi\IS$ on $\chi_+$.
__notes__.note.field-theory.choice-unit: The author adopted $i = I_4$ for the series' field theory on 16 October 2026. The reasons are Lorentz invariance and centrality; the cost is that every field is read in one chirality. Proposition \claimref{field-theory.mass} shows the cost is the standard two-component one.
__notes__.note.field-theory.what-does-t12: T12's orientation bit, which the dark-matter paper shows the descent cannot derive, is not removed by $i = I_4$; it moves into the relative sign of the conformal spinors' unit ($\pm I_6$, the twistor's unit) and the field's. If the series fixes that sign, and if the label copy's parity is identified with the conformal spinors' (the twistor's; the theorem T12 calls the same missing theorem as Hypothesis (S)), the orientation is fixed, through T12's Fact on the charge and helicity read on the conformal spinor space (twistor charge and helicity), whose conventions were not checked here. Its physical content would be at most the sign of CP violation.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-what-standard: Everything else: two-component mass, Fermi contact scattering, the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio condensate, Coulomb-gauge exchange and the quasi-spin are textbook results reproduced in the series' algebra. None of the runs produced a transport-essential result. The gravity run left the registered prediction unchanged and found its matter premises consistent with the field theory; the Standard-Model run found T12's assignments independent of the unit and relocated, but did not remove, its orientation bit.
__notes__.note.field-theory.setting-decisions-take: The author chose $i = I_4$ (16 October), composite bosons first and elementary bosons on their failure, then the elementary photon, and then to point the field theory at the gravity prediction and at T12.

__notes__.note.synthesis.n-plus-orientation-datum: Premise (N$_{+}$) (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}) assumes the orientation of the field's unit $I_{4}$ relative to the time orientation, which decides between the null vacuum and the filled positive-energy sea. Three facts now locate that datum. First, with the unit $I_{4}$ every massless mode's helicity is locked to its frequency sign, every map commuting with the Lorentz rotors is $I_{4}$-linear, and among the discrete maps of the massless field the frequency sign flips exactly under reversal of spatial orientation; Hestenes' charge conjugation flips the chirality of massless even spinors and not the frequency sign, and a CP map flips the frequency sign and not the chirality (\claimref{synthesis.massless-frequency-sign-relative-to-i4-is-not-the-chirality}). So the datum is odd under P and under CP, it is not that chirality, and no CP-invariant interaction fixes it. Second, on the Witt flags of $\R^{2,4}$ adapted to the conformal energy, the energy sign of a flag's vacuum and the stored flag bit flip together on each pair of conjugate flags (\claimref{synthesis.z-adapted-witt-flags-energy-sign-follows-the-flag-bit}), so read as the energy sign of the flag's vacuum the datum is the descent's flag bit (\claimref{dark-matter.premise-flag-as-datum}) up to the descent's kinematic sign on the four-space orthogonal to $Z$. Third, on every field the Hadamard deposit premise reaches, the datum is carried by that premise, through results that rest on no postulate (\claimref{synthesis.hadamard-scaling-limit-premise}). What is not shown is that the generators' modes inherit the descent's flag; on the eternal hole and eternal de Sitter, which no descent reaches, the datum stays assumed.

field-theory.elementary-photon-ga.technical:
With $i = I_4$ and complex coefficients on the left, the polarisation $\epsilon_h = t_1 - hI_4t_2$ satisfies $B_q\cdot\epsilon_h = hI_4\epsilon_h$ for the rotation bivector $B_q$ about $q$, on and off the coordinate axes; the geometric product of complex vectors is sesquilinear, $\proj(J\epsilon) = J\cdot\bar\epsilon$, because $I_4$ anticommutes with vectors; and the helicity sum $\tfrac12\sum_h\proj(J_A\epsilon_h)\proj(J_B\epsilon_{-h})$ is the transverse product $J_A^\perp\cdot J_B^\perp$.

Coulomb-gauge exchange, two time orderings and the instantaneous Coulomb term, equals the covariant $-e^2J_A\cdot J_B/t$, given current conservation, and massive vector exchange reduces to the contact term with $G = e^2/M^2$.

field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes.technical:
On polynomials with $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ coefficients, $a_m = \partial/\partial z_m$ and $a_m^* = z_m$ satisfy the CCR exactly, and $a_m^*$ is the adjoint of $a_m$ for $\ip{z^n}{z^{n'}} = n!\,\delta$: the polynomial representation of the palatial algebra, with variables indexed by photon modes, the relation to the palatial algebra itself being an analogy, not a construction. For null $k$ the bivectors $f$ with $kf = 0$ form a real two-dimensional $I_4$-stable space, one $I_4$-complex mode per momentum.

The positive-frequency mode $f\exp(-I_4k\cdot x)$ has helicity $+1$, and every massless even spinor of either chirality has the left-$I_4$ rotation phase of helicity $+\tfrac12$; so with $i = I_4$ positive frequency is positive helicity for every massless even field, and the field operator is the Riemann-Silberstein form $F = \sum N\,2X\,[\exp(-I_4k\cdot x)\,a_+ + \exp(+I_4k\cdot x)\,a_-^*]$, which annihilates helicity $+1$ and creates helicity $-1$.
field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes.lay: The photon's quantum states are built on polynomials, the standard representation of boson operators, with the spacetime volume element as imaginary unit. Each photon momentum then carries one complex mode, and with this choice of unit positive frequency coincides with positive helicity for every massless field, so the field operator destroys one helicity and creates the other.

field-theory.ground-does-not-attach-mode.formal: Over the conformal ground every even ground element commutes with every mode operator of every higher plane. In particular the conformal bivectors, the chart translations and the Lorentz rotors act trivially on the modes, so a field $\psi(x) = \sum_j u_j(x)a_j$ on which the ground's translations act covariantly has constant mode functions. The obstruction is finite-dimensionality: a noncompact group has no nontrivial unitary representation on a finite floor.
field-theory.ground-does-not-attach-mode.technical: Over the conformal ground every even ground element commutes with every mode operator of every higher plane. So the conformal bivectors, the chart translations and the Lorentz rotors act trivially on the modes, and a field $\psi(x) = \sum_ju_j(x)a_j$ on which the ground's translations act covariantly has constant mode functions. The obstruction is finite-dimensionality: a noncompact group has no nontrivial unitary representation on a finite floor.
field-theory.ground-does-not-attach-mode.lay: The tower adds quantum modes on top of the spacetime algebra, but the spacetime symmetries, translations, rotations and boosts, do not act on those modes at all. So the tower alone cannot place its modes in spacetime; something else must supply the link.

field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr.formal: For $n$ tower pairs, $B = \sum_jw_{c_j}w_{d_j}$ gives $[B, B^*] = n - (N_c + N_d)$; with $K_3 = (N_c + N_d - n)/2$ the triple $(B^*, B, K_3)$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ quasi-spin, the ladder has $n + 1$ states, and $[b, b^*] = 1 - 2k/n$ on $k$-pair states for $b = B/\sqrt{n}$. The CCR is the Inonu-Wigner contraction $n \to \infty$; the operator limit holds only on states of bounded boson number.
field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr.technical: For $n$ tower pairs, $B = \sum_jw_{c_j}w_{d_j}$ gives $[B, B^*] = n - (N_c + N_d)$; with $K_3 = (N_c + N_d - n)/2$ the triple $(B^*, B, K_3)$ is an $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ quasi-spin, the ladder has $n + 1$ states, and $[b, b^*] = 1 - 2k/n$ on $k$-pair states for $b = B/\sqrt{n}$. The CCR are the Inonu-Wigner contraction $n \to \infty$, and the operator limit holds only on states of bounded boson number.
field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr.lay: Pairs of fermion modes in the tower behave almost like bosons, but not exactly: they form a finite ladder of states, like a quantum spin. The exact boson relations appear only in the limit of infinitely many pairs, and then only for states with a bounded number of bosons.

field-theory.imported-standard-field-the.formal:
The Jost-point form of the spin-statistics theorem (Streater and Wightman, ch.~4), whose complex Lorentz path reads in geometric algebra as the rotation of one chirality through $2\pi$, $(1-\Pi) + \Pi\exp(\theta\gamma_1\gamma_2)$ with $\Pi = (1 - E)/2$, ending at conjugation by $E$, the total inversion $x \mapsto -x$ on the conformal model; the Penrose transform, whose kernels the spacetime algebra writes as $x\psi_0\gamma_0/Q(x)^2$ (spin $\tfrac12$), $xBx/Q(x)^3$ (Maxwell) and $1/Q(x)$ (scalar), and its $H^1$ isomorphism with cohomology on regions of the projective spinor space $\PCS$ (projective twistor space); the Weinberg-Witten theorem (massless particles of spin greater than one half carry no charge under a conserved Lorentz-covariant current); the random-phase Goldstone pole of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model; the Coulomb-gauge Hamiltonian of quantum electrodynamics; the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly.

\emph{Note (spin and statistics, 2026-11-01).} For the attached free fields (scalar, spinor, photon) the statistics follow from locality with a positive norm, given the massless two-point function (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}); the Jost-point form imported here is kept for interacting fields. The KMS condition at rapidity period $2\pi$ of the thermal premises (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}, and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}) holds for CAR and CCR modes alike and does not fix statistics (\claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}); modular covariance of the wedge algebras, which would fix them through an imported theorem, is not a premise of the store.

\emph{Note (the Jost import, 2 November 2026).} The Jost-point form is needed only beyond perturbation theory: in causal perturbation theory the interacting fields keep the spin-statistics connection of the free fields to every order, on every field with an even number of ghost factors (\claimref{synthesis.interacting-fields-of-causal-perturbation-theory-keep-the-spin-statistics-connection-at-even-ghost-number}). Beyond perturbation theory a premise remains. Kuckert's modular P$_{1}$CT symmetry (the modular conjugation of each wedge algebra acts on the local algebras as the wedge's reflection), with covariance under the covering group, the spectrum condition and compact internal symmetries, is a weaker alternative premise from which the connection follows (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-kuckert-modular-pct-spin-statistics-and-borchers-theorem}; its spacetime-algebra form, \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}); it is recorded here as a note only, not adopted, and nothing in the store supplies it. The imports listed above are unchanged.
field-theory.imported-standard-field-the.technical:
Six standard results that the field-theory note imports: the Jost-point form of the spin-statistics theorem; the Penrose transform and its $H^1$ isomorphism; the Weinberg-Witten theorem, that massless particles of spin greater than one half carry no charge under a conserved Lorentz-covariant current; the random-phase Goldstone pole of the Nambu-Jona-Lasinio model; the Coulomb-gauge Hamiltonian of quantum electrodynamics; and the Adler-Bell-Jackiw anomaly. (Note, 2026-11-01: for the attached free fields the spin-statistics connection follows from locality with a positive norm, \claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}; the Jost-point import is kept for interacting fields, and the thermal period alone does not fix statistics, \claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}.) (Note, 2 November 2026: the Jost-point import is needed only beyond perturbation theory, since causal perturbation theory carries the free fields' spin-statistics connection to interacting fields order by order, \claimref{synthesis.interacting-fields-of-causal-perturbation-theory-keep-the-spin-statistics-connection-at-even-ghost-number}; Kuckert's modular P$_{1}$CT symmetry with the spectrum condition would be a weaker premise there, noted and not adopted, \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}.)

In geometric algebra Jost's complex Lorentz path is the rotation of one chirality through $2\pi$, ending at conjugation by the ascent bivector $E$, and the Penrose transform's kernels are $x\psi_0\gamma_0/Q(x)^2$ for spin $\tfrac12$, $xBx/Q(x)^3$ for Maxwell and $1/Q(x)$ for the scalar, with the cohomology taken on regions of the projective spinor space $\PCS$.

field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-p.formal: The palatial algebra $[Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\,\delta^\alpha_\beta$ has no nonzero finite-dimensional representation and no embedding into any finite-dimensional algebra. It is realised on polynomials by $\bar Z_\beta = -\hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\beta$. \emph{Provenance:} T09, Prop.~prop:statistics and Lemma lem:weyl. For the bounded CAR algebra the corresponding statement is the Wielandt-Wintner theorem: no bounded operators satisfy $[a, a^*] = 1$.
field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-p.technical: The palatial algebra $[Z^\alpha, \bar Z_\beta] = \hbar\,\delta^\alpha_\beta$ has no nonzero finite-dimensional representation and no embedding into any finite-dimensional algebra, and it is realised on polynomials by $\bar Z_\beta = -\hbar\,\partial/\partial Z^\beta$. For the bounded CAR algebra the corresponding statement is the Wielandt-Wintner theorem: no bounded operators satisfy $[a, a^*] = 1$.
field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-p.lay: The canonical commutation relations of bosons cannot be realised by finite matrices, nor inside any finite-dimensional algebra such as a floor of the tower; they need infinitely many states, as in the standard representation on polynomials. Even in the infinite tower they cannot be realised by bounded operators.

field-theory.mass.formal: For the four even right factors $N \in \{\gamma_0\gamma_1, \gamma_0\gamma_2, \gamma_1\gamma_3, \gamma_2\gamma_3\}$ that anticommute with $\IS$, $B_N(\psi, \phi) = \proj(\tilde\psi\phi N)$ is a nonzero, antisymmetric, nondegenerate, Lorentz-invariant, $I_4$-bilinear pairing on $\chi_+$: the epsilon pairing $\lambda^{\mathsf T}\epsilon\lambda$, of charge two under the common phase. A massive Dirac plane wave splits as $\chi + \psi_-$ with $\eta = \psi_-N \in \chi_+$; $\chi$ and $\eta$ have opposite $I_4$-charges, the Dirac equation is the coupled pair, and the mass density is $2B(\chi, \eta)$. The common $I_4$ phase is axial and the mass breaks it. Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-one-datum-massive-law} stands: $I_4$ is the field algebra's unit, not the massive law's complex structure.
field-theory.mass.technical:
For the four even right factors $N \in \{\gamma_0\gamma_1, \gamma_0\gamma_2, \gamma_1\gamma_3, \gamma_2\gamma_3\}$ that anticommute with $\IS$, the pairing $B_N(\psi, \phi) = \proj(\tilde\psi\phi N)$ is nonzero, antisymmetric, nondegenerate, Lorentz-invariant and $I_4$-bilinear on $\chi_+$: the epsilon pairing $\lambda^{\mathsf T}\epsilon\lambda$, of charge two under the common phase. A massive Dirac plane wave splits as $\chi + \psi_-$ with $\eta = \psi_-N \in \chi_+$; $\chi$ and $\eta$ have opposite $I_4$-charges, the Dirac equation is the coupled pair, and the mass density is $2B(\chi, \eta)$.

So the common $I_4$ phase is axial and the mass breaks it, and the one-datum fact stands: $I_4$ is the field algebra's unit, not the massive law's complex structure.
field-theory.mass.lay: With the spacetime volume element as imaginary unit every field is read in one chirality, and a mass couples a left-handed part to a right-handed one. The mass term then takes exactly the standard two-component form. The unit belongs to the field algebra, not to the massive equation, which still needs its own geometric datum.

field-theory.orientation-relocated.technical:
Left multiplication by $e_+$ maps the even half $T$ of the conformal spinor module onto the odd half $T'$, commutes with $I_4$ and the Lorentz rotors and swaps the $E$-doublets, so $i = I_4$ and Lorentz symmetry alone cannot tell the halves apart. The unit commuting with Clifford multiplication is right multiplication by $I_6$, $J$; with it the halves are inequivalent, and on the momentum doublet $\ker n_0$, the $E = +1$ doublet of both halves, $J = +I_4$ in $T$ and $J = -I_4$ in $T'$.

Since the commutant fixes $J$ only up to sign, with the field's unit $I_4$ the question of which half's momentum spinors are complex-linear is the relative sign of $J$ and $I_4$.
field-theory.orientation-relocated.lay: The Standard-Model paper's matter keeps one binary choice, an orientation that tells particles from antiparticles. Fixing the field's imaginary unit does not remove it: the two halves of the conformal spinor space look the same to that unit and to relativity. The choice reappears as the relative sign between the field's unit and the conformal spinors' own unit.

field-theory.second-quantisation.formal:
With Definition \claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Lambda(k) = k\gamma_0/(2k_0)$ is the orthogonal projector onto $\ker k$.
\item The field's anticommutator has no tower part and equals $\ip{\phi_1}{\sum_j 2\alpha_j\cos(k_j\cdot\xi)\Lambda(k_j)\chi\,\phi_2}$; in the continuum it is $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_0$ with $D$ the Pauli-Jordan function, so the field is local.
\item The span$\{1, I_4\}$ part of $\Psi^*M\Psi$ is the second-quantised $d\Gamma(M)$ on particle modes; antiparticle terms need normal ordering.
\item With $i = I_4$ a field carrying both chiralities gives the right-handed part complex-linearly and the left-handed part conjugated. With Hestenes' $i = \IS$ the same field quantises as a whole Dirac field, at the cost of a frame-dependent unit. The split is forced by the choice $i = I_4$, not by the algebra.
\end{enumerate}
field-theory.second-quantisation.technical:
With the single-algebra field, $\Lambda(k) = k\gamma_0/(2k_0)$ is the orthogonal projector onto $\ker k$, and the field's anticommutator has no tower part and equals $\ip{\phi_1}{\sum_j 2\alpha_j\cos(k_j\cdot\xi)\Lambda(k_j)\chi\,\phi_2}$; in the continuum it is $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_0$ with $D$ the Pauli-Jordan function, so the field is local. The $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ part of $\Psi^*M\Psi$ is the second-quantised $d\Gamma(M)$ on particle modes, with antiparticle terms needing normal ordering.

With $i = I_4$ a field carrying both chiralities gives the right-handed part complex-linearly and the left-handed part conjugated; with Hestenes' $i = \IS$ the same field quantises as a whole Dirac field, at the cost of a frame-dependent unit. The split is forced by the choice $i = I_4$, not by the algebra.
field-theory.second-quantisation.lay: Fields whose values are elements of the spacetime algebra and whose modes are tower planes can be quantised inside one algebra, with the volume element as imaginary unit. The resulting field is local, and its observables are the standard second-quantised ones. The price of this unit is that a field's two chiralities enter differently, one directly and one conjugated; Hestenes' unit avoids that at the cost of choosing a frame.

field-theory.twistor-attachment.formal:
The attachment available to the series is the one through the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (the twistor attachment): the palatial storey supplies a positive-energy one-particle space with a conformal-group action, the Penrose transform supplies the mode functions, and the tower's CAR is the second quantisation over that space. In the oscillator model the helicity-$s$ module has energies $|s| + 1 + n$ with multiplicity $(n+1)(n + 2|s| + 1)$; the conformal energy is the palatial quadratic of the reversion form $h$ on $\CS$ (the twistor form); the sixteen generators of $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$, the algebra preserving $h$, preserve each positive-energy, fixed-helicity module. On this attachment the tower's floors are energy cut-offs, not regions of spacetime. Spin-statistics constrains it: a CAR lift is local exactly when $2s$ is odd, and the series' fermion assignments pass.

\emph{Note (spin and statistics, 2026-11-01).} For the attached free fields (scalar, spinor, photon) the clause on CAR lifts follows from locality with a positive norm, given the massless two-point function (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}); the Jost-point form of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-standard-field-theory} is kept for interacting fields. The positive norm is needed: with an indefinite (Krein) form a CAR scalar is local, the case of the Faddeev-Popov ghosts. The KMS condition at rapidity period $2\pi$ of the thermal premises (\claimref{synthesis.n-plus-null-ground-state}, and (R$_{\mathrm{loc}}$) of \claimref{synthesis.c-loc-local-horizon-premise}) holds for CAR and CCR modes alike and does not fix statistics (\claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}); modular covariance, which would fix them through an imported theorem, is not a premise of the store.

field-theory.where-each-lives.technical:
The centre of $\Cl^+(1,3)$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_4\}$ and that of $\Cl^+(2,4)$ is $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_6\}$, with $I_6 = I_4E$ for the ascended plane's bivector $E = e_+e_-$, $E^2 = 1$, $[I_4, E] = 0$. The conformal spinor space $\CS = \Cl^+(2,4)P$ has commutant $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_6\}$, so its complex unit is $\pm I_6$; at a point it splits into the Lorentz-invariant $E = \pm 1$ eigenspaces $L_0 \oplus L_\infty$, on which $I_6 = +I_4$ and $-I_4$: the two chiral doublets.

For massless fields the complex structure is the pseudoscalar, $\pm I_4$ by helicity sector for Maxwell, and on the chiral subspaces of the Weyl field $I_4$ agrees with Hestenes' right $\IS$ up to the chirality sign; a mass term anticommutes with $I_4$.
field-theory.where-each-lives.lay: Every square root of minus one the field theory needs is an element of the real geometric algebra. The conformal spinors' unit is the conformal volume element, which on the spinors at a point becomes the spacetime volume element with a sign set by chirality. For massless fields the unit is the spacetime volume element, which agrees with Hestenes' choice up to that sign, while a mass term does not commute with it.

synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-o.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a torsion-free gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), $\Omega_{T}$ its tractor gauge field and $F_{T}$ the field strength of $\Omega_{T}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}), and let a bivector of $\Cl(2,4)$ act on the conformal spinor space $\CS$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}) by left multiplication, so that a $\CS$-valued field is parallel when $a\cdot\nabla\psi + \tfrac12\Omega_{T}(a)\psi = 0$ for every $a$, and a bivector field $X$ (an adjoint tractor) when $a\cdot\nabla X + \Omega_{T}(a)\times X = 0$. Write $\mathcal{W}$ for the Weyl curvature, an $I_{4}$-linear map on spacetime bivectors, and give each point the Petrov type of $\mathcal{W}$ there.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Ricci blindness; proved.)} $F_{T}(A\wedge B) = -\mathcal{W}(A\wedge B) + \nO\wedge C(A, B)$, with $C$ the Cotton term: the Schouten map, hence the Ricci curvature, enters only through $C$, which vanishes on every Einstein space (Ricci curvature proportional to the metric, $\Sch = \tfrac{\Lambda}{6}\id$); under Einstein's equations with matter it does not vanish in general.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Parallel conformal spinors; proved.)} A parallel $\CS$-valued field is annihilated by every $F_{T}(A\wedge B)$ at every point. The subspace of $\CS$ annihilated by the Weyl bivectors has complex dimension $4$ at type O points, $2$ at type N points, where it is the subspace annihilated by left multiplication by the repeated principal null vector $k$, and $0$ at points of type I, II, D and III; a nonzero Cotton term can only reduce it. Where $F_{T} = 0$ on a simply connected region (in four dimensions this is the case exactly where $\mathcal{W} = 0$, by the twistor-flat result (\claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein})) the parallel conformal spinors form a space of complex dimension $4$ carrying the attachment's $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$ action, form $h$ and grading $Z$ unchanged.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(No conformal-energy generator; proved.)} The bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$ commuting with every $F_{T}(A\wedge B)$, which contain every parallel adjoint tractor, span $15$ dimensions at type O points, $5$ at type N points and $1$ (the multiples of $E = e_{+}e_{-}$) at points of type I, II, D and III; at every point with $\mathcal{W} \neq 0$ each of them annihilates a null vector under the commutator product, while every nonzero multiple of a rotor conjugate of the attachment's conformal-energy generator $Z = e_{0}\nu$ (the grading of the massless, conformally invariant modules; for massive fields $Z$ is not a symmetry even where $\mathcal{W} = 0$) annihilates only a negative-definite $4$-plane. So no conformal-energy generator is parallel through a point where the Weyl curvature is nonzero.
\end{enumerate}
Hence the tractor transport carries the attachment's one-particle structure across a region only where $\mathcal{W} = 0$: on a general gravitational field the attachment's tractor transport does not construct the one-particle space and supplies no state (no choice of positive frequency); a state must come from another construction, which this result does not exclude.
synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-o.technical:
The series attaches its modes to spacetime through the conformal spinor space: a four-dimensional complex space with an invariant form of signature $(2,2)$, the conformal algebra $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$ acting on it, and the central rotation $Z$, whose grading gives the positive conformal energy. On a gravitational field the natural way to carry this space from point to point is the tractor gauge field, and the space survives transport only where that field's curvature annihilates it.

The curvature acting on conformal spinors is minus the Weyl curvature plus a Cotton term; the Ricci curvature, and with it the matter, drops out. Where the Weyl curvature vanishes the whole space is parallel (on such regions the Cotton term vanishes too, by the twistor-flat result (\claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein})). Where it does not, the annihilated part has complex dimension $2$ at points of Petrov type N (the spinors killed by the repeated principal null vector) and $0$ at points of every other type, the standard integrability condition of the twistor equation reproduced in $\Cl(2,4)$. No conformal-energy generator commutes with a nonzero Weyl curvature either: everything that does annihilates a null vector, while such a generator annihilates only a negative-definite plane.

So off Weyl-flat regions the attachment's tractor transport gives no one-particle space and supplies no state, the choice of positive frequency; that choice has to come from another construction. The grading $Z$ concerns the massless, conformally invariant modules. The result is transport-convenient.
synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-o.lay: The series links its quantum modes to spacetime through a special four-dimensional space of spinors, which in flat space comes with a built-in notion of positive energy. In a gravitational field one has to carry that space from point to point, and gravity's tidal part, the Weyl curvature, twists it on the way. This result shows that the space survives only where that tidal part vanishes: at a point of one special radiation type half of it can survive, and at every other point none of it, and the built-in notion of positive energy is lost. So in a general gravitational field this way of attaching the modes does not fix the quantum state; the state has to be supplied in some other way.

proofs.main:
Work in $\Cl(2,4)$ with the generators of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection} ($e_{0}$, $e_{+}$ squaring to $+1$; $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{-}$ to $-1$; $
O = 	frac12(e_{+} + e_{-})$, $
Inf = e_{+} - e_{-}$), so $
u = e_{+}$ and $Z = e_{0}e_{+}$ in the notation of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z}. By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.where-each-lives}, $\CS$ is the minimal left ideal $\Cl^{+}(2,4)P$, with complex unit $I_{6} = I_{4}E$ ($E = e_{+}e_{-}$) and the splitting $\CS = L_{0} \oplus L_{\infty}$ into the two chiral doublets, on which $I_{6} = \pm I_{4}$. So $\Cl^{+}(2,4)$, a complex algebra of complex dimension $16$, acts on itself from the left as four copies of $\CS$, and the subspace of $\CS$ annihilated by a set of bivectors has complex dimension one eighth of the real dimension of their common left kernel on $\Cl^{+}(2,4)$; the checks compute that kernel.

\emph{Transport and integrability.} The tractor gauge field acts on a $\CS$-valued field through the spin action, $D^{T}_{a}\psi = a\cdot
abla\psi + 	frac12\Omega_{T}(a)\psi$, whose commutator on the plane of $a, b$ is $	frac12 F_{T}(a\wedge b)\psi$ with $F_{T}$ the field strength of $\Omega_{T}$ (the standard curvature of a gauge field with the gauge law of $\Omega$, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}). A parallel field therefore satisfies $F_{T}(a\wedge b)\psi = 0$ at every point and for every plane, and a parallel adjoint tractor $X$ (a bivector field with $D^{T}_{a}X = a\cdot
abla X + \Omega_{T}(a)	imes X = 0$) satisfies $F_{T}(a\wedge b)	imes X = 0$. Conversely, where $F_{T} = 0$ on a simply connected region the connection is flat and the parallel sections of $\CS$ form a space of complex dimension $4$, on which the constant $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$ action, the form $h$ and $Z$ of the attachment are carried unchanged.

\emph{(i) Ricci blindness.} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.gtg-tractor-gauge-field-reproduces-tractor-connection}(iv), on a torsion-free field the part of $F_{T}$ with no derivative of the frame or of $\Sch$ is $-\mathcal{R}(A\wedge B) + \Theta(A)	imes\Theta(B)$, whose spacetime block is $-\mathcal{W}(A\wedge B)$ with no other block; the derivative part is the Cotton term in the $
O$ block. The check recomputes this with $\mathcal{R}(A\wedge B) = \mathcal{W}(A\wedge B) + \Sch(A)\wedge B + A\wedge\Sch(B)$ for six Weyl maps (one of each Petrov type) and two non-Einstein symmetric $\Sch$: the Schouten map cancels on all six coordinate planes. Each Weyl map is built as an $I_{4}$-linear map from a complex symmetric traceless $3	imes3$ matrix $M$ in the basis $\sigma_{k} = e_{k}e_{0}$; the check confirms pair symmetry, vanishing Ricci trace, the first Bianchi identity, and the type from the minimal polynomial of $M$ (O: $M = 0$; N: $M^{2} = 0$; III: $M^{3} = 0 
eq M^{2}$; otherwise a repeated eigenvalue exactly when $(\mathrm{tr}M^{2})^{3} = 6(\mathrm{tr}M^{3})^{2}$, D or II as $(M - \lambda)(M + 2\lambda)$ vanishes or not, I if no repeat).

\emph{(ii) The annihilated subspace.} (Two-spinor reading, labelled: on $L_{0} \oplus L_{\infty}$ a conformal spinor is a pair $(\omega^{A}, \pi_{A'})$, and the Weyl bivectors act on $\omega$ through the Weyl spinor $\Psi_{ABCD}$ and on $\pi$ through its conjugate.) The common annihilator of the Weyl bivectors in $\CS$ is therefore $\{\omega : \Psi_{ABCD}\omega^{D} = 0\} \oplus \{\pi :  ar\Psi_{A'B'C'D'}\pi^{D'} = 0\}$. If $\omega 
eq 0$ and $\Psi_{ABCD}\omega^{D} = 0$, complete $o = \omega$ to a spin frame $(o, \iota)$: every component of $\Psi$ with at least one contraction with $o$ vanishes, so $\Psi_{ABCD} = \Psi_{4}\,o_{A}o_{B}o_{C}o_{D}$, type N with principal spinor $o$ (or zero); conversely at a type N point $\Psi_{ABCD}\omega^{D} = 0$ exactly for $\omega$ proportional to $o$. This is the standard integrability condition of the twistor equation, which restricts the field to Petrov types N and O (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-twistor-equation-integrability-petrov-n-or-o}). So the complex dimension is $4$ at type O, $2$ at type N and $0$ at types I, II, D, III. The check computes the common left kernel of the six field strengths $F_{T}(e_{m}\wedge e_{n})$ for each Petrov sample: real dimension $32, 16, 0, 0, 0, 0$, that is complex dimension $4, 2, 0, 0, 0, 0$ on $\CS$; for type N it coincides with the left kernel of the repeated principal null vector $k = e_{0} + e_{3}$ (which every type N curvature bivector annihilates under the commutator product) and meets the left kernel of $m = e_{0} - e_{3}$ only in zero. The samples are general: type N and type III normal forms are unique up to a Lorentz rotor and a complex scale, neither of which changes the kernel dimension, and the spinor argument above covers types I, II and D for every value of their invariants. A Cotton block $
O\wedge c$ adds the condition of being annihilated by it, which can only cut the subspace; in the samples it keeps the type N subspace for $c$ along $k$ and cuts it to complex dimension $1$ for $c = e_{1}, e_{0}, m$. Where $\mathcal{W}$ vanishes on a region the Cotton term vanishes too and $F_{T} = 0$: this converse is proved on twistor-flat fields in \claimref{synthesis.twistor-flat-fields-give-nordstrom-not-einstein}, clause (i), from Weyl's theorem (stored as an imported Fact, correspondence.imported-weyls-theorem) and the conformal invariance of the tractor connection, and is not used in the checks. On every Einstein space ($\Sch = 	frac{\Lambda}{6}\id$, parallel) the Cotton term vanishes; under Einstein's equations with matter it is in general nonzero.

\emph{(iii) No conformal-energy generator.} At points of type II and D, and of type I with nonzero eigenvalues, the matrix $M$ is invertible, so the Weyl bivectors span all of $\so(1,3)$, and the bivectors of $\Cl(2,4)$ commuting with $\so(1,3)$ are the multiples of $E = e_{+}e_{-}$. Type III, and type I with a zero eigenvalue, have normal forms unique up to a Lorentz rotor and a complex scale; for both the check finds the same one-dimensional commutant, spanned by $E$. At type N the commutant is the five-dimensional span of $k\wedge e_{1}$, $k\wedge e_{2}$, $k\wedge e_{+}$, $k\wedge e_{-}$ and $E$; at type O it is all fifteen bivectors. In each case with $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$ every element of the commutant annihilates the null vector $k$ under the commutator product ($E$ annihilates every spacetime vector). The generator $Z = e_{0}e_{+}$ has $Z^{2} = -1$ and annihilates exactly the span of $e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{-}$, a negative-definite $4$-plane; a rotor $g$ is an isometry, so $\lambda\,gZ	ilde g$ ($\lambda 
eq 0$) annihilates exactly the negative-definite plane $g(\mathrm{span}\{e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{-}\})$, which contains no null vector. Hence no nonzero multiple of a conjugate of $Z$ lies in the commutant at a point with $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$, and no parallel adjoint tractor through such a point is a conformal-energy generator; at type O, $Z$ commutes with the curvature (computed).

\emph{Reading.} The attachment's one-particle structure is $\CS$ with its invariant form $h$, the $\mathfrak{u}(2,2)$ action, and the grading $Z$ that turns $h$ into the Hilbert form and generates the positive conformal energy of the massless, conformally invariant modules ($Z$ is not a symmetry of a massive field even on a flat region) (Propositions \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, \claimref{synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z}). By (ii) and (iii) the tractor transport carries it across a region only where $\mathcal{W} = 0$; where $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$ at most a two-dimensional subspace of $\CS$ is parallel, and no conformal-energy generator is. So on a general gravitational field the attachment's tractor transport does not construct the one-particle space and supplies no state: a choice of positive frequency has to come from another construction, which this result does not exclude. The companion result on the Hadamard class and null planes (\claimref{synthesis.bulk-hadamard-states-restrict-to-the-generator-condition-on-flat-null-planes}) is proved on the flat field only and says nothing about fields with $\mathcal{W} 
eq 0$. That the field algebra itself, the CAR algebra over the Dirac solution space, exists on every field with a Cauchy surface is standard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimock-dirac-car-algebra-on-a-gravitational-field}) and is not used here; what is missing off Weyl-flat regions is a state on that algebra, not the algebra. Transport-convenient: the result is the standard integrability condition of the twistor equation, reproduced in the series' tractor gauge field and read through the attachment's $Z$; the series' transport adds the reading, not the mathematics.

synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-.formal:
Work in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$, $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$, with $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ and $\sigma_{3} = \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}$. Let $k = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3}$ and $m = \gamma_{0} - \gamma_{3}$, so $Q(k) = Q(m) = 0$ and $\ip{k}{m} = 2$; let $N_{k} = \{x : \ip{x}{k} = 0\}$ be the null plane whose generators run along $k$ (any future null direction is carried to this one by a rotor, and $m$ is then the second null direction of the plane of $k$ and $\gamma_{0}$); let $B = \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}$ ($B^{2} = 1$) and $\Lambda(a) = a\gamma_{0}/(2a_{0})$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)). Spinors are even multivectors $\psi \in \Cl^{+}(1,3)$ (real dimension $8$), on which a rotor $R$ acts by $\psi \mapsto R\psi$; $L_{X}\psi = X\psi$, and $J_{\psi} = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}$ is the Dirac current. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The projectors.)} $\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12 k\gamma_{0} = \tfrac12(1 + B) = \tfrac14 km$ and $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12 m\gamma_{0} = \tfrac12(1 - B) = \tfrac14 mk$ are complementary idempotents, $\Lambda(k) + \Lambda(m) = 1$, $\Lambda(k)\Lambda(m) = \Lambda(m)\Lambda(k) = 0$, each self-adjoint for the Dirac adjoint ($\gamma_{0}\tilde{\Lambda}\gamma_{0} = \Lambda$). On $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$, $L_{\Lambda(m)}$ projects onto $\ker L_{m}$, the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $L_{B}$, and $L_{\Lambda(k)}$ onto $\ker L_{k}$, the $(+1)$-eigenspace; each has real dimension $4$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The flux.)} $J_{\psi}\cdot k = 2\,|\Lambda(m)\psi|^{2}$ and $J_{\psi}\cdot m = 2\,|\Lambda(k)\psi|^{2}$, the squared Euclidean norm in the blade basis $1$, $\gamma_{\mu}\gamma_{\nu}$ ($\mu < \nu$), $I_{4}$. So the flux of the current through $N_{k}$ vanishes identically on the image of $\Lambda(k)$ and is positive definite on the image of $\Lambda(m)$: the part of a spinor field that carries its current through $N_{k}$, its canonical part on $N_{k}$, is $\Lambda(m)\psi$. The image of $\Lambda(k)$ is the spinor of plane waves of momentum $k$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)); its canonical data live on $N_{m}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Two complex channels.)} $L_{I_{4}}$ and Hestenes' unit $R_{I_{4}\sigma_{3}}$, $\psi \mapsto \psi I_{4}\sigma_{3}$, each square to $-1$ and commute with $L_{B}$, so the image $V_{\Lambda}$ of $\Lambda(m)$ (and likewise that of $\Lambda(k)$) is invariant under both and is a complex vector space of dimension $2$ under either unit: the canonical part is two complex channels.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Mass terms reach only the constraint.)} Every vector splits as $a = \tfrac12 m\,\ip{k}{a} + \tfrac12 k\,\ip{m}{a} + a_{\perp}$ with $a_{\perp}$ orthogonal to $k$ and $m$, so $k\nabla = 2\Lambda(k)(k\cdot\nabla) + k\nabla_{\perp}$ contains no derivative off $N_{k}$; $k$ anticommutes with $\gamma_{1}$ and $\gamma_{2}$ and $k\Lambda(k) = 0$, so $k\psi X = k\Lambda(m)\psi X$ for every multivector $X$ acting from the right, and $L_{k}$ is injective on the image of $\Lambda(m)$. The linear maps $\Cl^{+}(1,3) \to \Cl(1,3)$ that commute with left multiplication by every even element are exactly the right multiplications, so every Lorentz-covariant mass term, of Dirac or of Majorana type, acts from the right (with an internal index, a matrix of right multiplications), and on $N_{k}$ it enters only the equation that fixes $\Lambda(k)\psi$ along each generator from $\Lambda(m)\psi$ (up to its value at one end of each generator): the free data on $N_{k}$ are $\Lambda(m)\psi$, together with that one boundary value of $\Lambda(k)\psi$ per generator, for every mass matrix.
\end{enumerate}
These are identities in $\Cl(1,3)$; they use no thermal, counting or matter premise.
synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-.technical: On a null plane, with generators along $k$ and second null direction $m$, the flux of a spinor's Dirac current through the plane is twice the squared norm of $\Lambda(m)\psi$, where $\Lambda(m) = m\gamma_{0}/2 = mk/4$ is one of the two complementary idempotents of the plane of $k$ and $m$. That half of the spinor, of real dimension four, is its canonical part on the plane; the other half, the spinor of plane waves moving along $k$, carries no flux through it. Both the field theory's unit $I_{4}$ and Hestenes' unit preserve the canonical part, which is therefore two complex channels under either. Multiplying a spinor field equation by $k$ on the left removes every derivative off the plane, and since Lorentz-covariant mass terms are right multiplications in the spacetime algebra, the mass enters only the equation that fixes the other half from the canonical part, up to one boundary value per generator: the free data on the plane are the canonical part, with that boundary value, whatever the masses. All of this is algebra; it is the common ground of the light-ray count of arrays, the slot module's Weyl-component count and the restriction of Hadamard states to null planes, none of whose further premises it needs.
synthesis.canonical-part-of-a-spinor-on-.lay: A spin-one-half field, such as the electron's, has eight real components at each point. On a surface swept out by light rays, only four of them carry the field across the surface; the other four describe waves running along the light rays themselves and carry nothing through it. The four that count form two complex channels, and the particle's mass does not change which four they are: the mass only ties the other four to them. This result proves these facts by direct algebra, so that later results can use them without taking on any further assumptions.

proofs.main:
\emph{Origin and numbering.} Clauses (i) to (iii) are clause (i) of Theorem synthesis.light-ray-good-part-of-a-spinor-is-two-chirality-arrays, split in three (its projectors, its flux identity, and the two complex channels, whose count it gave in its clause (iii)); clause (iv) is clause (i) of Theorem synthesis.slot-module-light-ray-arrays-are-weyl-components. The arguments below are moved from those proofs; the step that Lorentz-covariant mass terms act from the right, argued there, is proved here.

\emph{Setting.} Every statement is about linear maps and quadratic forms on the real vector space $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ with basis $1$, $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{i}$, $\gamma_{i}\gamma_{j}$ ($i < j$), $I_{4}$, or on $\Cl(1,3)$ with its sixteen blades. The script builds the rational matrices of the maps below and decides each identity and each dimension by exact rank computation. A rotor carrying $\gamma_{0} \pm \gamma_{3}$ to another pair of null directions conjugates every map below to the corresponding map and preserves ranks, so the choice of $k$ and $m$ is no loss.

\emph{(i).} $B^{2} = \gamma_{3}\gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}\gamma_{0} = -\gamma_{3}^{2}\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, so $L_{B}^{2} = 1$ and $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ is the direct sum of the $\pm1$ eigenspaces of $L_{B}$. Directly, $k\gamma_{0} = 1 + B$, $m\gamma_{0} = 1 - B$, $km = 2 + 2B$ and $mk = 2 - 2B$, so $\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12 k\gamma_{0} = \tfrac12(1 + B) = \tfrac14 km$ and $\Lambda(m) = \tfrac12 m\gamma_{0} = \tfrac12(1 - B) = \tfrac14 mk$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1) at $a_{0} = 1$). From $B^{2} = 1$ they are idempotents with sum $1$ and product $\tfrac14(1 - B^{2}) = 0$ in either order. $\tilde{B} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3} = -B$, so the reverse of $\Lambda(m)$ is $\tfrac12(1 + B)$, and $\gamma_{0}B\gamma_{0} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{3} = -B$, so $\gamma_{0}\tfrac12(1 + B)\gamma_{0} = \tfrac12(1 - B) = \Lambda(m)$; likewise for $\Lambda(k)$. If $B\psi = -\psi$ then $\psi = \tfrac12 m\gamma_{0}\psi$ and $m\psi = \tfrac12 m^{2}\gamma_{0}\psi = 0$; conversely $m\psi = 0$ gives $\Lambda(k)\psi = \tfrac14 km\psi = 0$. The script finds $\ker L_{m}$ and the $(-1)$-eigenspace of $L_{B}$ both of dimension $4$ with intersection of dimension $4$, and $L_{m}L_{\Lambda(m)} = 0$, $(L_{B} + 1)L_{\Lambda(m)} = 0$, $\mathrm{rank}\,L_{\Lambda(m)} = 4$; the same with $k$ and the $(+1)$-eigenspace.

\emph{(ii).} If $\psi = \Lambda(k)\chi = \tfrac12 k\gamma_{0}\chi$, then $J_{\psi} = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi} = \tfrac14 k(\gamma_{0}\chi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\chi}\gamma_{0})k$, and for any vector $v$, $kvk = 2\ip{k}{v}k - vk^{2} = 2\ip{k}{v}k$, so $J_{\psi}$ is a multiple of $k$ and $J_{\psi}\cdot k = 0$: the image of $\Lambda(k)$ carries no flux through $N_{k}$. The script computes the full Gram matrix of $\psi \mapsto J_{\psi}\cdot k = \langle\psi\gamma_{0}\tilde{\psi}k\rangle_{0}$ and finds it equal to $2\Lambda(m)^{T}\Lambda(m)$ exactly, so $J_{\psi}\cdot k = 2|\Lambda(m)\psi|^{2}$, positive definite on the image of $\Lambda(m)$ (rank $4$) and zero on that of $\Lambda(k)$; the flux through $N_{m}$ is $2|\Lambda(k)\psi|^{2}$, likewise, and as a contrast the flux through a hyperplane with normal $\gamma_{0}$ is not carried by either half alone. On the spinor $\psi = 1 + 2\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2} + 3\gamma_{0}\gamma_{3}$ it finds $J_{\psi}\cdot k = 20 = 2|\Lambda(m)\psi|^{2}$. The canonical part of a spinor field on $N_{k}$ is therefore the part that carries its current through $N_{k}$, $\Lambda(m)\psi$. The spinor $\Lambda(k)$ of a plane wave of momentum $k$ (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1)) is constant along the generators of $N_{k}$, and its canonical data live on $N_{m}$. (This is the good component of light-front quantisation, Kogut and Soper, cited from memory as orientation.)

\emph{(iii).} $I_{4}^{2} = -1$ and $(I_{4}\sigma_{3})^{2} = -1$. $I_{4}$ commutes with every bivector, so $L_{I_{4}}$ commutes with $L_{B}$; right and left multiplications commute, so $R_{I_{4}\sigma_{3}}$ commutes with $L_{B}$. Each therefore commutes with $L_{\Lambda(m)} = \tfrac12(1 - L_{B})$ and preserves its image $V_{\Lambda}$, which, of real dimension $4$, is a complex vector space of dimension $2$ for the complex structure given by either unit (the script checks both squares, both commutations and $U L_{\Lambda(m)} = L_{\Lambda(m)} U L_{\Lambda(m)}$ for both units $U$, and, as a contrast, that left multiplication by $\gamma_{1}\gamma_{3}$ does not commute with $L_{\Lambda(m)}$). The same holds for the image of $\Lambda(k)$.

\emph{(iv).} With $\ip{k}{m} = 2$ and $Q(k) = Q(m) = 0$ the reciprocal vectors of $k$ and $m$ in the plane of $k$ and $m$ are $\tfrac12 m$ and $\tfrac12 k$, so every vector is $a = \tfrac12 m\,\ip{k}{a} + \tfrac12 k\,\ip{m}{a} + a_{\perp}$ with $a_{\perp}$ orthogonal to both, and correspondingly $\nabla = \tfrac12 m\,(k\cdot\nabla) + \tfrac12 k\,(m\cdot\nabla) + \nabla_{\perp}$. The derivative $k\cdot\nabla$ is along the generators, inside $N_{k}$, and $\nabla_{\perp}$ is along $N_{k}$ as well; only $m\cdot\nabla$ leaves the plane. Since $k^{2} = Q(k) = 0$, $k\nabla = \tfrac12 km\,(k\cdot\nabla) + k\nabla_{\perp} = 2\Lambda(k)(k\cdot\nabla) + k\nabla_{\perp}$ has no derivative off $N_{k}$. By (i) $k\Lambda(k) = \tfrac12 k^{2}\gamma_{0} = 0$, and $k$ anticommutes with $\gamma_{1}$ and $\gamma_{2}$ because $\ip{k}{\gamma_{j}} = 0$; so for every multivector $X$, $k\psi X = k(\Lambda(k) + \Lambda(m))\psi X = k\Lambda(m)\psi X$.

\emph{Covariant maps are right multiplications.} Let $f : \Cl^{+}(1,3) \to \Cl(1,3)$ be linear and commute with left multiplication by every even element, $f(Y\psi) = Yf(\psi)$. Then $f(\psi) = f(\psi\cdot 1) = \psi f(1)$, so $f$ is right multiplication by $f(1)$, and conversely every right multiplication commutes with every left one. Lorentz covariance of a mass term is commutation with $\psi \mapsto R\psi$ for every rotor $R$, and the rotors span $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ ($e^{\theta X}$ for the basis bivectors $X$ give $1$ and the six bivectors, and products of two commuting ones give $I_{4}$), so a Lorentz-covariant mass term is a right multiplication on the spinor index, and with an internal index a matrix of right multiplications, $\psi_{a} \mapsto \sum_{b}\psi_{b}X_{ba}$ (the same argument applied entrywise): $\psi \mapsto \psi\gamma_{0}$ for a Dirac mass (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}), and $\psi \mapsto \psi\sigma_{1}$, the charge conjugate, composed with a symmetric matrix on the internal index, for a Majorana mass. The script confirms this by solving the linear equations $FL_{X} = L_{X}F$ for an unknown $16 \times 8$ matrix $F$, $X$ the six basis bivectors (which generate $\Cl^{+}(1,3)$ as an algebra): the solution space has dimension $16$ and is spanned by the sixteen right multiplications by blades.

\emph{The constraint.} Write a massive spinor equation as $\nabla\psi I_{4}\sigma_{3} = \mathcal{M}(\psi)$ with $\mathcal{M}$ such a right multiplier. Multiplying on the left by $k$ gives
\[
2\Lambda(k)\,(k\cdot\nabla)\psi\,I_{4}\sigma_{3} + k\nabla_{\perp}\psi\,I_{4}\sigma_{3} = k\,\mathcal{M}(\psi).
\]
Here $\Lambda(k)$ commutes with $k\cdot\nabla$ and with right multiplication, $k\nabla_{\perp}\Lambda(k)\psi = -\nabla_{\perp}k\Lambda(k)\psi = 0$, and $k\,\mathcal{M}(\Lambda(k)\psi) = 0$ for every right multiplier. So the equation reads $2(k\cdot\nabla)(\Lambda(k)\psi)I_{4}\sigma_{3} = -k\nabla_{\perp}\Lambda(m)\psi\,I_{4}\sigma_{3} + k\,\mathcal{M}(\Lambda(m)\psi)$: along each generator it fixes $\Lambda(k)\psi$ from $\Lambda(m)\psi$ (up to its value at one end of the generator), and the mass enters only here. The flux identity (ii), which defines the canonical part, involves no field equation. So the free data on $N_{k}$ are $\Lambda(m)\psi$, together with the one boundary value of $\Lambda(k)\psi$ per generator that the integration along it leaves free (the light-front zero mode), for every mass matrix. (The mass independence of the null-plane data is the familiar property of light-front quantisation, cited from memory as orientation; the argument above does not use it.) The script checks $k^{2} = 0$, $km = 2 + 2B$, the splitting of each $\gamma_{\mu}$, the anticommutation of $k$ with $\gamma_{1}, \gamma_{2}$, $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}L_{\Lambda(k)}) = 0$, $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}L_{\Lambda(m)}) = 4$, and $\mathrm{rank}(L_{k}R_{X}L_{\Lambda(k)}) = 0$ for each of the sixteen basis blades $X$, and, as a contrast, that the left multiplier $\gamma_{3}$ does not pass: $k\gamma_{3}\Lambda(k) = -2\Lambda(k)$.

\emph{What is and is not derived.} All four clauses are exact identities in $\Cl(1,3)$ resting only on the field theory's projector $\Lambda(a)$ and Dirac mass term. They do not compute the anticommutator of the restricted field, which the results that use them compute in their own settings.

synthesis.chiral-abelian-loops-with-i4-a.formal:
In $\Cl(1, D-1)$ (integer $D \geq 4$, signature $(1, D-1)$) call components along $\gamma_{0}, \ldots, \gamma_{3}$ barred and the rest (evanescent) hatted, $k = \bar k + \hat k$. Take the unit of the Feynman rules as the right unit $x \mapsto xI_{4}$, a coefficient outside the product (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), and the chirality $\gamma_{5}$ as $x \mapsto I_{4}xI_{4}$: on the left $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ inside the product, the Breitenlohner-Maison-'t Hooft-Veltman element (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.unit-i4-keeps-its-three-properties-only-in-dimension-zero-mod-four}(iv); Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}), and on the right the unit; $P_{R,L} = \tfrac12(1 \pm \gamma_{5})$, and the trace $4\langle X\rangle_{0}$. A massless fermion of charge $Y$ couples to an abelian gauge field through the vertex $\bar\gamma^{\mu}P_{R}$ (or $\bar\gamma^{\mu}P_{L}$) with the full propagator numerator $k$; external momenta are four-dimensional. In the purely chiral formulation every field of the content couples this way.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (The projectors delete the evanescent momentum.) $\bar\gamma^{\mu}P_{R}k\bar\gamma^{\nu}P_{R} = \bar\gamma^{\mu}\bar k\bar\gamma^{\nu}P_{R}$, the same with $P_{L}$, so around a closed loop of chiral vertices every propagator numerator is replaced by its barred part; $\hat k$ enters only through traces with zero scalar part.
\item[(ii)] (Two-point contraction.) After $\ell^{a}\ell^{b} \to g^{ab}Q(\ell)/D$, the $\ell\ell$ part of the normalised numerator is $-\bar g^{\mu\nu}$ for the chiral loop and $\tfrac{2 - D}{2}\bar g^{\mu\nu}$ for half the vector-like Dirac loop, for $D = 4, \ldots, 8$; the difference is $\tfrac{D-4}{2}\bar g^{\mu\nu}$.
\item[(iii)] (Four-point contraction.) After $\ell^{a}\ell^{b}\ell^{c}\ell^{d} \to S^{abcd}Q(\ell)^{2}/(D(D+2))$, $S^{abcd} = g^{ab}g^{cd} + g^{ac}g^{bd} + g^{ad}g^{bc}$, the $\ell^{4}$ part summed over the six orderings of the photons is $0$ for the chiral loop (its $\gamma_{5}$ part included) and $(D-4)(D-2)S^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma}$ for half the vector-like loop, for $D = 4, \ldots, 7$.
\item[(iv)] (Breaking and counterterms.) Under dimensional regularisation (imported), the chiral loops equal the gauge-invariant half Dirac loops plus the local finite terms
\[
\Pi_{\mathrm{break}}^{\mu\nu} = -\frac{e^{2}Y^{2}}{48\pi^{2}}\,Q(\bar q)\,\bar g^{\mu\nu}, \qquad \Gamma_{\mathrm{break}}^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma} = -\frac{e^{4}Y^{4}}{24\pi^{2}}\,S^{\mu\nu\rho\sigma},
\]
the first not transverse. They are cancelled by the finite counterterms
\[
S_{\mathrm{fct}} = \frac{1}{16\pi^{2}}\int\Bigl[-\frac{e^{2}}{6}\sum Y^{2}\,\bar A_{\mu}\bar\partial^{2}\bar A^{\mu} + \frac{e^{4}}{12}\sum Y^{4}\,(\bar A^{2})^{2}\Bigr],
\]
the sums over the chiral fields, the published values \cite{BeluscaMaito2020, BeluscaMaito2021} recomputed (standard). In the purely chiral formulation both sums are positive, so these counterterms never cancel between fields (a vector-like pair given a $D$-dimensional vector vertex has no such breaking); for the left-handed content of one generation of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content} ($m = 1$), $\sum Y^{2} = \tfrac{10}{3}$ and $\sum Y^{4} = \tfrac{95}{54}$, while $\sum Y^{3} = 0$.
\end{enumerate}
Clauses (i) to (iii) are exact algebra in the integer-dimensional algebras; (iv) is computed given the scheme and its master integrals (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimensional-regularisation-and-the-bmhv-gamma5}(iv)).
synthesis.chiral-abelian-loops-with-i4-a.technical: Dimensional regularisation continues the Clifford algebra to $D$ dimensions; the stored unit result identifies the four-dimensional $I_{4}$ inside $\Cl(1, D-1)$ with the chirality element of the standard consistent scheme, which anticommutes with the four original directions and commutes with the extra ones. With the unit kept outside the product, the chiral projectors at the vertices of a loop delete the evanescent part of every internal momentum. The loop of a chiral abelian field is then the gauge-invariant half of a Dirac loop minus the evanescent remainder of the vector-like contraction, which this result computes exactly as a polynomial in the integer dimension: $(D-4)/2$ for the photon two-point function and $(D-4)(D-2)$ for the four-point function. Multiplied by the poles of the dimensionally continued integrals these give finite local terms that break the Ward identity: a non-transverse photon term $-(e^{2}Y^{2}/(48\pi^{2}))Q(\bar q)\bar g^{\mu\nu}$ and a four-photon contact term. The finite counterterms that restore the symmetry are $\frac{1}{16\pi^{2}}[-\frac{e^{2}}{6}\sum Y^{2}\bar A\cdot\bar\partial^{2}\bar A + \frac{e^{4}}{12}\sum Y^{4}(\bar A^{2})^{2}]$, the published values. These are the standard values. Unlike the anomaly, when every field carries a chiral vertex they never cancel between fields; for one generation of the series' content the sums are $10/3$ and $95/54$.
synthesis.chiral-abelian-loops-with-i4-a.lay: Calculations of quantum corrections often pretend that spacetime has a slightly different number of dimensions. In that method the four-dimensional volume element, which elsewhere in the series supplies the imaginary number of quantum theory, plays the role of the standard chirality element, which is not defined beyond four dimensions; the imaginary number itself stays outside the products. This result works out what that costs for particles that feel a force only in one handedness: the calculation breaks the force's symmetry by small, definite amounts, which have to be removed by hand with two correction terms. Their sizes come out equal to the published ones, and when every particle is treated as one-handed they add up rather than cancel over the particles of a generation, unlike the anomaly.
