synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-tw.formal:
Units and signature of the store. Let $\CS$ be the eight-dimensional conformal spinor module of $\Cl(2,4)$ with the generators $e_{1}$ ($e_{1}^{2} = 1$, the time), $e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}$ (squares $-1$) and the ascent plane $e_{\pm}$ ($e_{\pm}^{2} = \pm 1$), the positive Hermitian structure $h$ for which every generator is unitary, $J = ie_{1}e_{+}$ and the twistor form $\Sigma(\psi, \varphi) = h(\psi, J\varphi)$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}. Write $A^{\dagger}$ and $A^{\sharp}$ for the adjoints of an operator $A$ on $\CS$ for $h$ and for $\Sigma$, $\bar A$ for Clifford conjugation (the anti-automorphism with $\bar a = -a$ on vectors, extended antilinearly to complex combinations), and $\tau(A) = \tfrac18\operatorname{tr}A$. Polarisation vectors $u, w$ are vectors of the span of $e_{1}, \dots, e_{4}$, with $u\cdot w$ the store's metric, $Q(e_{1}) = 1$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The twistor adjoint is Clifford conjugation; proved.)} $A^{\sharp} = JA^{\dagger}J$; for every $A$ in $\Cl(2,4)$ acting on $\CS$, $A^{\sharp} = \bar A$, so $B^{\sharp} = (-1)^{k(k+1)/2}B$ for a blade $B$ of grade $k$; and $A^{\sharp}$ is unchanged when $\Sigma$ is replaced by $\lambda\Sigma$, $\lambda$ real and nonzero.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Its trace form on vectors is minus the metric; proved.)} For real vectors $a, b$ of $\Cl(2,4)$, $\tau(a^{\sharp}b) = \langle\bar ab\rangle_{0} = -a\cdot b$, of signature $(4, 2)$; the identity $\langle\bar ab\rangle_{0} = -a\cdot b$ holds in every Clifford algebra, with no module and no twistor form. $\tau(a^{\dagger}b)$ is the Euclidean form in which the six generators are orthonormal. The two are related by $J$: $\tau(a^{\sharp}b) = \tau(a^{\dagger}JbJ)$, where $b \mapsto JbJ$ reverses $e_{1}$ and $e_{+}$ and fixes $e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}, e_{-}$. On polarisation vectors the first is the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form $-u\cdot w$, negative on $e_{1}$ and positive on $e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}$ (the sign from the store's signature, the normalisation by the choice of $\tau$); the second is the Euclidean form of the time $e_{1}$; and $J$ acts as $u \mapsto -e_{1}ue_{1}$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Invariance; proved.)} $\tau(a^{\sharp}b)$ is invariant under every rotor of $\Cl(2,4)$; the positive form $\tau(a^{\dagger}b)$ is not invariant under the boost $\tfrac54 + \tfrac34e_{1}e_{2}$, which takes $e_{1}$ to a vector of positive norm $\tfrac{257}{32}$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Uniqueness; proved.)} The real bilinear forms on the polarisation space invariant under the six Lorentz bivectors form a one-dimensional space spanned by the metric. Hence every Lorentz-invariant Hermitian form on the complex polarisations is a real multiple of $-u\cdot w$, and none is definite.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Second quantisation; proved.)} On the polynomials in $z_{0}, \dots, z_{3}$ with the form $\langle z^{\alpha}, z^{\beta}\rangle = \alpha!\,\delta_{\alpha\beta}$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}), the bosonic Fock form over the one-particle form $\tau(u^{\sharp}w)$ is $\langle z^{\alpha}, (-1)^{n_{0}}z^{\beta}\rangle$, and for it the adjoint of $a_{\mu} = \partial/\partial z_{\mu}$ is $-g_{\mu\mu}z_{\mu}$, so $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$ on all four polarisations: the Feynman-gauge ($\alpha = 1$) realisation of the form in clause (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, with fundamental symmetry the second quantisation of $b \mapsto JbJ$. Covariant gauges with $\alpha \neq 1$ use the dipole state space with an auxiliary field, not a Fock space over a one-particle form, and are not described here.
\item[(vi)] \emph{(The ghost twist; computed.)} $J = 2n_{c} - 1$, with $n_{c}$ the number operator of the mode $c = \tfrac12(e_{1} + ie_{+})$; on a floor of two tower modes $b, d$ (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) the ghost twist $S = 1 - (b^{*} - d^{*})(b - d)$ of (K2) is $1 - 2n_{-}$, the parity of the mode $(b - d)/\sqrt2$. Both twists are parities of one mode; every fundamental symmetry of this kind on a fermion floor has that form, so this does not single out (K2).
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading (argued).} The one-particle form of (K1) is minus the store's metric, the trace form of Clifford conjugation in any Clifford algebra; the twistor form supplies the involution $J$ that relates it to the positive polarisation form, so the frame that the positive form singles out is the attachment's imaginary time point. Clause (K1) as a premise, that the polarisation and ghost state spaces carry the indefinite form, is not derived, and neither are (K2) to (K4). The covariant and the positive forms are both present in the attachment, as in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}(iv), where the covariant form is the one on the whole space and states exist only for positive structures. Standard; transport-absent.
synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-tw.technical: The Krein premise of the series' gauge-field theory gives the polarisations of a gauge field the indefinite Gupta-Bleuler form, minus the Minkowski metric. This result places that form among the series' structures. The adjoint of the twistor form on the conformal spinor module of Cl(2,4) is Clifford conjugation, the anti-automorphism that negates every vector, whatever the real factor of the twistor form; its normalised trace form on vectors is minus the metric. That last identity holds in every Clifford algebra, so the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form is simply the series' metric with its sign reversed, and the twistor form adds the involution J, which relates it to the positive structure's trace form, the Euclidean form of the time used for the stored photon, and whose second quantisation is the stored fundamental symmetry (-1)^{n_0}. Every Lorentz-invariant Hermitian form on the polarisations is a multiple of this one (computed). The Fock space over it is the Feynman-gauge realisation; other covariant gauges need a dipole state space and are not covered. The ghost twist is, like J, the parity of one fermion mode, which every such twist is. Nothing here derives that the unphysical modes must carry the indefinite form, the regulator fields, or positivity of the physical space. Standard; transport-absent.
synthesis.clifford-conjugation-is-the-tw.lay: The indefinite "length" used to quantise force fields covariantly gives the time direction negative length and the space directions positive length. This is the series' own spacetime metric with its sign reversed. The result shows that the conformal spinors of the series carry the same rule, and that the ordinary positive length used for light corresponds to choosing a time direction. It does not show that the series must use the indefinite length for its unphysical states; that remains an assumption.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} $\CS$, $h$, $J = ie_{1}e_{+}$ and $\Sigma = h(\cdot, J\cdot)$ are those of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}; in its model the generators are realised on three fermion modes in the Jordan-Wigner basis and $h$ is the identity Gram matrix. The check uses that model in exact Gaussian rationals. Adjoints are antilinear in complex scalars.

\emph{Step 1 (the $\Sigma$-adjoint; proved).} By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}(i), $J^{2} = 1$ and $J^{\dagger} = J$. For operators $A$, $\Sigma(\psi, A\varphi) = h(\psi, JAJ\,J\varphi) = h((JAJ)^{\dagger}\psi, J\varphi) = \Sigma(JA^{\dagger}J\psi, \varphi)$, so $A^{\sharp} = JA^{\dagger}J$. Replacing $\Sigma$ by $\lambda\Sigma$ with $\lambda$ real and nonzero multiplies both sides of the defining identity $\Sigma(A^{\sharp}\psi, \varphi) = \Sigma(\psi, A\varphi)$ by $\lambda$, so $A^{\sharp}$ is unchanged (the check also computes $(\lambda\Sigma)^{-1}A^{\dagger}(\lambda\Sigma)$ for $\lambda = -3, \tfrac27$). The map $A \mapsto A^{\sharp}$ is an antilinear anti-automorphism of $\operatorname{End}\CS$. By Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}(iii) the $\Sigma$-adjoint of every real vector is minus itself (directly: $e_{k}^{\dagger} = e_{k}^{-1} = e_{k}/Q(e_{k})$, and $J$ anticommutes with $e_{1}, e_{+}$, the generators of square $+1$, and commutes with the others, so $e_{k}^{\sharp} = -e_{k}$ for all six). Clifford conjugation is the unique anti-automorphism of $\Cl(2,4)$ that negates vectors, since the vectors generate the algebra; hence $A^{\sharp} = \bar A$ on $\Cl(2,4)$, and on a blade of grade $k$, $\bar B = (-1)^{k}\widetilde B = (-1)^{k}(-1)^{k(k-1)/2}B = (-1)^{k(k+1)/2}B$. The check compares $JB^{\dagger}J$ with $(-1)^{k(k+1)/2}B$ on all $64$ blades. This is (i).

\emph{Step 2 (trace forms on vectors; proved).} The complexified $\Cl(2,4)$ acts irreducibly on the eight-dimensional $\CS$, and $\tau(B) = 0$ for every blade $B \neq 1$: if $B$ has even grade below six it contains a generator $e$ with $eBe^{-1} = -B$; if $B$ has odd grade some generator $f$ is missing from $B$ and $fBf^{-1} = -B$; the pseudoscalar anticommutes with every generator. So $\tau(A) = \langle A\rangle_{0}$ for $A$ in the algebra. Then $\tau(a^{\sharp}b) = \langle\bar ab\rangle_{0} = -\langle ab\rangle_{0} = -a\cdot b$ for real vectors, a form of signature $(4,2)$ because $a\cdot b$ has signature $(2,4)$; and $\tau(e_{j}^{\dagger}e_{k}) = \langle e_{j}^{-1}e_{k}\rangle_{0} = \delta_{jk}$, the Euclidean form of the frame. By Step 1, $\tau(a^{\sharp}b) = \tau(Ja^{\dagger}Jb) = \tau(a^{\dagger}JbJ)$ by cyclicity, and $JbJ = (e_{1}e_{+})b(e_{1}e_{+})^{-1}$ ($i^{2} = -1$ and $(e_{1}e_{+})^{2} = -1$), which reverses $e_{1}$ and $e_{+}$ and fixes the other four generators. Restricted to $u, w$ in the span of $e_{1}, \dots, e_{4}$: $\tau(u^{\sharp}w) = -u\cdot w$, negative on $e_{1}$ and positive on $e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}$ (Gram matrix $\operatorname{diag}(-1, 1, 1, 1)$, checked), $\tau(u^{\dagger}w)$ is the Euclidean form with $e_{1}$ as time, and $JuJ = -e_{1}ue_{1}$ there. The check computes all $36$ Gram entries of both forms, the identity on three sample vectors with all six components, and the action of $J$. The identity $\langle\bar ab\rangle_{0} = -\langle ab\rangle_{0} = -a\cdot b$ uses only $\bar a = -a$, so it holds in every Clifford algebra; the check also computes it directly in $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(2,4)$ with no module and no twistor form. The sign that makes $e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}$ positive is the store's signature, $Q(e_{1}) = 1$; the normalisation is the choice of $\tau$ and of the sign in front of it. What the twistor form contributes is the identification of $\sharp$ with Clifford conjugation and the involution $J$ between the two forms. This is (ii).

\emph{Step 3 (invariance; proved).} For a rotor $R$ (even, $R\widetilde R = 1$), Clifford conjugation equals reversion on even elements, so $\overline{RaR^{-1}} = \overline{R^{-1}}\,\bar a\,\bar R = R\bar a\widetilde R$, and $\tau(\overline{RaR^{-1}}\,RbR^{-1}) = \langle R\bar ab\widetilde R\rangle_{0} = \langle\bar ab\rangle_{0}$. The check computes the invariance for the boost $\tfrac54 + \tfrac34e_{1}e_{2}$, the rotation $\tfrac35 + \tfrac45e_{2}e_{3}$, the translation $1 + \tfrac12e_{3}n_{\infty}$ ($n_{\infty} = e_{+} - e_{-}$) and the dilation $\tfrac54 + \tfrac34e_{+}e_{-}$, on sample vectors, by conjugating the $8 \times 8$ matrices. The boost takes $e_{1}$ to $\tfrac{17}{8}e_{1} \pm \tfrac{15}{8}e_{2}$, whose positive norm is $\tfrac{289 + 225}{64} = \tfrac{257}{32} \neq 1$ while its $\Sigma$-norm stays $-1$. That no positive structure is boost invariant is Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}(iv). This is (iii).

\emph{Step 4 (uniqueness; proved).} Let $X_{ij}$ be the matrices of $u \mapsto e_{i}e_{j}u - ue_{i}e_{j}$ on the span of $e_{1}, \dots, e_{4}$, computed in $\Cl(1,3)$. A real bilinear form with matrix $M$ is invariant under the Lorentz algebra if and only if $X_{ij}^{T}M + MX_{ij} = 0$ for the six pairs. These are $96$ linear equations in the $16$ entries of $M$; their solution space, computed exactly, is one-dimensional and spanned by $\operatorname{diag}(1, -1, -1, -1)$. A Hermitian form $H = S + iA$ ($S$ real symmetric, $A$ real antisymmetric) on $\mathbb{C}^{4}$ is invariant under the real matrices $X_{ij}$ exactly when $S$ and $A$ are (the equations are real-linear and the $X_{ij}$ are real); $A$ lies in the solution space and is antisymmetric, so $A = 0$ and $H$ is a real multiple of the metric, hence of $-u\cdot w$, and not definite. This is the computed form of Schur's lemma for the real irreducible vector representation. This is (iv).

\emph{Step 5 (second quantisation; proved).} For a one-particle space with an orthogonal basis $z_{\mu}$ of norms $\kappa_{\mu} = \pm1$, the bosonic Fock form on monomials is $\langle z^{\alpha}, z^{\beta}\rangle_{K} = \delta_{\alpha\beta}\,\alpha!\prod_{\mu}\kappa_{\mu}^{\alpha_{\mu}}$. By Step 2, $\kappa = (-1, 1, 1, 1)$ for $\tau(u^{\sharp}w)$, so $\langle z^{\alpha}, z^{\beta}\rangle_{K} = (-1)^{\alpha_{0}}\alpha!\,\delta_{\alpha\beta} = \langle z^{\alpha}, (-1)^{n_{0}}z^{\beta}\rangle$ with the form $\langle z^{n}, z^{n'}\rangle = n!\,\delta$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}. For $a_{\mu} = \partial/\partial z_{\mu}$: $\langle z^{\alpha}, a_{\mu}z^{\beta}\rangle_{K} = \beta_{\mu}\langle z^{\alpha}, z^{\beta - e_{\mu}}\rangle_{K}$, nonzero only for $\alpha = \beta - e_{\mu}$, where it is $\beta!\,\kappa^{\beta}/\kappa_{\mu} = \kappa_{\mu}\langle z_{\mu}z^{\alpha}, z^{\beta}\rangle_{K}$. So the $K$-adjoint of $a_{\mu}$ is $\kappa_{\mu}z_{\mu} = -g_{\mu\mu}z_{\mu}$ and $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$ for real polarisations, the form (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}; its fundamental symmetry $(-1)^{n_{0}}$ is the second quantisation of $u \mapsto JuJ$, which reverses $e_{1}$ only. The check verifies both identities on all monomials of degree at most three. The commutator $-u\cdot w$ on all four polarisations of each mode, with propagator $-g_{\mu\nu}/k^{2}$, is the Feynman-gauge ($\alpha = 1$) realisation. A covariant gauge with $\alpha \neq 1$ adds to the propagator a term $(1 - \alpha)k_{\mu}k_{\nu}/k^{4}$, whose two-point function has dipole support ($\delta'(k^{2})$); its state space needs the auxiliary (Nakanishi-Lautrup) field and is not a Fock space over a one-particle form at fixed momentum, so it is neither obtained nor excluded here (standard, cited from memory). This is (v).

\emph{Step 6 (the ghost twist; computed).} With $c = \tfrac12(e_{1} + ie_{+})$: $c^{2} = \tfrac14(e_{1}^{2} - e_{+}^{2}) = 0$ and $c^{\dagger}c = \tfrac14(e_{1} - ie_{+})(e_{1} + ie_{+}) = \tfrac12(1 + ie_{1}e_{+}) = \tfrac12(1 + J)$, so $n_{c} = c^{\dagger}c$ is a projection and $J = 2n_{c} - 1$: up to sign, $J$ is the parity of the mode $c$. On a floor of two tower modes $b, d$ with the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}, $n_{-} = \tfrac12(b^{*} - d^{*})(b - d)$ is the number operator of $(b - d)/\sqrt2$, $n_{-}^{2} = n_{-}$, and $S = 1 - 2n_{-}$, with $S^{2} = 1$, $S^{*} = S$ and $SbS = d$. Every fundamental symmetry that is the parity of one mode has this form, so the computation records the shape of (K2) and does not select it; the operative content of (K2) is the pairing of ghost and antighost in the indefinite form. This is (vi).

\emph{Step 7 (what does not follow; argued).} (a) The forms above are the covariant ones; the positive ones $\tau(a^{\dagger}b)$ and $h$ are equally present in the attachment. That a field theory's polarisation and ghost state spaces carry the covariant form rather than a frame's positive form is the content of (K1) and (K2) as a premise, and it is not derived here; Step 4 shows only that a Lorentz-invariant polarisation form is $-u\cdot w$ up to a real factor, which is standard. (b) Clause (K3) concerns additional massive fields entering loops with negative weights; nothing here says which fields exist. (c) Clause (K4) needs a BRST charge, that is, dynamics; positivity of its cohomology is computed in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts} only for the free charge at a null momentum up to three quanta. (d) The Fock form over an indefinite one-particle form is the standard construction; Clifford conjugation and its trace form, the Gupta-Bleuler form and the twistor form are standard. What is recorded is that, inside the store, the one-particle form of the premise is the trace form of the twistor adjoint (as of Clifford conjugation in any Clifford algebra), and that the fundamental symmetry and the frame of the positive form are supplied by the same $J$.

\emph{Status.} (i) to (v) proved, with exact checks; (vi) computed; the reading argued. A restatement of the one-particle content of (K1), not a derivation of the premise. Transport-absent.

synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vac.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$. \emph{Hypothesis:} the descended field near the descent is the Weyl-flat gravitational field on flat spacetime $\hb(b) = b/a(t)$, $t = x\cdot e_{0}$ the conformal time, $a$ smooth and positive on the collar where the deposit is set (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}; derived metric $a(t)^{2}$ times the flat one, a Robertson-Walker field, read through Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}), as for a descent of radiation type. Let $\psi$ be the massless Dirac field of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation} on it, $\chi = a^{3/2}\psi$ the conformally rescaled field, which solves the flat massless Dirac equation, and $\omega_{c}$ the conformal vacuum, the flat massless vacuum of $\chi$. A \emph{diagonal homogeneous deposit} is a gauge-invariant quasi-free state $\omega$ diagonal in the plane-wave quasi-particle modes of $\omega_{c}$ (no particle-antiparticle pair coherence, no coherence between momenta or helicities), with particle and antiparticle occupations $n_{+}(p), n_{-}(p) \in [0, 1]$ per comoving momentum $\vec p$ and helicity, $p = |\vec p|$; write $M_{k} = 2\int d^{3}p\,p^{k}\,(n_{+} + n_{-})$ and $R^{(\pm)} = \mathcal{G}_{\omega}^{(\pm)} - \mathcal{G}_{\omega_{c}}^{(\pm)}$ for the remainders of both orderings (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b)).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Reference; standard.)} $\omega_{c}$ is Hadamard.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Criterion; the standard flat criterion carried by conformal covariance; the converse given the moment lemma.)} If $M_{k} < \infty$ for every $k$, both remainders are smooth on $M \times M$ and $\omega$ is Hadamard. Conversely, if $\omega$ is Hadamard, every $M_{k}$ is finite. More precisely, $M_{0}, \dots, M_{j} < \infty$ gives remainders of class $C^{j}$, and a remainder of class $C^{2m+1}$ along a timelike line gives $M_{2m+1} < \infty$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The thermal deposit; proved.)} For the Fermi-Dirac profile $n_{\pm} = (e^{p/T} + 1)^{-1}$ (Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state}; $T = a_{d}T_{d}$ comoving), $M_{k} \le 16\pi\,(k + 2)!\,T^{k + 3}$ for every $k$, so the thermal deposit is Hadamard; so is every diagonal deposit whose profile is bounded by $C_{N}(1 + p/T)^{-N}$ for every $N$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The shot-noise data do not decide it; proved.)} The profile $n_{\pm} = (1 + p/T)^{-6}$ has finite number, mean energy $\tfrac32 T$ and energy spread $c = \langle\omega^{2}\rangle/\langle\omega\rangle^{2} = \tfrac83$, so the shot term of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(iv) is finite, while $M_{k} = \infty$ for every $k \ge 3$: its remainders are of class $C^{2}$ and not of class $C^{3}$ along a timelike line, and it is not Hadamard.
\item[(v)] \emph{(A finite number alone, Hadamard or not; proved.)} If $M_{0} < \infty$, then $|R^{(\pm)}(x, y)| \le (2\pi)^{-3}M_{0}\,a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}$, a bounded remainder, so at every point $x_{0}$ the scaling limit of $\omega$ (weight $\tfrac32$ per leg) equals that of $\omega_{c}$, the flat massless vacuum in the local inertial coordinates $a(t_{0})(x - x_{0})$, even when $\omega$ is not Hadamard.
\end{enumerate}
So under the hypothesis the stored thermal deposit is a Hadamard state on the descent's collar; the number of quanta controls the scaling limit, the first two moments the shot noise, and the whole ultraviolet tail the Hadamard class.
synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vac.technical:
The question is whether the state the descent deposits on the fields is a Hadamard state, the class on which a renormalised stress tensor exists and which the horizon premises need. The store describes the deposit as the vacuum plus quanta, with a bound on its fluctuations in terms of the number of quanta and their energy spread.

The result assumes that the descended field near the descent is of Robertson-Walker form with a smooth scale factor, as for a descent of radiation type; a kink in the scale factor would make the Hadamard condition undefined there. It treats the massless Dirac field, which is conformally the flat one, so the conformal vacuum is Hadamard, and deposits diagonal in that vacuum's particle modes, with no particle-antiparticle pair coherence. Such a deposit is Hadamard exactly when every moment of its occupation profile is finite. This is the standard flat-space criterion, carried over by conformal covariance: sufficiency by differentiating under the integral, necessity because odd time derivatives at coincidence weigh particles and antiparticles with the same sign, so their finiteness forces the moments.

The thermal profile decays exponentially and has every moment, so the thermal deposit is Hadamard. A profile falling as the sixth inverse power has a finite shot term, the kind of data the stored bound uses, yet infinite moments from the third on: it is twice but not three times differentiable at coincidence and not Hadamard. So the number of quanta does not decide the Hadamard property. A finite number alone still makes the remainder bounded, so the deposit looks like the vacuum at short distances even when it is not Hadamard. Transport-absent.
synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vac.lay: When the universe's earlier phase handed its contents to the later one, it left the quantum fields in some state. Physics in a gravitational field needs that state to be of a particular well-behaved kind, called Hadamard, which roughly means it looks like empty space at very short distances in a smooth way. This result shows, for massless spin-one-half particles and assuming the young universe was uniform and expanding smoothly, that a thermal hand-over, the kind the series uses, is of that kind. It also shows that the series' earlier calculation of how much the hand-over can disturb things, which uses only how many particles there are and how their energies spread, cannot settle the question: what matters is how fast the number of particles falls off at high energy.

proofs.main:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$; $\Cl(1,3)$ with $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{i}^{2} = -1$; the unit imaginary is $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$ ($I_{4}^{2} = -1$, checked). Matrix forms are parenthetical readings of left multiplication.

\emph{Set-up.} The field $\hb(b) = b/a(t)$ has $\hb^{-1}(b) = a\,b$, so its derived metric is $g(u, v) = a^{2}\,u\cdot v$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i)), conformally flat, so the Weyl part of its field strength vanishes (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(a)); $a$ is smooth and positive on the collar by hypothesis. The massless Dirac equation is conformally covariant with weight $\tfrac32$: $\psi = a^{-3/2}\chi$ solves it on $(\hb, \Omega)$ exactly when $\chi$ solves the flat massless equation (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(b); the conformal transfer of null geodesics and wave-front sets is proved for every conformal factor in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scaling-limit-premise-and-robertson-walker-generators-see-the-schwarzian}(i)), and the map is unitary for the conserved current, so the CAR algebras of $\psi$ and $\chi$ are identified. The flat massless vacuum of $\chi$ has (matrix reading, as in the stored kernels of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}; the phases are numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$) $\omega_{c}(\chi(x)\chi^{\dagger}(y)) = \int\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}}\Lambda_{+}(\hat p)\,e^{-I_{4}p\cdot(x - y)}$ and the other ordering with $\Lambda_{-}$, where $p = |\vec p|(e_{0} + \hat p)$ is the null momentum, $\hat p$ the unit spatial vector ($\hat p^{2} = -1$) and $\Lambda_{\pm}(\hat p) = \tfrac12(1 \pm \hat p e_{0})$. The check verifies on Pythagorean directions that $(\hat p e_{0})^{2} = 1$, that $\Lambda_{\pm}$ are idempotent, complementary, mutually annihilating and self-adjoint for the Dirac adjoint ($e_{0}\tilde\Lambda e_{0} = \Lambda$), with scalar part $\tfrac12$, that $\Lambda_{+} = pe_{0}/(2p_{0})$ and $p\Lambda_{+} = 0$ on the null shell: orthogonal projectors of norm one onto the solutions.

\emph{The deposit's remainder.} In the quasi-particle modes of $\omega_{c}$ (annihilators $a_{\vec p}$ for particles, $b_{\vec p}$ for antiparticles), the deposit has $\omega(a^{\dagger}a) = n_{+}$ and $\omega(bb^{\dagger}) = 1 - n_{-}$ mode by mode, with no coherences and no pairing (gauge invariance and diagonality). Hence each remainder is a superposition of plane waves,
\[
R^{(\pm)}(x, y) = a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}\sum_{h}\int\frac{d^{3}p}{(2\pi)^{3}}\Bigl(\epsilon^{\pm}_{+}\,n_{+}(p)\,\Pi_{+}\,e^{-I_{4}p\cdot(x - y)} + \epsilon^{\pm}_{-}\,n_{-}(p)\,\Pi_{-}\,e^{+I_{4}p\cdot(x - y)}\Bigr),
\]
summed over the helicities $h$, with signs $\epsilon = \pm 1$ fixed by the ordering and projector weights $\Pi_{\pm}$ of the form $\Lambda_{\pm}(\pm\hat p)$ (times a helicity projector), of norm one. The factor $a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}$ is smooth and nonvanishing, so smoothness and boundedness of $R^{(\pm)}$ are those of the integral.

\emph{(i)} This is standard, and is proved for every conformal factor in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scaling-limit-premise-and-robertson-walker-generators-see-the-schwarzian}(i): the flat null lines with affine parameter $\tilde\lambda$, $d\tilde\lambda = a^{2}d\lambda$, are the affine null geodesics of the derived metric (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(iii)) and carry the flat covectors, so the relation $\sim$ and the sets $C^{\pm}$ of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition} are the same for the derived metric and the flat one. The flat massless vacuum satisfies $\mathrm{WF}'(\mathcal{G}^{(\pm)}) = C^{\pm}$ (Fact (b) for the flat field), and multiplication by the smooth nonvanishing $a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}$ does not change a wave-front set (standard). So $\omega_{c}$ is Hadamard on $(\hb, \Omega)$.

\emph{(ii), sufficiency.} This is the standard flat-space criterion (rapid decrease of the occupation numbers), carried to the descended field by conformal covariance; the argument is recorded for completeness. For a null momentum $|p_{\mu}| \le p$ in every component, so every derivative of order $j$ of the integrand in $(x, y)$ is bounded by $p^{j}(n_{+} + n_{-})$ times a constant; if $M_{0}, \dots, M_{j} < \infty$ (the factor 2 in $M_{k}$ counts the helicities), dominated convergence gives remainders of class $C^{j}$, and if every $M_{k}$ is finite they are smooth. A smooth kernel has empty wave-front set, so $\mathrm{WF}'(\mathcal{G}^{(\pm)}_{\omega}) = \mathrm{WF}'(\mathcal{G}^{(\pm)}_{\omega_{c}}) = C^{\pm}$ and $\omega$ is Hadamard by (i).

\emph{(ii), necessity.} Suppose $\omega$ is Hadamard; by Fact (b) its remainders relative to the Hadamard $\omega_{c}$ are smooth. Restrict the ordering $\omega(\chi^{\dagger}(y)\chi(x))$ to a timelike line $x = y + \tau e_{0}$ and take the scalar part of the spin trace: $\phi(\tau) = \int e^{-I_{4}\nu\tau}\,d\mu(\nu)$ in the frequency $\nu$, where particles sit at $\nu = p$ with weight $+n_{+}$ and antiparticles at $\nu = -p$ with weight $-n_{-}$ (the sign of reordering $bb^{\dagger}$ against the vacuum), both times the positive spin trace. The measure $\mu$ is signed, but $\nu\,d\mu$ is positive: $p \cdot n_{+} \ge 0$ and $(-p)(-n_{-}) \ge 0$, and for every odd power $\nu^{2m+1}d\mu$ weighs particles and antiparticles alike by $p^{2m + 1}n_{\pm}$ (checked, with the even powers shown to mix signs). So $I_{4}\phi'$ is the Fourier transform of the positive tempered measure $\nu\,d\mu$. A positive tempered measure whose Fourier transform is continuous near $0$ is finite, and if the transform is of class $C^{2m}$ near $0$ the measure has a finite moment of order $2m$ (Bochner's theorem and the moment lemma for characteristic functions, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-bochner-theorem-moment-lemma-and-whitney-even-functions}(a), (b); the step uses that $(z + z^{-1} - 2)^{m} = (-1)^{m}|z - 1|^{2m}$ for unit $z = c + sI_{4}$, so the $2m$-th symmetric differences at coincidence are of one sign, checked on Pythagorean phases). Hence a remainder of class $C^{2m+1}$ along the line, for which $I_{4}\phi'$ is of class $C^{2m}$, gives $\int p^{2m + 1}(n_{+} + n_{-})\,d^{3}p < \infty$, that is $M_{2m+1} < \infty$, and smoothness gives every odd moment; the even ones follow from $p^{2m} \le 1 + p^{2m+1}$ and $n_{\pm} \le 1$ on $p < 1$.

\emph{(iii)} The thermal deposit has the Fermi-Dirac occupations of Theorem \claimref{hawking.i-state} in the comoving momenta. With $y = e^{-p/T} \in (0, 1]$, $n_{\mathrm{FD}} = y/(1 + y) \le y$ (checked on samples), and $\int_{0}^{\infty}x^{k}e^{-x}dx = k!$: the antiderivative is $-e^{-x}P_{k}(x)$ with $P_{k} = \sum_{j \le k}\tfrac{k!}{j!}x^{j}$, and $P_{k} - P_{k}' = x^{k}$, an exact polynomial identity (checked for $k \le 15$, with the factorials $0!, \dots, 7!$ and the bounds $16(k+2)!$ for $k \le 3$ asserted). So $M_{k} \le 2\cdot 2\cdot 4\pi\int_{0}^{\infty}p^{k + 2}e^{-p/T}dp = 16\pi(k + 2)!\,T^{k + 3}$ (two helicities, particles and antiparticles), finite for every $k$; by (ii) the thermal deposit is Hadamard. The exact moments are $16\pi(k + 2)!\,\eta(k + 3)T^{k+3}$ with $1 - 2^{-s} \le \eta(s) \le 1$ (alternating series, standard). The same bound holds whenever $n_{\pm} \le C_{N}(1 + p/T)^{-N}$ for every $N$.

\emph{(iv)} For $n = (1 + p/T)^{-6}$, substitute $q = u/(1 + u)$, $u = p/T$: $\int_{0}^{\infty}u^{2 + k}(1 + u)^{-6}du = \int_{0}^{1}q^{2 + k}(1 - q)^{2 - k}dq$, which is $\tfrac{1}{30}$, $\tfrac{1}{20}$, $\tfrac15$ for $k = 0, 1, 2$ (exact polynomial integrals, checked). So the number density, the mean energy $\tfrac{1/20}{1/30}T = \tfrac32 T$ and the energy spread $c = \tfrac{(1/5)(1/30)}{(1/20)^{2}} = \tfrac83$ are finite, and the shot term $(3c_{k}k^{3}/2\pi^{2}\bar n)^{1/2}$ of Proposition \claimref{synthesis.quasi-free-deposit-is-vacuum-plus-shot-noise}(iv) is finite ($c_{k} \le c(1 + k/\langle\omega\rangle)^{2}$ as there). For $k = 3$ the integrand is $q^{5}(1 - q)^{-1}$; on the piece $[1 - 2^{1 - j}, 1 - 2^{-j}]$ of length $2^{-j}$, $(1 - q)^{-1} \ge 2^{j - 1}$ and $q^{5} \ge (1 - 2^{1 - j})^{5}$, so each piece contributes at least $\tfrac12(1 - 2^{1-j})^{5} \ge \tfrac{1}{10}$ for $j \ge 3$ and the integral diverges (checked over forty pieces); since $u^{2 + k} \ge u^{5}$ for $u \ge 1$, every $M_{k}$ with $k \ge 3$ is infinite. By (ii) the remainders are of class $C^{2}$ and, since $M_{3} = \infty$, not of class $C^{3}$ along a timelike line; the deposit is not Hadamard. So the number of quanta and their energy spread, the data of the stored shot-noise bound, do not decide the Hadamard property. The profile is a valid occupation, $0 < n \le 1$.

\emph{(v)} With $\|\Pi_{\pm}\| = 1$, $|R^{(\pm)}(x, y)| \le a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}(2\pi)^{-3}\sum_{h}\int d^{3}p\,(n_{+} + n_{-}) = (2\pi)^{-3}M_{0}\,a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}$, the stated bound, finite when $M_{0}$ is, whether or not the higher moments are. Under the scaling about $x_{0}$ with weight $\tfrac32$ per leg, $(S_{l}R)(x, y) = l^{3}R(x_{0} + lx, x_{0} + ly)$, a remainder bounded by $C$ near $x_{0}$ is bounded by $l^{3}C \to 0$. The scaling limit of $\omega_{c}$ is the flat massless vacuum in the local inertial coordinates $a(t_{0})(x - x_{0})$: its kernel is $a(x)^{-3/2}a(y)^{-3/2}$ times the flat one, which is homogeneous of degree $-3$ (standard; computed in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.weyl-flat-fields-need-no-scaling-limit-premise-and-robertson-walker-generators-see-the-schwarzian}(i)). So the scaling limit of $\omega$ is the same, even when $\omega$ is not Hadamard; for Hadamard states this is that result's clause (i).

synthesis.electron-positron-to-muon-pair.technical:
With the conventions of one-loop electrodynamics in the spacetime algebra, the scattering of an electron and a positron into a muon pair is computed through the reduction formula. On shell, the propagator residue $p + m$ is twice the mass times an idempotent of trace two, so the spin sums of the external states are the real multivectors $p + m$ (particles) and $p - m$ (antiparticles); no imaginary unit enters.

At tree level the spin-averaged squared amplitude is the product of two Clifford traces, which reproduces the standard form exactly; for massless leptons it gives the $1 + \cos^{2}\theta$ distribution and $\sigma = 4\pi\alpha^{2}/(3s)$, and with the muon mass the threshold factor $\beta(3 - \beta^{2})/2$ (checked exactly at rational speeds, including threshold-free and massless limits).

At one loop the vacuum-polarisation insertion on the s-channel photon multiplies the tree amplitude by $1/(1 - \hat\Pi(s))$, the longitudinal part dropping between on-shell currents. Its absorptive part, the integral of $x(1-x)$ over the window where $x(1-x)s > m^{2}$, is $(\alpha/3)\beta(3 - \beta^{2})/2$ in size, which is exactly $s\sigma_{\mathrm{tree}}/(4\pi\alpha)$ for producing that fermion: the s-channel optical-theorem relation for the photon self-energy. The loop has no internal photon and the subtracted function does not depend on the regulator. At high energy the insertion is $(\alpha/(3\pi))(\ln(s/m^{2}) - 5/3)$, the running of the coupling, and under the Krein-form premise $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ makes the charge renormalisation $Z_{3}^{1/2}$ alone. These are standard results, recomputed. Vertex and box corrections and soft-photon emission are not computed.
synthesis.electron-positron-to-muon-pair.lay: The series' algebra of spacetime now reproduces a standard textbook scattering prediction: an electron and a positron annihilate into a muon and an antimuon. The incoming and outgoing particles are fixed by algebraic projections built from their momenta, each picking out the particle's two spin states, and the rate comes out as the textbook formula, with the characteristic angular pattern and the suppression near the energy threshold for making the muons. At the next order the photon in the middle is dressed by virtual pairs; the part of this dressing that corresponds to real pairs being produced matches the rate computed at the first order exactly, one instance of the rule that probabilities add up to one, and the rest is the slow growth of the electric force with energy. Reading that growth as a change of the charge itself assumes the series' premise that the photon's states carry the standard indefinite measure.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} $\Cl(1,3)$ with signature $(+,-,-,-)$; vectors $p = p^{\mu}\gamma_{\mu}$, $\gamma^{\mu}$ the reciprocal frame; the matrix trace is $4\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ and the units of the Feynman rules, the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, are coefficients collected outside the product (the right unit) (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(1), (5)). The vertex is $\gamma^{\mu}$ with the coupling of \claimref{field-theory.coupled-system-tree-level}; the free Dirac fields and their two spin states per momentum are those of \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}. The s-channel photon at tree level couples conserved currents, so the stored photon suffices there. The polarisation loop inside the photon line is a fermion loop with no internal photon; the stored result computes it with Pauli-Villars fermions (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}), and the subtracted function $\hat\Pi$ used here does not depend on the regulator (a regulator-free construction with no Krein form is \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}(ii)). Only the charge-renormalisation sentence of Step 5 uses loops with an internal photon, and so the Krein-form premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}.

\emph{Step 1 (LSZ).} Let $Q(p) = m^{2}$. Then $p^{2} = m^{2}$ as multivectors, so $(p + m)^{2} = p^{2} + 2mp + m^{2} = 2m(p + m)$, $(p - m)^{2} = -2m(p - m)$ and $(p + m)(p - m) = p^{2} - m^{2} = 0$; $\langle p\rangle_{0} = 0$ gives $4\langle p \pm m\rangle_{0} = \pm 4m$. So for $m \neq 0$, $P_{\pm} = (m \pm p)/(2m)$ are complementary idempotents with $4\langle P_{\pm}\rangle_{0} = 2$: each projects the spinor module onto a two-dimensional space, the two spin states. Off shell $(p - m)S(p) = 1$ with $S(p) = (p + m)/(Q(p) - m^{2})$, and $(Q(p) - m^{2})S(p) = p + m$, the residue at the pole. The reduction formula \cite{LSZ1955} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lsz-reduction-ward-identity-and-the-second-qed-beta-coefficient}(i); Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(v)) writes an S-matrix element as the amputated Green function at the poles times $Z_{2}^{1/2}$ per external fermion; at tree level $Z_{2} = 1$. Summed over spins, an outgoing particle and an incoming particle contribute $p + m$ (the residue), an incoming antiparticle and an outgoing antiparticle $p - m$ (the residue of $S(-p)$ up to sign). For $m = 0$ the residue $p$ is nilpotent ($p^{2} = 0$) and $4\langle\cdot\rangle_{0}$ of $p$ times anything is the massless spin sum. The check verifies these identities at three rational on-shell momenta (masses $4$, $12$, $0$) and the residue at an off-shell momentum.

\emph{Step 2 (tree amplitude).} With $q = p_{1} + p_{2}$, the amplitude is $M = \frac{e^{2}}{s}\,[\bar v(p_{2})\gamma^{\mu}u(p_{1})][\bar u(p_{3})\gamma_{\mu}v(p_{4})]$ (units collected in front). Squaring and summing over spins by Step 1, $\tfrac14\sum|M|^{2} = \tfrac{e^{4}}{4s^{2}}T_{e}^{\mu\nu}T_{\mu\nu}^{\mu}$ with $T_{e}^{\mu\nu} = 4\langle(p_{2} - m_{e})\gamma^{\mu}(p_{1} + m_{e})\gamma^{\nu}\rangle_{0}$, $T^{\mu}_{\mu\nu} = 4\langle(p_{3} + m_{\mu})\gamma_{\mu}(p_{4} - m_{\mu})\gamma_{\nu}\rangle_{0}$. Expanding $4\langle abcd\rangle_{0} = 4[(a\cdot b)(c\cdot d) - (a\cdot c)(b\cdot d) + (a\cdot d)(b\cdot c)]$ and $4\langle ab\rangle_{0} = 4a\cdot b$ gives the standard form of clause (2); the check computes the two traces and their contraction exactly at three rational configurations (both masses, electron massless, both massless) and compares with the standard form, with a control (the particle residue in place of the positron's fails). Massless kinematics in the centre-of-mass frame, $p_{1} = E(\gamma_{0} + \gamma_{3})$, $p_{3} = E(\gamma_{0} + \sin\theta\,\gamma_{1} + \cos\theta\,\gamma_{3})$, give $\tfrac14\sum|M|^{2} = e^{4}(1 + \cos^{2}\theta)$ (checked at five rational angles; a polynomial of degree two in $\cos\theta$ is fixed by three). With $d\sigma/d\Omega = \tfrac{1}{64\pi^{2}s}\tfrac{|p_{3}|}{|p_{1}|}\tfrac14\sum|M|^{2}$ (standard two-body phase space \cite{PeskinSchroeder1995}) and $e^{2} = 4\pi\alpha$: $d\sigma/d\Omega = \tfrac{\alpha^{2}}{4s}(1 + \cos^{2}\theta)$ and $\sigma = 2\pi\tfrac{\alpha^{2}}{4s}\int_{-1}^{1}(1 + c^{2})\,dc = \tfrac{4\pi\alpha^{2}}{3s}$. For $m_{e} = 0$ and muon speed $\beta$ ($m_{\mu} = \tfrac{\sqrt s}{2}(1 - \beta^{2})^{1/2}$) the trace result is a polynomial of degree two in $c = \cos\theta$; it is fixed by $c = -1, 0, 1$, checked at $c = 3/5$, and $\sigma\,s/(\pi\alpha^{2}) = \tfrac{\beta}{2}\int_{-1}^{1}\tfrac{|M|^{2}}{e^{4}}dc = \tfrac43\cdot\tfrac{\beta(3 - \beta^{2})}{2}$ at $\beta = \tfrac35, \tfrac45, \tfrac{12}{13}, 1$, exactly. Since both sides are polynomials in $\beta$ of degree three after multiplying by $s^{2}$ and fixing $s$, four values of $\beta$ establish the identity at that $s$, and both scale as $1/s$.

\emph{Step 3 (one loop: the insertion).} The photon two-point function with polarisation insertions is, in a covariant gauge (the unit of the Feynman rules the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), $\frac{-I_{4}}{q^{2}(1 - \hat\Pi(q^{2}))}\bigl(g_{\mu\nu} - \frac{q_{\mu}q_{\nu}}{q^{2}}\bigr) + (\text{gauge part})\frac{q_{\mu}q_{\nu}}{q^{4}}$, by transversality of the stored polarisation (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(2)). Between on-shell currents every $q_{\mu}$ term vanishes: $4\langle(p_{2} - m)\,q\,(p_{1} + m)\gamma^{\nu}\rangle_{0} = 0$ for $q = p_{1} + p_{2}$, because $(p_{2} - m)(p_{1} + p_{2})(p_{1} + m) = (p_{2} - m)[(p_{1} - m) + (p_{2} + m)](p_{1} + m) = 0$ by Step 1; the check verifies this for both currents and every $\nu$, with the control $q = p_{1} - p_{2}$, which does not drop. So the s-channel amplitude is $M_{\mathrm{tree}}/(1 - \hat\Pi(s))$, with $\hat\Pi(s) = \Pi(s) - \Pi(0)$ the on-shell subtracted function of the stored result: $\hat\Pi(s) = -\tfrac{2\alpha}{\pi}\int_{0}^{1}x(1 - x)\ln\frac{m^{2}}{m^{2} - x(1-x)s - I_{4}0}dx$ (\cite{PeskinSchroeder1995}, sec. 7.5, eqs. (7.90) to (7.92); the regulator scale cancels in the subtraction).

\emph{Step 4 (absorptive part and the optical theorem).} For $s > 4m^{2}$ the argument $m^{2} - x(1-x)s$ is negative exactly on the window $x_{-} < x < x_{+}$, $x_{\pm} = (1 \pm \beta)/2$, since $x_{\pm}(1 - x_{\pm}) = (1 - \beta^{2})/4 = m^{2}/s$ (checked). There $\ln\frac{m^{2}}{A - I_{4}0} = \ln\frac{m^{2}}{|A|} + I_{4}\pi$ ($\mathrm{Im}$ the coefficient of $I_{4}$), so $\mathrm{Im}\,\hat\Pi(s + I_{4}0) = -2\alpha\int_{x_{-}}^{x_{+}}(x - x^{2})dx = -\tfrac{\alpha}{6}\beta(3 - \beta^{2})$, exactly (checked at four rational $\beta$; the integral is the polynomial $\beta(3 - \beta^{2})/12$). By Step 2, $s\,\sigma_{\mathrm{tree}}(e^{+}e^{-} \to f\bar f)/(4\pi\alpha) = \tfrac{\alpha}{4}\cdot\tfrac43\cdot\tfrac{\beta(3 - \beta^{2})}{2} = \tfrac{\alpha}{6}\beta(3 - \beta^{2})$, the same. This is the s-channel optical-theorem relation for the photon self-energy: the discontinuity of the one-loop photon line is the phase-space integral of the squared tree amplitude for producing the pair (\cite{PeskinSchroeder1995}, sec. 7.3; argued here, the two sides computed). Full unitarity of the S-matrix at order $e^{4}$ also involves $e^{+}e^{-} \to \gamma\gamma$, the t-channel and box cuts, which are not computed.

\emph{Step 5 (large $s$ and the charge).} For $s \gg m^{2}$, $\ln\frac{m^{2}}{|m^{2} - x(1-x)s|} = -\ln\frac{s}{m^{2}} - \ln(x(1-x)) + O(m^{2}/s)$, so $\mathrm{Re}\,\hat\Pi = \tfrac{2\alpha}{\pi}[\tfrac16\ln\tfrac{s}{m^{2}} + J]$ with $J = \int_{0}^{1}x(1-x)\ln(x(1-x))\,dx = 2\int_{0}^{1}(x - x^{2})\ln x\,dx = 2(-\tfrac14 + \tfrac19) = -\tfrac{5}{18}$, by $\int_{0}^{1}x^{n}\ln x\,dx = -1/(n+1)^{2}$: $\mathrm{Re}\,\hat\Pi = \tfrac{\alpha}{3\pi}(\ln\tfrac{s}{m^{2}} - \tfrac53)$ (the rationals checked). In multiplicative renormalisation the charge is $e = Z_{1}^{-1}Z_{2}Z_{3}^{1/2}e_{0}$ (the vertex counterterm $Z_{1}$, the fermion field factor $Z_{2}^{1/2}$ on either side of the vertex, which LSZ supplies on external legs, and the photon field factor $Z_{3}^{1/2}$); under the Krein-form premise, with $Z_{1} = Z_{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(4); Ward's identity, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-lsz-reduction-ward-identity-and-the-second-qed-beta-coefficient}(ii)) the fermion factors cancel and $e = Z_{3}^{1/2}e_{0}$, so the insertion is the running coupling $\alpha(s) = \alpha/(1 - \mathrm{Re}\,\hat\Pi(s))$ at this order (argued). Not computed: the vertex and box corrections and real soft-photon emission, whose infrared divergences cancel only in the inclusive rate.

\emph{Status.} Clause (1) proved (algebra); clause (2) computed exactly (an identity of polynomials, sampled at rational kinematics) with the phase-space formula imported; clause (3) computed for the absorptive part and the constant, argued for the optical-theorem reading and the charge renormalisation. All standard (LSZ 1955; Peskin and Schroeder secs. 5.1, 7.3, 7.5), recomputed in the spacetime algebra. Transport-absent; the spacetime algebra is convenient.

synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.formal:
Fields at a point and all their derivatives generate the jet algebra: $A^{a}_{\mu}$ and $B^{a}$ even, the ghosts $c^{a}$ and antighosts $\bar c^{a}$ odd (generators of a Grassmann algebra, the Clifford algebra of a form that vanishes), the coupling $g$ and gauge parameter $\xi$ even constants; $\partial_\mu$ acts by shifting the jet index. The gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ of the minimal massive composite, Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} has basis $T_a$ with $[T_a, T_b] = f_{ab}{}^{c}T_c$. The vector potential is $A = T_a A^{a}$, $A^{a} = A^{a}_{\mu}\gamma^{\mu}$ a vector field of the spacetime algebra, $\nabla = \gamma^{\mu}\partial_\mu$, and the field strength is the bivector $F^{a} = \nabla\wedge A^{a} + \tfrac{g}{2}f_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}\wedge A^{c}$. The BRST differential $s$ is the odd derivation, acting from the left and commuting with every $\partial_\mu$, with
\[
sA^{a} = \nabla c^{a} + g f_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}c^{c}, \qquad sc^{a} = -\tfrac{g}{2}f_{bc}{}^{a}c^{b}c^{c}, \qquad s\bar c^{a} = B^{a}, \qquad sB^{a} = 0 .
\]
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The algebra as bivectors; computed.)} The twelve bivectors $T_{1,2,3} = \tfrac12 e_{12}, \tfrac12 e_{20}, \tfrac12 e_{01}$ on $e_0, e_1, e_2$, the eight traceless bivectors of the $e_3, \dots, e_8$ block commuting with $J = e_{34} + e_{56} + e_{78}$, and $T_{12} = \tfrac12 J$, in $\Cl(9,0)$, close under the commutator into $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$: $58$ nonzero rational structure constants, $J$ spanning the centre, a derived algebra $[\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{g}]$ of dimension $11$, a positive-definite ad-invariant form $\kappa_{ab} = -\langle T_aT_b\rangle_0$, and an eight-dimensional block whose adjoint representation has one-dimensional commutant. This realisation is isomorphic to, not identical with, the realisation on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite}, and it does not fix how the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ (hypercharge) acts on matter; the pure gauge differential depends only on the isomorphism class.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Nilpotency; proved.)} For any Lie algebra, $s^2 = 0$ on the whole jet algebra, for every $g$. The check confirms $s^2 = 0$ exactly on all $300$ generators $A^{a}_{\mu}$, $c^{a}$ with at most one derivative for the algebra of (i), as polynomials in $g$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(What nilpotency needs; computed.)} Replacing $\tfrac{g}{2}$ by $2g$ in $sc$ leaves $s^2c = 0$ but gives $s^2A^{a}_{\mu} = 3(D_\mu Y)^{a}$ with $Y = sc$ the correct ghost variation (in general the residual is $(2h - 1)D_\mu Y$ for $sc = -hg[c, c]$); dropping the term $gf_{bc}{}^{a}A^{b}c^{c}$ gives $s^2A^{a}_{\mu} = \partial_\mu(sc^{a})$, nonzero on the $44$ components of the eleven non-abelian generators; shifting one antisymmetric pair of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ structure constants (so that the Jacobi identity fails) gives $s^2 \neq 0$ on $30$ of the $60$ underived generators.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Covariance and invariance; proved.)} $sF^{a} = g f_{bc}{}^{a}F^{b}c^{c}$, so for every ad-invariant $\kappa$ the scalar and pseudoscalar densities $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_0$ and $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_4$ are $s$-invariant. The check confirms the first identity for all twelve components, the ad-invariance of $\kappa$ and its failure for a perturbed $\kappa$, and the invariance of both densities on the $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ block exactly, with a perturbed $\kappa$ breaking the scalar one.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Gauge fixing; proved.)} With $\Psi = \kappa_{ab}\bar c^{a}(\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{b})$,
\[
s\Psi = \kappa_{ab}\big(B^{a}\,\nabla\cdot A^{b} + \tfrac{\xi}{2}B^{a}B^{b} - \bar c^{a}\,\nabla\cdot(Dc)^{b}\big), \qquad (Dc)^{b} = \nabla c^{b} + g f_{cd}{}^{b}A^{c}c^{d},
\]
so $\kappa_{ab}\langle F^{a}F^{b}\rangle_0 + s\Psi$, the Yang-Mills density with a covariant gauge fixing and the Faddeev-Popov operator $\nabla\cdot D$, is $s$-invariant; the check confirms the expansion and $s(s\Psi) = 0$ for the full algebra.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} The non-abelian gauge fields of $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ admit the standard covariant BRST gauge fixing at the level of local fields: the ghost's covariant derivative is forced (iii), and the differential is nilpotent for every coupling. The differential involves no imaginary unit and no inner product, so it is compatible with $i = I_4$ and is independent of the Krein-form premise (KF); that premise and the quartet mechanism concern the state space, not the differential. Standard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(i)); transport-absent. Not addressed: the Goldstone and doublet terms of the differential, the operator charge of the interacting theory, its renormalisation, anomalies and the Gribov ambiguity, which confines the construction to perturbation theory (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv); the lattice computation \claimref{synthesis.non-abelian-gauge-fixing-has-gribov-copies-and-the-weak-rotor-lattice-with-doublets-has-a-perimeter-law}).
synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.technical:
The problem asks for the interacting BRST charge of the gluons and the W and Z, in which the ghost's covariant derivative acts on the gauge field. At the level of local fields this is a differential on the algebra generated by the fields and their derivatives. Here the gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ of the minimal massive composite is written, up to isomorphism, by bivectors of $\Cl(9,0)$: the weak factor as half the bivectors on $e_0, e_1, e_2$ (the rotor generators already used on the stored lattice), colour as the eight traceless bivectors of the $e_3, \dots, e_8$ block that commute with a complex structure $J$, and the $\mathfrak{u}(1)$ as $J/2$. This is isomorphic to the stored realisation on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, not identical with it, and it does not fix the hypercharge embedding, which the pure gauge differential does not see; with matter or Goldstone fields it would matter. The structure constants are rational and exact, and the commutant test identifies the eight-dimensional block as simple, hence $\mathfrak{su}(3)$.

The vector potential is a Lie-algebra-valued vector field of the spacetime algebra and its field strength is the bivector $F = \nabla\wedge A + \tfrac{g}{2}[A\wedge A]$. The differential acts as a gauge transformation with the ghost as parameter, $sA = Dc$, and on the ghost as $sc = -\tfrac{g}{2}[c, c]$. Squaring to zero on the ghost is the Jacobi identity; on the vector potential it needs, in addition, the factor $\tfrac12$ and the covariant term, and the exact computation shows each failing when altered. Because $s$ commutes with derivatives, nilpotency on the underived fields gives it on every derivative; the check confirms it directly up to first derivatives (300 generators), as a polynomial identity in the coupling.

The field strength transforms covariantly, so both invariant densities, the Yang-Mills scalar $\langle FF\rangle_0$ and the pseudoscalar $\langle FF\rangle_4$, are BRST invariant for any ad-invariant form. A gauge-fixing fermion $\Psi$ adds the exact term $s\Psi$, which contains the covariant gauge condition, the Gaussian weight $\tfrac{\xi}{2}B^2$ and the Faddeev-Popov term $-\bar c\,\nabla\cdot Dc$; invariance of the sum is then nilpotency. All of this is standard BRST, recomputed in the series' algebra; nothing in it comes from transport. The Goldstone and doublet terms of the differential are not included, and the construction is perturbative (Gribov copies, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv)). The differential has rational coefficients, so the unit $i = I_4$ never enters, and it needs no inner product; positivity of the physical states is a statement about the state space (the Krein-form premise and the quartet mechanism), which this result does not touch.
synthesis.field-level-brst-differential-.lay: To describe the strong and weak forces as quantum fields in a way that respects relativity, one adds fictitious ghost fields and a bookkeeping operation that must give zero when applied twice. This result writes that operation for the full set of the series' force fields (without the Higgs fields' part), with the force fields' symmetry written as plane elements of a Clifford algebra, and checks exactly that it gives zero twice, for any strength of the force. It also shows that each ingredient is needed: removing the term in which the ghost feels the force field, or changing a factor of one half, spoils it. The usual energy of the force fields and the usual way of fixing the gauge pass the test. Nothing here is new physics; it confirms that the series' algebra carries the standard construction.

synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.formal:
Let a floor of the tower carry $2N$ planes, with mode operators $a_k^{*}, a_k$ ($k = -N, \dots, N - 1$) obeying the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}, read as the right-moving modes of one chirality on a circle of $2N$ momenta in units of the circle's $2\pi/L$, with $n_k = a_k^{*}a_k$, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$, $\mathcal{N} = \sum_k n_k$ and $\rho(p) = \sum_{k,\,k+p} a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ (both indices in the window).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Charge and continuity; proved.)} $[\mathcal{N}, H] = 0$, $[\mathcal{N}, \rho(p)] = 0$ and $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$ exactly on every floor, for $1 \le |p| \le 2N - 1$; $\rho(\pm 2N) = 0$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The central term is an edge operator; proved.)} For $1 \le p \le 2N$,
\[
[\rho(p), \rho(-p)] = \sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k - \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k ,
\]
whose scalar part is zero; no floor carries a nonzero scalar central term.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(The continuum value below the cut-off; proved.)} On the filled sea $\Omega$ ($n_k = 1$ for $k < 0$, $0$ otherwise), $\rho(-p)\Omega = 0$, $[\rho(-p), \rho(p)]\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$, and $\rho(p)\Omega$ is an eigenvector of $H$ at energy $E_\Omega + p$ with $\rho(-p)\rho(p)\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$. So $b_p = \rho(-p)/\sqrt{p}$ satisfies $[b_p, b_p^{*}] = 1$ on $\Omega$ exactly for $p \le N$, the continuum central term $p$ and the continuum one-loop density response (all spectral weight at energy $p$, total weight $p$) are reproduced exactly up to the cut-off, and above it the weight is $2N - p$. The value depends on the state at the window's edges: with the top mode also occupied, $[\rho(-1), \rho(1)]$ acts as $0$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(No boost survives the conformal-energy cut; proved.)} In $\Cl(2,4)$ the commutant of the conformal Hamiltonian $\gamma_0e_+$ (the compact combination of $P_0 = \gamma_0n_\infty$ and $K_0 = \gamma_0n_0$, up to normalisation) among the fifteen bivectors is seven-dimensional; it meets the Lorentz bivectors in the span of the three rotations and contains no nonzero translation and no nonzero special conformal generator. So, if the floors are the conformal-energy cut-offs of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, every finite floor is invariant under the spatial rotations and not under any boost.
\item[(v)] \emph{(No weighting of the floors keeps a boost; merged from Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}(vii), 2 November 2026.)} The commutant $\mathfrak{k}$ of (iv) is closed under the commutator, and $\mathfrak{k}$ together with any one of the eight basis bivectors that anticommute with $\gamma_0e_+$ (among them the dilation $e_+e_-$), or of the boosts $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, the translations $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$ and the special conformal generators $\gamma_\mu n_0$, generates all fifteen bivectors (computed); for an arbitrary element outside $\mathfrak{k}$ the same follows from the irreducibility of the eight-dimensional complement under $\mathfrak{k}$ (argued). Hence on an irreducible unitary module, such as the attachment's one-particle helicity modules of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} (irreducibility cited), a bounded weighting $f(\gamma_0e_+)$ of the modes by conformal energy that commutes with one boost commutes with the whole conformal algebra and is a multiple of the identity (Schur's lemma, cited): no weighting of the floors, sharp or smooth, keeps a boost.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} As a regulator the floors keep the global Ward identity (charge conservation and the free continuity equation) exactly at every floor. The central term that makes the one-chirality density algebra a boson algebra, and that fixes the chiral fermion's vacuum polarisation and the two-dimensional chiral anomaly, is not a scalar on any floor (by the trace argument of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower}); it is an edge operator that equals its continuum value on the filled sea for every momentum up to the cut-off, the density analogue of the quasi-spin $[b, b^{*}] = 1 - 2k/n$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}. The regulator breaks Lorentz invariance at every finite floor, keeping only the compact part of the conformal algebra, and by (v) no smoothing of the cut-off restores a boost. A sharp cut-off on conformal energy also leaves terms in the regulated zero-point energy that match no local invariant, which a cut-off vanishing with its slope at the edge removes (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}); clauses (i) to (iii) concern the sharp cut-off only.
synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.technical:
The tower's finite floors are the natural candidate for a regulator native to the series: on the twistor attachment they are energy cut-offs. Nothing specific to the tower enters clauses (i) to (iii): they hold for any finite truncation of a chiral band, and the truncated-band origin of the central term is standard (Mattis and Lieb). This result tests what such a sharp cut-off keeps, on the computed model of a one-chirality field on a circle with $2N$ momentum modes taken from $2N$ tower planes, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$ and densities $\rho(p) = \sum_k a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$.

The global Ward identity survives exactly: the charge commutes with $H$ and with every density, and $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$, the free continuity equation of a chiral current, holds on every floor. The central term of the density algebra does not survive as a scalar: $[\rho(p), \rho(-p)]$ is the number in the top $p$ modes minus the number in the bottom $p$ modes, an edge operator with zero scalar part, as the trace argument of the no-CCR theorem requires. On the filled sea it equals $\min(p, 2N - p)$, so the continuum value $p$ (the Schwinger commutator term, the boson normalisation of bosonisation, and the weight of the chiral fermion's one-loop density response, all at energy exactly $p$) is reproduced exactly for $p \le N$ and falls linearly above the cut-off. With an excitation at the window's edge the value changes, so the central term holds on states with vacuum-like edges, as the quasi-spin reaches the CCR only on states of bounded number.

Lorentz invariance is not kept: in $\Cl(2,4)$ the commutant of the conformal Hamiltonian $\gamma_0e_+$ is the seven-dimensional compact algebra, which contains the three spatial rotations and no boost, translation or special conformal generator. A conformal-energy cut therefore regulates in one conformal frame; the four-dimensional loop integrals of the standard theory with a Lorentz-invariant regulator are not what the floors give. Nor does smoothing help: the commutant together with any one boost generates the whole conformal algebra, so on an irreducible module a weighting of the modes by conformal energy that commutes with a boost commutes with everything and is a constant (Schur's lemma); no weighting of the floors, sharp or smooth, keeps a boost (merged on 2 November 2026 from the regulator-free vacuum polarisation, where it was first stated).
synthesis.floor-regulator-keeps-the-char.lay: A calculation in quantum field theory with loops needs a regulator, a way of cutting off the infinitely many high-energy modes. The series has a natural candidate: its tower is built floor by floor, each floor holding finitely many fermion modes, and on the series' link to spacetime the floors are energy cut-offs. This result tests that candidate, and with it any sharp cut-off on the number of modes, on a simple model, one chirality of a fermion moving around a circle. The floor keeps electric charge exactly and keeps the charge flowing correctly. The subtle quantum term that gives the vacuum its polarisability, and that underlies the anomaly of chiral fermions, cannot exist exactly on any finite floor; instead it appears at the floor's edges, and it takes exactly the right value for every wavelength longer than the cut-off, provided the modes near the cut-off are in their vacuum state. The price is relativity: a floor is defined by one notion of energy and is unchanged by rotations but not by boosts. Smoothing the cut-off does not help: no gradual weighting of the floors by energy restores the boosts.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting.} By Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit} the planes of a floor give mode operators with $\{a_j, a_k^{*}\} = \delta_{jk}$, $a_j^2 = 0$; distinct planes anticommute in the algebra, so no ordering signs need inserting. Label the $2N$ planes of a floor by $k = -N, \dots, N - 1$ and read $k$ as the momentum of a right-moving mode of one chirality on a circle (in units of $2\pi/L$); this labelling is the model, not a premise. Write $n_k = a_k^{*}a_k$, $H = \sum_k k\,n_k$, $\mathcal{N} = \sum_k n_k$ and $\rho(p) = \sum_k a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ over the $k$ with $k$ and $k + p$ in the window, so $\rho(p)^{*} = \rho(-p)$ and $\rho(\pm 2N) = 0$ (no pair of window indices differs by $2N$).

\emph{(i).} From the CAR, $[n_j, a_{l}^{*}a_k] = (\delta_{jl} - \delta_{jk})\,a_l^{*}a_k$. Hence $[H, a_{k+p}^{*}a_k] = ((k + p) - k)\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_k = p\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_k$ and $[\mathcal{N}, a_{k+p}^{*}a_k] = 0$ term by term, so $[H, \rho(p)] = p\,\rho(p)$ and $[\mathcal{N}, \rho(p)] = 0$ with no boundary correction, and $[\mathcal{N}, H] = 0$ since both are sums of commuting numbers. For $1 \le |p| \le 2N - 1$ the sum defining $\rho(p)$ is not empty, so $\rho(p) \ne 0$. The check confirms these identities as algebra elements for $N = 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(ii).} Using $[a_{k+p}^{*}a_k, a_{l-p}^{*}a_l] = \delta_{k,l-p}\,a_{k+p}^{*}a_l - \delta_{l,k+p}\,a_{l-p}^{*}a_k$ and summing over window indices, the terms with $l = k + p$ give $\sum_k (n_{k+p} - n_k)$ over the $k$ for which both $k$ and $k + p$ lie in the window, that is $k \in \{-N, \dots, N - 1 - p\}$ for $1 \le p \le 2N$. Shifting the first sum, this is $\sum_{k = -N + p}^{N - 1} n_k - \sum_{k = -N}^{N - 1 - p} n_k$, and the common terms cancel, leaving $\sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k - \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k$ (for $p > N$ the two ranges overlap and the same cancellation holds, leaving the same expression). Each $n_k$ has scalar part $\tfrac12$ in the floor's algebra and the two sums have $p$ terms each, so the scalar part is zero; this is the trace argument of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower}, which forbids any commutator on a floor from having a nonzero scalar part. The check confirms the identity and the vanishing scalar part for $N = 1, 2, 3$ and every $p \le 2N$.

\emph{(iii).} On $\Omega$ the modes $k < 0$ are filled and $k \ge 0$ empty. A term $a_{k-p}^{*}a_k$ of $\rho(-p)$ ($p \ge 1$) needs $k$ filled and $k - p$ empty, impossible when $k < 0$, so $\rho(-p)\Omega = 0$. By (ii), $[\rho(-p), \rho(p)] = \sum_{k < -N + p} n_k - \sum_{k \ge N - p} n_k$ acts on $\Omega$ as the number of filled modes among the bottom $p$ minus the number among the top $p$: for $p \le N$ these are $p$ and $0$; for $N < p \le 2N$ they are $N$ and $p - N$. In both cases the value is $\min(p, 2N - p)$. By (i), $\rho(p)\Omega$ is an eigenvector of $H$ with eigenvalue $E_\Omega + p$, and $\rho(-p)\rho(p)\Omega = [\rho(-p), \rho(p)]\Omega = \min(p, 2N - p)\,\Omega$, which is the squared norm of $\rho(p)\Omega$ for the floor's inner product. So the spectral measure of $\rho(p)$ in $\Omega$ is a single point at energy $p$ of weight $\min(p, 2N - p)$; the one-loop density response of the free field (the particle-hole bubble, exact for a free field) is determined by it. In the continuum (the CAR limit, with the sea filled below every momentum) the same computation gives weight $p$ for every $p$, the central term of the density algebra (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-schwinger-term-and-mattis-lieb-density-algebra}: Schwinger's commutator term, and the boson algebra of Tomonaga and of Mattis and Lieb). Hence the floor reproduces the continuum exactly for $p \le N$, and $b_p = \rho(-p)/\sqrt{p}$ obeys $[b_p, b_p^{*}] = 1$ on $\Omega$ there. With the top mode also occupied, (ii) at $p = 1$ gives $n_{N-1} - n_{-N} = 1 - 1 = 0$, so the value is not a property of the algebra alone but of the state at the edges; the check confirms all of (iii) for $N = 1, 2, 3$.

\emph{(iv).} Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} states that on the attachment the tower's floors are energy cut-offs, the energy being the conformal energy of the palatial storey. In $\Cl(2,4)$ with $Q(e_+) = 1$, $Q(e_-) = -1$, $n_\infty = e_+ + e_-$ and $n_0 = e_+ - e_-$ (null; any normalisation), $P_0 + K_0 = \gamma_0(n_\infty + n_0) = 2\gamma_0e_+$, and $(\gamma_0e_+)^2 = -1$, so $\gamma_0e_+$ generates the compact one-parameter group whose generator is the conformal Hamiltonian. The check computes the kernel of $B \mapsto [\gamma_0e_+, B]$ on the fifteen bivectors exactly: it is seven-dimensional (the compact $\mathfrak{so}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{so}(4)$: $\gamma_0e_+$, the three $\gamma_i\gamma_j$, the three $\gamma_ie_-$), its intersection with the Lorentz bivectors $\gamma_\mu\gamma_\nu$ is the span of the three rotations, and it has zero intersection with the span of the boosts $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, of the translations $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$ and of the special conformal generators $\gamma_\mu n_0$. A generator commuting with the conformal Hamiltonian preserves each of its eigenspaces, so the spatial rotations preserve every floor. Invariance of a single spectral subspace is weaker than commutation, so the converse needs one more step. The boosts, translations and special conformal generators lie in the eight-dimensional complement of the commutant (the noncompact part of $\mathfrak{so}(2,4)$); in the positive-energy modules their complex combinations raise or lower the conformal energy by one, as in the oscillator model of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}, and a nontrivial unitary representation of a noncompact simple group has no nonzero finite-dimensional invariant subspace (standard). A floor is the span of the finitely many lowest energies of a module whose energies are bounded below, so a nonzero noncompact generator, whose raising part moves the top energy of the floor out of it, does not preserve the floor. Hence a floor is invariant under the spatial rotations and under no boost.

\emph{(v).} This clause was first stated as clause (vii) of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}; it is merged here with its proof. Every basis bivector of $\Cl(2,4)$ either commutes or anticommutes with $H = \gamma_0e_+$ (a product of basis vectors); the commuting ones span the seven-dimensional $\mathfrak{k}$ of (iv), the anticommuting ones an eight-dimensional complement $\mathfrak{p}$, and $\mathfrak{k}$ is closed under the commutator (it is a centraliser). The check computes the Lie closure of $\mathfrak{k}$ together with each of the eight anticommuting basis bivectors ($\gamma_0\gamma_j$, $\gamma_0e_-$, $\gamma_je_+$, $e_+e_-$) and each of the eleven generators $\gamma_0\gamma_j$, $\gamma_\mu n_\infty$, $\gamma_\mu n_0$ exactly, by ranks of rational vectors: each time it is all fifteen bivectors. For an arbitrary $X \notin \mathfrak{k}$, write $X = X_{\mathfrak{k}} + X_{\mathfrak{p}}$ with $X_{\mathfrak{p}} \neq 0$; the closure contains $X_{\mathfrak{p}}$ and the $\mathfrak{k}$-module it generates, which is all of $\mathfrak{p}$ when $\mathfrak{p}$, the module $\R^{2}\otimes\R^{4}$ of $\mathfrak{so}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(4)$, is irreducible, and then $[\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{p}]$ supplies the rest (argued). Let $f$ be a bounded function and $f(H)$ the weighting of the modes of an irreducible unitary module by conformal energy. Every generator in $\mathfrak{k}$ commutes with $H$, hence with $f(H)$; if $f(H)$ also commutes with one boost, it commutes with the Lie algebra they generate, the whole conformal algebra, so by Schur's lemma (cited from memory) it is a multiple of the identity on that module and regulates nothing. The attachment's one-particle modules are irreducible under the conformal algebra (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}; irreducibility cited from memory), so no weighting of the floors, sharp as in (iv) or smooth, keeps a boost.

\emph{The reading.} Nothing in (i) to (iii) uses more than a finite truncation of a chiral band, so they hold for any sharp mode cut-off; the truncated-band origin of the central term is standard (Mattis and Lieb; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-schwinger-term-and-mattis-lieb-density-algebra}(ii)). A sharp cut-off on conformal energy also leaves non-local terms in the regulated zero-point energy, which a smooth cut-off vanishing with its slope at the edge removes (\claimref{synthesis.attachment-modules-give-sakharov-weights-cancelling-at-three-separate-generations}). The first two parts concern the global charge, which a floor keeps exactly; the local Ward identity of a gauge-invariant regulator requires the central term to be the scalar $p$, which (ii) excludes on any floor and (iii) restores on the filled sea for momenta up to the cut-off. In two dimensions the chiral anomaly and the photon mass of the Schwinger model are fixed by that central term through bosonisation (standard, cited from memory); the floors therefore reproduce them for the modes below the cut-off and not above. The four-dimensional analogue (conformal-energy modules of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} in place of momenta on a circle) is argued, not computed: the trace argument again excludes a scalar central term on a floor, and (iv) shows that the regulator is not Lorentz-invariant. The comparison with the quasi-spin of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}, where $[b, b^{*}] = 1 - 2k/n$ reaches the CCR only on states of bounded number, is a parallel, not a step of the proof.
