synthesis.interacting-fields-of-causal-p.formal:
Units and signature of the store; $\Cl(1,3)$ with $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$. The attached free fields are the Dirac spinor values $\psi$ of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}, on which a Lorentz rotor $R$ acts by $\psi \mapsto R\psi$; the gauge potentials and their gradients, vector values with $x \mapsto Rx\tilde R$; palatial scalars, any number of doublets; and the Faddeev-Popov ghosts $c$, $\bar c$, scalar CAR modes on tower planes (\claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}). Their statistics are those of \claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}: anticommuting spinors, commuting scalars and field strengths, anticommuting ghosts in the indefinite form; for the potential itself in Feynman gauge, which that result does not cover, we assume the Gupta-Bleuler (indefinite) form, clause (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, in which its polarisation sum is $-a\cdot b$, of degree $0$ in $k$, and it is local as a commuting field (computed in (i)). Let the interaction density $\mathcal{L}$ be a sum of the monomials (i) below, and let the interacting field of a Wick polynomial $A$ be Bogoliubov's $A_{\mathrm{int}}(x) = \frac{\delta}{I_{4}\,\delta h(x)}S(\mathcal{L})^{-1}S(\mathcal{L} + hA)\big|_{h = 0}$ (the complex unit of the free fields' Fock space is the field theory's unit $I_{4}$, numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), a formal power series, with time-ordered products that are graded symmetric and preserve the Grassmann parity, factorise causally, satisfy the Wick expansion (the free-field condition (N3) of \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}), and, as an assumption, are covariant under a representation $U$ of the covering group of the Poincar\'e group (\cite{DutschFredenhagen1999} state covariance, (N1), for the Poincar\'e group itself; Epstein and Glaser \cite{EpsteinGlaser1973}, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products}; \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}, (2.2), (2.3), (2.7)). Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The interaction density; computed.)} The rotor of the loop of four quarter turns in the plane $\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$ is $-1$: it fixes every vector and bivector value and negates every spinor value. The vector vertex $\langle\psi\gamma_{0}\tilde\psi A\rangle_{0}$, the axial vertex $\langle\psi\gamma_{3}\tilde\psi A\rangle_{0}$, the scalar and pseudoscalar Yukawa terms and mass insertions $\langle\psi\tilde\psi\rangle_{0}\phi$, $\langle\psi\tilde\psi I_{4}\rangle_{0}\phi$, the scalar gauge couplings, the quartic, the non-abelian cubic and quartic terms, the gauge fixing $\langle\nabla A\rangle_{0}^{2}$ and the ghost terms $\langle\nabla\bar c\,\nabla c\rangle_{0}$, $\langle\nabla\bar c\,A\rangle_{0}c$ are Lorentz scalars, each with an even number of spinor factors (so $U(2\pi)$ acts on $\mathcal{L}$ as $+1$) and with as many ghost as antighost factors; nothing depends on the number of scalar doublets. The free Feynman-gauge potential has the polarisation sum $-a\cdot b$, independent of $k$ and indefinite, and the bracket factor of the stored locality result vanishes for it as a commuting field.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Wick monomials; proved.)} On a Wick monomial with $n_{\psi}$ spinor and $n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$ ghost factors, $U(2\pi)$ acts as $(-1)^{n_{\psi}}$ and the Grassmann parity is $(-1)^{n_{\psi} + n_{c} + n_{\bar c}}$; they agree if and only if $n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$ is even, in particular at ghost number zero, and two such monomials on disjoint modes anticommute exactly when both have $U(2\pi) = -1$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Interacting fields; proved given the imported axioms.)} Every order of $A_{\mathrm{int}}$ is a retarded product of copies of $\mathcal{L}$ with $A$; by parity preservation it has the Grassmann parity of $A$, and by covariance under the covering group its $2\pi$ eigenvalue is that of $A$; the interacting fields are graded-local with that parity (\cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}, Proposition 2, (2.25), for QED, where the ghosts do not couple; for a coupled ghost vertex, Yang-Mills, \cite{Hollands2008}, cited from memory), the first order following from the graded Jacobi identity for even $\mathcal{L}$ and the light-cone lemma of the proof. Hence, if the time-ordered products satisfy these conditions, then on every interacting field with an even number of ghost factors, in particular the interacting field of every Wick polynomial of ghost number zero, the statistics operator equals $U(2\pi)$ to every order: the spin-statistics connection holds in perturbation theory with no Jost-point or modular premise. Ghost fields of odd ghost count have the opposite sign, the Krein exception of the free-field result.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(What remains; argued.)} The statement concerns formal power series. Beyond perturbation theory a premise remains (the Jost point of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-standard-field-theory}, or a modular premise, \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}); for electrically charged fields the nonperturbative charge classes are localised in hypercones \cite{BuchholzRoberts2014}, where a spin-statistics theorem is not supplied by the sources read.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.interacting-fields-of-causal-p.technical:
The question is whether the spin-statistics connection of interacting fields needs the Jost-point theorem. In perturbation theory it does not. Interacting fields are built from the free fields by Bogoliubov's formula, each order a retarded product of the Wick polynomial with copies of the interaction density, and causal perturbation theory proves that interacting fields are graded-local with the free grading and covariant whenever the time-ordered products are (standard: Epstein-Glaser; Dütsch-Fredenhagen for QED with spinors and ghosts; Hollands for Yang-Mills). The conditions used are graded symmetry and parity preservation, causal factorisation, the Wick expansion and covariance under the covering group, the last assumed (the standard axiom is stated for the Poincar\'e group); the free potential in Feynman gauge is taken in its indefinite form, where it is local. The series' part is the bookkeeping on its own field list, done exactly in the spacetime algebra: the rotation by $2\pi$ is the rotor $-1$, which negates spinor values and fixes vector, bivector and scalar values; every monomial of the series' interaction (vector and axial vertices, Yukawa and mass insertions with any number of doublets, scalar and non-abelian gauge couplings, gauge fixing, ghost terms) is a Lorentz scalar with an even number of spinors and as many ghosts as antighosts. So an interacting field keeps both the Grassmann parity and the $2\pi$ eigenvalue of its Wick polynomial, and the two agree exactly when the number of ghost factors is even, in particular at ghost number zero. The first-order locality step reduces, by the graded Jacobi identity for an even interaction and a light-cone lemma, to free graded locality, checked exactly on the tower's CAR modes.

So the Jost import is needed only beyond perturbation theory, where a premise remains (the Jost point or a modular premise, \claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}); electrically charged fields add an infrared obstacle there.
synthesis.interacting-fields-of-causal-p.lay: Particles of half-integer spin obey the exclusion rule and those of whole-number spin do not. For the series' free particles this tie was already derived; the question was whether it survives interactions. In the standard step-by-step construction of interacting fields, it does: each step combines the free fields with the interaction, and every term of the series' interaction contains matter fields in pairs, so turning a field by a full circle and exchanging two fields give the same sign before and after the interaction is switched on. The bookkeeping fields used to fix gauges are the one exception, as they were for free fields, and they always appear in pairs in anything physical. What the step-by-step construction does not give is a statement about the full theory beyond that expansion; there a deeper assumption is still needed.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting and imports.} Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$ and $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$. A rotor $R$ ($R\tilde R = 1$, even) acts on the series' Dirac values by $\psi \mapsto R\psi$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}), on vector values (potentials, gradients) and bivector values by $x \mapsto Rx\tilde R$, and trivially on scalar values (the components of any number of scalar doublets and the ghosts of \claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}). The covering group of the Lorentz group is the rotor group; its element $-1$ is the end point of the lift of a closed loop of rotations. The free fields have the statistics of \claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}: with positive norm the spinor is a CAR field and the scalars and the field strength CCR fields; the ghosts are local CAR scalars, which needs the indefinite form. The potential itself in Feynman gauge is not covered by that result; it enters as a condition (Step 2). From outside the store the proof uses only the axioms and results of causal perturbation theory (standard): time-ordered products $T$ that are multilinear, graded symmetric in their arguments and preserve the Grassmann parity (the renormalisation freedom is spanned by local terms of the parity of the product), satisfy the Wick expansion in the free fields ((N3) of \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}), factorise causally ($T(A_{1}(x_{1})\cdots A_{n}(x_{n})) = T(A_{1}\cdots A_{k})T(A_{k+1}\cdots A_{n})$ when no $x_{j}$, $j > k$, lies in the closed causal future of an $x_{i}$, $i \le k$) and are covariant, $\mathrm{Ad}\,U(L)\,T(A_{1}(x_{1})\cdots) = T(\mathrm{Ad}\,U(L)A_{1}(x_{1})\cdots)$ \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999} ((2.2), (2.3)); there (N1) is stated for the proper orthochronous Poincar\'e group, and covariance under its covering group, with $U$ acting on spinor fields through the rotor group, is an assumption of the present result (standard for spinor fields, cited from memory); their existence \cite{EpsteinGlaser1973} (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-epstein-glaser-extension-theorem-and-ward-preserving-time-ordered-products}(i)); Bogoliubov's interacting fields \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999} ((2.7)); and graded locality of interacting fields to all orders \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999} (Proposition 2 and (2.25), read: the bracket is an anticommutator only when both fields have an odd number of spinor fields or both an odd number of ghost fields, in a convention where free spinors commute with free ghosts; in their QED the ghosts do not couple); with a coupled ghost vertex (Yang-Mills) \cite{Hollands2008} (cited from memory, the relevant sections not read).

\emph{Step 1: the rotation by $2\pi$ (clause (i), first sentence).} Let $B = \gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}$, $B^{2} = -1$. The versor $q = 1 + B$ has $q\tilde q = 2$ and $q x \tilde q/2$ is the quarter turn in the plane $B$; $q^{2} = 2B$, so $q^{2}/2 = B$ is the half turn ($B\gamma_{1}\tilde B = -\gamma_{1}$, checked), and $q^{4} = (2B)^{2} = -4$. The four quarter turns compose the closed loop of rotations by $\pi/2, \pi, 3\pi/2, 2\pi$; its lift to rotors, normalised by $(q\tilde q)^{2} = 4$, ends at $q^{4}/4 = -1$. The script computes $q^{4}$, its norm and the action of $U = -1$: $Ux\tilde U = x$ on five vectors and two bivectors, $U\psi = -\psi$ on three even multivectors. So $U(2\pi)$ multiplies a monomial by $(-1)^{n_{\psi}}$, $n_{\psi}$ its number of spinor factors (the conjugate $\tilde\psi$ counts as a spinor factor, $\tilde\psi \mapsto \tilde\psi\tilde R$).

\emph{Step 2: the interaction density (clause (i)).} The monomials are those of the stored results: the vector vertex $\langle J A\rangle_{0}$, $J = \psi\gamma_{0}\tilde\psi$, of the one-loop QED result (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}, the matrix reading $\bar\psi\gamma^{\mu}\psi A_{\mu}$); the axial vertex $\langle K A\rangle_{0}$, $K = \psi\gamma_{3}\tilde\psi$ (with the vector vertex it gives the chiral couplings of the weak factor); the Yukawa terms of the doublets and their mass insertions $\langle\psi\tilde\psi\rangle_{0}\phi$, $\langle\psi\tilde\psi I_{4}\rangle_{0}\phi$; the scalar gauge couplings $\langle A\nabla\rangle_{0}\phi\phi$ and $\langle AA\rangle_{0}\phi\phi$ and the quartic $\phi^{4}$; the non-abelian cubic $\langle(\nabla \wedge A)(A \wedge A)\rangle_{0}$ and quartic $\langle(A \wedge A)(A \wedge A)\rangle_{0}$ with structure constants as scalar coefficients; the gauge fixing $\langle\nabla A\rangle_{0}^{2}$; and the ghost terms $\langle\nabla\bar c\,\nabla c\rangle_{0}$ and $\langle\nabla\bar c\,A\rangle_{0}c$ of the BRST result. The scalar content enters only through Lorentz scalars of scalar values, so the number of doublets plays no role. Each is a scalar part of a product of rotor-covariant values, hence invariant under every rotor: $\psi\gamma_{\mu}\tilde\psi \mapsto R\psi\gamma_{\mu}\tilde\psi\tilde R$, $\psi\tilde\psi \mapsto R\psi\tilde\psi\tilde R = \psi\tilde\psi$ (its scalar and $I_{4}$ parts are invariant), and $\langle R X\tilde R\rangle_{0} = \langle X\rangle_{0}$. The script evaluates every monomial on three spinors and sample vectors and scalars, before and after four exact rotors (a rotation $(3 + 4\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2})/5$, a boost $(5 + 4\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1})/3$, a rotation $(5 + 12\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3})/13$ and their product), and under $U = -1$, where the value is $(-1)^{n_{\psi}}$ times the original and nonzero; it also checks that a one-spinor scalar such as $\langle\psi\gamma_{0}A\rangle_{0}$ changes sign under $U$, so the test is not vacuous. The counts are not labelled by hand: the script computes $n_{\psi}$, $n_{c}$, $n_{\bar c}$ as the homogeneity degrees of each monomial under $\psi \mapsto 2\psi$, $c \mapsto 3c$, $\bar c \mapsto 5\bar c$, and finds $n_{\psi} \in \{0, 2\}$, $n_{c} = n_{\bar c}$; the control scalar has degree $1$. The free potential in Feynman gauge: by the Gupta-Bleuler form of the BRST result, $[a_{\mu}, a_{\nu}^{\dagger}] = -g_{\mu\nu}$, so its polarisation sum on test vectors is $\sum_{\mu}(-g_{\mu\mu})(a\cdot\gamma_{\mu})(\gamma_{\mu}\cdot b) = -a\cdot b$ (checked on five vectors), independent of $k$, of degree $d = 0$, and indefinite (negative on a timelike test vector). With the bracket factor $1 + \eta c(-1)^{d}$ of the stored locality result and $c = 1$ (the antiparticle sum equals the particle sum for a Hermitian field), the factor vanishes for $\eta = -1$: the potential is a local commuting field in the indefinite form, the standard Gupta-Bleuler statement (the stored result treats only the field strength at positive norm, so this is a condition of the present result, clause (K1) of Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, with the degree computed).

\emph{Step 3: Wick monomials (clause (ii)).} The Grassmann parity of a Wick monomial is the parity of its number of anticommuting factors, $n_{\psi} + n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$, by the free statistics; $U(2\pi)$ acts as $(-1)^{n_{\psi}}$ by Step 1. They agree if and only if $n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$ is even; at ghost number $n_{c} - n_{\bar c} = 0$ the sum $2n_{c}$ is even. The script models the anticommuting factors as tower modes $v_{j} = \tfrac12(e_{j} + f_{j})$ on distinct tower planes of $\Cl(m, m)$ ($e_{j}^{2} = 1$, $f_{j}^{2} = -1$; $v_{j}^{2} = 0$, $\{v_{j}, v_{k}\} = 0$, the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), reads the Grassmann parity from the grade involution there, and computes the $2\pi$ eigenvalue separately in $\Cl(1,3)$ as the sign by which $U$ applied to each factor changes the product $\psi_{1}\gamma_{0}\psi_{2}\gamma_{0}\cdots\psi_{n_{\psi}}$ of sample spinors (nonzero); over $n_{\psi} \le 3$, $n_{c}, n_{\bar c} \le 2$ the two disagree on exactly the $16$ monomials with $n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$ odd. For ghost-even monomials on disjoint modes the script checks that they anticommute exactly when both have $U(2\pi) = -1$ and commute otherwise. In the convention of \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}, where spinors commute with ghosts, the bracket sign is $(-1)^{n_{\psi}(A)n_{\psi}(B) + n_{gh}(A)n_{gh}(B)}$; for fields of even ghost count it is $(-1)^{n_{\psi}(A)n_{\psi}(B)}$ in both conventions.

\emph{Step 4: interacting fields keep parity and spin (clause (iii), first part).} The $n$-th order of $A_{\mathrm{int}}(x)$ is $\tfrac{I_{4}^{n}}{n!}\int R(\mathcal{L}(y_{1})\cdots\mathcal{L}(y_{n}); A(x))\,g(y_{1})\cdots g(y_{n})$, a retarded product, a finite combination of time-ordered and anti-time-ordered products of the same factors. By the causal Wick expansion its terms are Wick monomials obtained from the product $\mathcal{L}^{n}A$ by contracting pairs of a field with its conjugate (a $\psi$ with a $\tilde\psi$, a $c$ with a $\bar c$, two bosons), which changes $n_{\psi}$ and $n_{c} + n_{\bar c}$ by even numbers; local renormalisation terms have the Grassmann parity of the product by the parity condition. Since each copy of $\mathcal{L}$ is even (Step 2), every term has the Grassmann parity of $A$. (No conservation of ghost number by the time-ordered products is needed: the result uses only the Grassmann parity and the $2\pi$ eigenvalue, whose ratio is the ghost parity.) By covariance, $\mathrm{Ad}\,U(2\pi)$ acts on the retarded product as on the product of its arguments, that is by $(+1)^{n}(-1)^{n_{\psi}(A)}$. So $A_{\mathrm{int}}$ has the Grassmann parity and the $U(2\pi)$ eigenvalue of $A$, and by Step 3 they agree when $A$ has an even ghost count, in particular when $A$ has ghost number zero. The script checks in the tower model that for an even element $\mathcal{L}$ (spinor and ghost bilinears) the graded commutator $[\mathcal{L}, A]$ has the grade and the spinor-mode sign of $A$, and that $\mathcal{L}$ is fixed by the spinor-mode sign flip.

\emph{Step 5: graded locality (clause (iii), second part).} To all orders this is \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999} (2.25) for QED and \cite{Hollands2008} (cited from memory) with coupled ghosts. At first order it follows from the free statistics, and we give the step since it shows where evenness of $\mathcal{L}$ enters. Write $[X, Y\} = XY - (-1)^{|X||Y|}YX$ for homogeneous $X$, $Y$. With the first-order retarded product $R(\mathcal{L}(y); A(x)) = \theta(x^{0} - y^{0})[A(x), \mathcal{L}(y)]$ (up to a constant), for $x$ and $z$ spacelike separated the first-order part of $[A_{\mathrm{int}}(x), B_{\mathrm{int}}(z)\}$ is a multiple of $\int g(y)\bigl(\theta(x^{0} - y^{0})[[A(x), \mathcal{L}(y)], B(z)\} + \theta(z^{0} - y^{0})[A(x), [B(z), \mathcal{L}(y)]\}\bigr)dy$. For $\mathcal{L}$ even, $\mathrm{ad}_{\mathcal{L}}$ is an even derivation of the graded commutator: $[\mathcal{L}, [A, B\}] = [[\mathcal{L}, A], B\} + [A, [\mathcal{L}, B]\}$ (graded Jacobi; checked for all pairs of five homogeneous elements in $\Cl(6, 6)$; with an odd $\mathcal{L}$ the identity needs the sign $(-1)^{|\mathcal{L}||A|}$ on the second term and the even form fails, both checked). Where both step functions are $1$ the integrand is $-[\mathcal{L}(y), [A(x), B(z)\}] = 0$, since free fields at spacelike separation graded-commute. Where only the first is $1$, $y^{0} > z^{0}$ and $[A(x), \mathcal{L}(y)] \neq 0$ only for $y$ in the causal past $J^{-}(x)$; then $y$ is spacelike to $z$ (the light-cone lemma: $y \in J^{+}(z)$ would give $x \in J^{+}(z)$, and $y \in J^{-}(z)$ contradicts $y^{0} > z^{0}$; the script confirms it on a rational grid of trial points for three spacelike pairs, and finds grid points in $J^{-}(x) \cap J^{-}(z)$ with $y^{0} \le z^{0}$, so the hypothesis $y^{0} > z^{0}$ is needed), so $B(z)$ graded-commutes with $A(x)$ and with $\mathcal{L}(y)$ and hence, by the Jacobi identity, with $[A(x), \mathcal{L}(y)]$. The last case is symmetric. So the first-order bracket vanishes. Together with Step 4, on interacting fields of even ghost count the statistics grading is $U(2\pi)$ to every order; a ghost field of odd ghost count has grading $-U(2\pi)$, the Krein case of the free-field result.

\emph{Step 6: scope (clause (iv)).} The statement is about formal power series in the coupling; the interacting local algebras exist without the adiabatic limit \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}, but convergence and a nonperturbative vacuum are not addressed. The free-field input is the store's result for massless fields; the series' masses come from Yukawa couplings to the rung field and its vacuum value, which are even two-spinor insertions covered by Step 2, so the expansion can be posed around massless free fields (massive free Dirac locality is standard, cited from memory). Gauge anomalies and the positivity of the physical quotient (\cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}, Theorem 4) are not used: statistics and covariance do not depend on the Ward identities. Beyond perturbation theory the spin-statistics connection rests on a premise: the Jost-point theorem of Wightman's framework (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-standard-field-theory}) or a modular premise (\claimref{synthesis.wedge-reflections-compose-to-the-two-pi-rotor-so-geometric-modular-conjugations-give-interacting-spin-statistics}). For electrically charged fields the nonperturbative charge classes are localised in hypercones and are of Bose or Fermi type with a covariant positive-energy representation \cite{BuchholzRoberts2014} (abstract and introduction read); a spin-statistics theorem for them was not found there. Transport-absent: the inheritance is standard causal perturbation theory; the series supplies the field list, the spacetime-algebra form of its monomials and the tower ghosts.

synthesis.kasner-field-is-weyl-flat-only.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose derived metric is the four-dimensional diagonal Kasner field $g_{p} = -dt^{2} + t^{2p_{1}}dx^{2} + t^{2p_{2}}dy^{2} + t^{2p_{3}}dz^{2}$, $t > 0$, with $p_{1} + p_{2} + p_{3} = 1$ (the Kasner plane of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching} with three exponents; no field equation imposed, and under Einstein's equations the source is stiff, $P = \rho$). Put $S = \sum p_{i}^{2}$, $E_{1} = p_{1}^{2} - 2p_{1}p_{2} - p_{1} - 2p_{2}^{2} + 2p_{2}$, $E_{2} = 2p_{1}^{2} + 2p_{1}p_{2} - 2p_{1} - p_{2}^{2} + p_{2}$, and let $e_{0}, e_{1}, e_{2}, e_{3}$ be the orthonormal frame of $g_{p}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(The Weyl map; proved.)} The Weyl map on bivectors has the frame bivectors $e_{0}\wedge e_{i}$ and their duals $I_{4}\,e_{0}\wedge e_{i}$ as eigenvectors, with the same eigenvalue $\lambda_{i}$ on both, the mixed component $C_{0i}{}^{0i} = C_{jk}{}^{jk}$ ($\{i, j, k\} = \{1, 2, 3\}$): $\lambda_{i} = (p_{i}^{2} - p_{i} + \tfrac{1 - S}{3})\,t^{-2}$, so $\lambda_{1} = E_{1}/(3t^{2})$, $\lambda_{2} = -E_{2}/(3t^{2})$, $\lambda_{1} + \lambda_{2} + \lambda_{3} = 0$. So the Weyl curvature vanishes exactly where $E_{1} = E_{2} = 0$, and elsewhere it is nonzero at every $t > 0$ and grows as $t^{-2}$ toward the wall.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(The Weyl-flat points; proved.)} On the plane $E_{1} = E_{2} = 0$ holds exactly at the Milne points $(1, 0, 0)$, $(0, 1, 0)$, $(0, 0, 1)$, where $g_{p}$ is flat, and at the isotropic point $(\tfrac13, \tfrac13, \tfrac13)$, where $Rt^{2} = -\tfrac23$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(No attached state at the wall; proved, a corollary.)} At every other point of the plane the Weyl curvature is nonzero on all of $t > 0$, so by Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes} the tractor transport of the attachment supplies no state on any neighbourhood of the wall: on a four-dimensional Kasner approach as in Premise \claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-contracting-kasner-stage-premise} (P1), the state carried into the descended phase is not the attachment's, and must be supplied by the rule of Premise \claimref{synthesis.pre-descent-state-carried-into-descended-phase-premise} (P2).
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Not tame walls in cosmic time; proved.)} In the smooth structure of the cosmic coordinate $t$ neither Weyl-flat case is a tame corank-one wall (in the sense of the wall Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}): at the isotropic point $g_{p} = t^{2/3}$ times a flat bracket whose cometric degenerates at order $\tfrac23$, and at a Milne point the metric itself degenerates at order two while the cometric has a pole. In its conformal time $\eta = \tfrac32 t^{2/3}$, and $t' = \eta^{2}/4$, the isotropic bracket is the radical-normal wall $-t'^{-1}dt'^{2} + \delta$, as for every decelerating power law (\claimref{synthesis.radical-normal-tame-wall-is-a-regular-initial-surface-whose-smoothness-selects-no-state}), (iv)).
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.kasner-field-is-weyl-flat-only.technical: If the descent ends a contracting four-dimensional Kasner approach, the state that reaches the descended phase is set on a field whose Weyl curvature this result computes exactly. Over the whole plane of Kasner exponents with sum one (under Einstein's equations, the stiff-source family) the Weyl curvature is the inverse square of the time times two quadratic forms in the exponents, and the two forms vanish together at only four points: the three flat Milne points and the isotropic point. Since the attachment's transport supplies a state only where the Weyl curvature vanishes, at every other Kasner point it supplies none near the wall, and the state must come from the matching rule of the second Kasner premise. In cosmic time the two Weyl-flat cases are not tame walls of the series' degenerate geometry, so in that coordinate the regular wall case and the conformally flat Kasner case do not meet; in conformal time the isotropic point is the regular wall. Transport-absent.
synthesis.kasner-field-is-weyl-flat-only.lay: One proposal for the very early universe is a stage that shrinks unevenly in different directions before the descent. The series' way of building a quantum state from its geometry works only where a certain part of the curvature, the part that distorts shapes, is absent. For such uneven stages in four dimensions, this result computes that part and finds that it is absent only in four special cases; in all the others the series' construction gives no state near the descent, so another rule must supply it. Measured in the usual cosmic time, even the four special cases do not have the regular form the series' wall theory uses.
flags: four-dimensional diagonal Kasner fields only; the stored setting also allows hidden directions (the five-dimensional end (0, 0, 0, 1) of (P2)), Bianchi I fields with rotating axes and the BKL sequence, none of which is covered
the not-tame clause holds in the smooth structure of cosmic time; in conformal time the isotropic point is the radical-normal wall

proofs.main:
\emph{(i)} For a diagonal metric depending on $t$ only, the check computes the Christoffel symbols, the Riemann tensor $R^{\rho}{}_{\sigma\mu\nu} = \partial_{\mu}\Gamma^{\rho}_{\nu\sigma} - \partial_{\nu}\Gamma^{\rho}_{\mu\sigma} + \Gamma^{\rho}_{\mu\lambda}\Gamma^{\lambda}_{\nu\sigma} - \Gamma^{\rho}_{\nu\lambda}\Gamma^{\lambda}_{\mu\sigma}$, the Ricci tensor and $R$, and the Weyl components $C_{abab} = R_{abab} - \tfrac12(g_{aa}R_{bb} + g_{bb}R_{aa}) + \tfrac{R}{6}g_{aa}g_{bb}$ ($a \neq b$), divided by $g_{aa}g_{bb}$, which gives the mixed components $C_{ab}{}^{ab}$, all exactly as monomials $c\,t^{e}$ with rational $e$. By hand: with $\sum p = 1$ every spatial Ricci component vanishes, $R_{ii}/g_{ii} = p_{i}(\sum p - 1)/t^{2} = 0$, while $R_{00} = (1 - S)/t^{2}$ and $R = (S - 1)/t^{2}$. The orthonormal Riemann components are $R_{0i0i} = -p_{i}(p_{i} - 1)/t^{2}$, and the Weyl formula gives the mixed component $t^{2}C_{0i}{}^{0i} = p_{i}^{2} - p_{i} + \tfrac{1 - S}{3}$ (the orthonormal component $C_{0i0i}$ is its negative, since $g_{00} = -1$). With $p_{3} = 1 - p_{1} - p_{2}$ this is $E_{1}/3$ for $i = 1$ and $-E_{2}/3$ for $i = 2$. The engine agrees on nine rational points of the plane, for the general formula at each $i$ and for $E_{1}$, $E_{2}$, and confirms $C_{23}{}^{23} = C_{01}{}^{01}$, $C_{13}{}^{13} = C_{02}{}^{02}$, $C_{12}{}^{12} = C_{03}{}^{03}$ and the vanishing trace $\sum_{i}C_{0i}{}^{0i} = 0$, with every component a pure $t^{-2}$ term. For a diagonal field the Weyl curvature is purely electric: the Weyl map on bivectors, $W(B) = \tfrac14 C_{ab}{}^{cd}B^{ab}e_{c}\wedge e_{d}$ for $B = \tfrac12 B^{ab}e_{a}\wedge e_{b}$, is diagonal on the frame bivectors, with $W(e_{0}\wedge e_{i}) = C_{0i}{}^{0i}\,e_{0}\wedge e_{i}$ and the same eigenvalue on the dual bivector $e_{j}\wedge e_{k}$, which is $\pm I_{4}\,e_{0}\wedge e_{i}$. So the Weyl map vanishes exactly when every $\lambda_{i}$ vanishes, that is (by the trace) when $E_{1} = E_{2} = 0$; otherwise a nonzero eigenvalue is a constant times $t^{-2}$, nonzero on all of $t > 0$. The check also computes the Einstein tensor: $G_{00} = G_{ii}/g_{ii} = (1 - S)/(2t^{2})$ at every sample, so under Einstein's equations the source has $P = \rho$, with $\rho \ge 0$ exactly when $S \le 1$.

\emph{(ii)} By (i), $\lambda_{1} = \lambda_{2} = \lambda_{3} = 0$ exactly when $p_{i}^{2} - p_{i}$ takes the same value for all $i$, and a value $c$ of $p^{2} - p$ is taken at the two roots $r$ and $1 - r$. So each $p_{i} \in \{r, 1 - r\}$ for one $r$. If $n$ of the exponents equal $r$ and $3 - n$ equal $1 - r$, the sum condition is $nr + (3 - n)(1 - r) = 1$, that is $(2n - 3)r = n - 2$: $n = 3$ gives $r = \tfrac13$, the isotropic point; $n = 2$ gives $r = 0$, the exponents $(0, 0, 1)$; $n = 1$ gives $r = 1$, again $(1, 0, 0)$ up to order; $n = 0$ is $n = 3$ with $r$ and $1 - r$ exchanged. Hence the Weyl-flat points are exactly the three permutations of $(0, 0, 1)$ and $(\tfrac13, \tfrac13, \tfrac13)$; the check enumerates this. As an independent confirmation the check also eliminates $p_{2}$ from $E_{1} = E_{2} = 0$ over the rational functions of $p_{1}$: the Sylvester determinant is $-9p_{1}^{2}(p_{1} - 1)(3p_{1} - 1)$, and the fibres over $p_{1} = 0, 1, \tfrac13$ give exactly $(0, 0)$, $(0, 1)$, $(1, 0)$ and $(\tfrac13, \tfrac13)$ in $(p_{1}, p_{2})$. At the Milne points the engine returns vanishing Ricci and Weyl tensors: the field is flat. At the isotropic point it returns $R = -\tfrac23 t^{-2}$, the value stored for the isotropic disk point.

\emph{(iii)} Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-transport-is-flat-only-where-weyl-vanishes} gives that the conformal spinors of the attachment can be parallel for the tractor gauge field only where the Weyl curvature vanishes, and that off Weyl-flat regions the transport supplies no state. A purely electric Weyl map with real eigenvalues is of Petrov type I or D, so the type N case of that theorem does not arise. By (i) and (ii), off the four points the Weyl curvature is nonzero at every $t > 0$, in particular on every neighbourhood of the wall. The rest is the reading of (P1) and (P2): (P1) supplies the contracting Kasner stage that Theorem \claimref{synthesis.kasner-exit-needs-a-contracting-metric-stage-and-a-wall-matching} requires, and (P2) a rule carrying its state across; the rule's form is not fixed there, and by this clause it cannot be the attachment's transport.

\emph{(iv)} At $p_{i} = \tfrac13$ the check divides $g_{p}$ by $t^{2/3}$ and finds a flat bracket $-t^{-2/3}dt^{2} + \delta$ (vanishing Riemann tensor); its cometric entry $-t^{2/3}$ vanishes at order $\tfrac23$, not one, so in the smooth structure of $t$ condition (T3) of tameness fails (and the cometric is not smooth in $t$). With $\eta = \tfrac32 t^{2/3}$, $d\eta/dt = t^{-1/3}$ and the bracket is $-d\eta^{2} + \delta$; with $t' = \eta^{2}/4$, $dt'/d\eta = \eta/2$, so $-d\eta^{2} = -(4/\eta^{2})dt'^{2} = -t'^{-1}dt'^{2}$: the radical-normal tame wall in the coordinate $t'$. Tameness is therefore a property of the smooth structure; the general power-law statement, in cosmic and in conformal time, is clause (iv) of the result (\claimref{synthesis.radical-normal-tame-wall-is-a-regular-initial-surface-whose-smoothness-selects-no-state}). At the Milne point $(0, 0, 1)$ the engine finds the field flat; its metric entry $t^{2}$ vanishes at order two, so the metric degenerates and the cometric entry $t^{-2}$ has a pole: the opposite of a tame wall, at which the cometric degenerates at order one and the metric has a simple pole (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}).

\emph{Reading (argued, not part of the statement).} Under (P1) and (P2), with four-dimensional Kasner exponents, the deposit chain's first step cannot start from the attachment's conformal vacuum at a generic Kasner point; the reference state must come with the (P2) rule. At the isotropic point a conformal vacuum exists for conformally covariant fields, and in conformal time its wall is the regular radical-normal wall; in cosmic time it is not tame. At the Milne points the field is flat and the restriction of the Minkowski vacuum to the Milne wedge is available, but those walls are null cones of flat space, not degenerate cometrics. So in the cosmic-time smooth structure the two routes to a state at the descent that the series has, the attachment where the Weyl curvature vanishes and the regular radical-normal wall, do not meet on the four-dimensional Kasner plane. Kasner approaches with hidden directions, such as the five-dimensional end of (P2), are not covered. Transport-absent.

synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-.technical:
The store quantises the photon in Coulomb gauge on a positive polynomial representation, and its tower floors carry positive forms. Two standard tools of covariant quantum field theory need an indefinite metric instead: a self-adjoint nilpotent BRST charge, which vanishes on any positive space, and Pauli-Villars regulator fields, which enter loops with negative weights. This premise adopts one indefinite (Krein) inner product for both. On a polarisation quantum it is the Gupta-Bleuler form, the Minkowski metric of the polarisations, which is Lorentz invariant where the positive form singles out a frame; ghost pairs are tower modes with the floor's form twisted by the involution exchanging the pair; regulator fields of negative weight are negative-norm states of the same form. The physical space is the BRST cohomology at ghost number zero and is required to be positive: the unphysical polarisations and the ghosts appear only in zero-norm quartets (Kugo and Ojima), and regulators decouple at infinite mass. Strocchi's theorem says a local covariant vector potential obeying Maxwell's equations cannot live on a positive-metric space with nonzero field strength, so a covariant formulation needs some such form.

Results that rest on it say so: one-loop electrodynamics in the spacetime algebra in a covariant gauge with Pauli-Villars regulators, the one-loop running coefficients in the background Feynman gauge, the self-adjoint BRST charge with tower ghosts, and (from 2 November 2026) the two-loop vacuum polarisation, the free quartet positivity at every number of quanta, the charge renormalisation of electron-positron annihilation, the self-energy and vertex parts of the regulator-free one-loop extensions, the running of the rung-field quartics, the Krein quartet of induced gravity, the gauge parts of the slot-module coefficients and the interacting spin-statistics of causal perturbation theory. Note of 2 November 2026: the Pauli-Villars clause is not needed for the one-loop vacuum polarisation, which extends across the coincident point with no regulator (the clause is kept for the stored self-energy and vertex); the one-particle Gupta-Bleuler form is restated in the store as the trace form of Clifford conjugation, minus the metric, which restates and does not derive the premise; and given the polarisation and ghost clauses the free physical space is positive at every number of quanta. It is not derived from the series (the form is the same in any formalism), it supplies no native covariant regulator, and positivity of the physical space beyond the free charge is imported, not computed. It would be refuted by a negative-norm or stray null state in the physical space of the series' gauge fields (a failure of unitarity), by gauge-parameter or regulator dependence of physical amplitudes, or by a derivation that every state space of the series is positive.
synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-.lay: To describe light and the other force fields in a way that treats space and time alike, physicists use bookkeeping in which some unphysical states have negative or zero length, and remove them again before anything is measured. The same device is used to tame the infinities of quantum corrections, with auxiliary particles that count negatively. The series' quantum spaces all have positive lengths, so it cannot use this bookkeeping as it stands. This premise adopts it: the force fields of the series carry the standard indefinite measure built from the spacetime metric of their polarisations, and only states of positive length remain once the unphysical parts cancel in groups of four. Several results use it, among them the series' calculations of the first and second quantum corrections of electrodynamics, its calculation of how the force strengths change with energy, and its construction of the ghost bookkeeping. One of the two uses, the auxiliary negative particles, turns out not to be needed for the screening of charge by the vacuum, which can be computed without them. It is taken as given, not derived; it would be refuted if the physical states it leaves were found to include ones of negative length.

synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.formal:
In the setting of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}: the complexified rung summand $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ with $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$, $Q(c) = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$, $N = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} + |\beta|^{2})$, $m = \tfrac12(|\alpha|^{2} - |\beta|^{2})$, the slot mixing $U(2)$ with generators $T_{j}$ and $Y$, the rung boost $e^{tK}$, the D-term potential $V_{D}$ at level $\xi = 2\zeta$, the null-lift locus $L = \{Q = -H^{2}\}$, its cone $L_{0} = \{Q = 0\}$ (the limit $H \to 0$) and the physical family point $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$ of $L_{0}$, with $N^{*} = \tfrac12\lambda^{2}$, $M_{W}^{2} = \tfrac12 g^{2}N^{*}$, $M_{Z}^{2} = \tfrac12(g^{2} + g'^{2})N^{*}$, $v^{2} = 2N^{*}$. Take the field theory's unit to be $I_{4}$ (\claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}). The \emph{linear rung field} is the field with values in all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, eight real components, with a real $U(2)$-invariant polynomial potential; the \emph{constrained field} is its restriction to $L$ or $L_{0}$. Masses are eigenvalues of the Hessian divided by the kinetic coefficient of the stored Hermitian term. Write $r = \sqrt{k_{8}^{2} + k_{9}^{2}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{(The unit.)} In $\Cl(3,5)$, spacetime with the two rung planes, $I_{4}^{2} = -1$ and $I_{4}$ commutes with every $v_{a}$, $w_{a}$; so $\mathcal{R}_{\C} = \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}\otimes(H_{4} \oplus H_{5})$ inside the algebra, $c^{2} = Q(c)$ is $I_{4}$-bilinear, and the field has four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum. With $b = \sum_{a}v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$, $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{tb})$ is the rung boost $e^{tK}$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{\phi I_{4}b})$ multiplies each $v_{a}$ by $e^{\phi I_{4}}$ and each $w_{a}$ by $e^{-\phi I_{4}}$, which is $e^{2\phi Y}$: on the rung summand the hypercharge rotation is the rung boost at $I_{4}$-imaginary rapidity, the reading \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes} gives on the modes. Since $I_{4}b$ anticommutes with every spacetime vector, $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{\phi I_{4}b})$ does not fix the spacetime vectors (it moves $\gamma_{0}$ for $\cos\phi = -\tfrac{7}{25}$), so the identification holds on rung values, not on spacetime points.
\item \emph{(Spectrum of the linear field.)} Let $V = V_{D} + W(N) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$, with the level fixed by the stored vacuum condition so that the family point is critical. Its eight masses there are $0$ three times (the gauge orbit), $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 2N^{*}W''$ and $m_{\pm}^{2} = M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$ twice, as on $L$, and the \emph{normal pair}, spanned by the two directions of $\alpha_{1}$, the only directions that change $Q$ at first order, with
\[
m_{H}^{2},\ m_{A}^{2} = 2W'(N^{*}) + 4N^{*}(k_{10} \pm r) = m_{\pm}^{2} - M_{W}^{2} + 4N^{*}(k_{10} \pm r),
\]
not mixed with the other modes. For the pure D-term the normal pair is massless. With $k_{8} = k_{9} = 0$ and the term $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2}$, the vacuum lies at $Q = -H^{2}(1 - 2W'/m_{H}^{2})$ to first order in $H^{2}$: the constrained field is the limit $k_{10} \to \infty$ of the linear one, at fixed $m_{h}$ and $m_{\pm}$.
\item \emph{(Scale-free linear field.)} Let $V$ be a quartic over the ten stored invariants on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $V = k_{1}|\alpha|^{4} + k_{2}|\beta|^{4} + k_{3}|\alpha|^{2}|\beta|^{2} + |\alpha|^{2}(k_{4}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{5}\operatorname{Im}Q) + |\beta|^{2}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}Q) + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} + k_{10}|Q|^{2}$, with the flat condition $a + b - e = 0$ and the admissibility $e \ge 0$, $2a \ge e$ of \claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(3). The physical ray $\alpha = 0$ is a critical point exactly when $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$. There the masses are $0$ four times (three gauge directions and the scalon), $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2(2a - e)N$ twice, and $m_{H}^{2}, m_{A}^{2} = 2(2a - e)N + 4N(k_{10} \pm r)$, all proportional to $N$. If $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$ and $k_{10} \ge r$, then $V \ge 0$ on $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$ and $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$; if $k_{10} + r < -(2a - e)/2$ the normal pair is tachyonic.
\item \emph{(The scalon sum.)} Under the hypotheses (GW) and (D) of \claimref{synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev}, applied to the scale-free linear field of (3) (real scalars with a quartic polynomial potential, the setting of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}), the real scalars other than the scalon and the gauge directions are the charged pair and the normal pair, and
\[
8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4} + 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} - 12m_{t}^{4} - \ell, \qquad \ell = 12m_{b}^{4} + 12m_{c}^{4} + 4m_{\tau}^{4}.
\]
With the stored input box of that result ($m_{h} \in [125, 125.4]$, $v \in [246, 247]$, $m_{t} \in [162, 173]$ GeV, the stored $M_{W}$, $M_{Z}$, $m_{b}$, $m_{c}$, $m_{\tau}$), $2 \cdot 450^{4} < 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4} < 2 \cdot 456^{4}$ GeV$^{4}$. Hence $m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV and $m_{H}, m_{A} < 542$ GeV; when $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$ (as under $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$, $k_{10} \ge r$), $m_{\pm} < 383$ GeV. The stored bracket $450 < m_{\pm} < 456$ GeV is the case $m_{H} = m_{A} = 0$. The displayed relation is the standard Gildener-Weinberg sum rule of the scale-invariant two-doublet model; what is new is that the linear rung field is that model.
\item \emph{(Diphoton rate.)} Under the same hypotheses, with the loop functions of the stored result, the normal pair is neutral and does not enter $h \to \gamma\gamma$ at one loop, the charged pair enters with unit weight, and its loop function $A_{0}(\tau) = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 2}4^{n}\tau^{n - 2}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, $\tau = m_{h}^{2}/4m_{\pm}^{2}$, increases as $m_{\pm}$ decreases; so $\mu_{\gamma\gamma}$ decreases with $m_{\pm}$ and $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ for every $m_{\pm} \in (m_{h}/2, 456]$ GeV.
\end{enumerate}

\emph{Note (the transmutation branch excluded, 2 November 2026).} Under the decided coupling reading, the $\su(2)_{R}$-covariant completion $Yc + \tilde{Y}c^{*}$ with complex symmetric family matrices (the rung $10$), the scale-free (transmutation) branch of clauses (3) to (5) is recorded as excluded, by three independent strikes: (a) $h \to \gamma\gamma$: the bound $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$ of (5) lies $3.3$ standard deviations below the Particle Data Group 2026 average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ (pdglive node S126SGG, read on 2 November 2026; inputs ATLAS 2023 $1.04^{+0.10}_{-0.09}$, CMS 2022 $1.13 \pm 0.09$, ATLAS and CMS Run 1 $1.14^{+0.19}_{-0.18}$); (b) $B$-meson mixing: with the normal pair below $542$ GeV, as (4) requires, its tree-level exchange exceeds the measured $B_{s}$ and $B_{d}$ mass differences more than $50$ times for every splitting of $m_{H}$ and $m_{A}$ (more than $52$ and $50$), with quark mixing from tree-level determinations and three-family unitarity (\claimref{synthesis.covariant-rung-coupling-gives-the-normal-pair-tree-level-b-meson-mixing-that-excludes-the-transmutation-branch}); (c) strong coupling: on the surface of (4) the quartic couplings reach $4\pi$ between about $0.8$ and $4$ TeV at one loop (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-quartics-run-to-strong-coupling-within-a-few-tev-on-the-transmutation-branch}). Clauses (1) to (5) and their mathematics are unchanged: (1) and (2) hold for the linear field on every branch, and (3) to (5) stand as statements about the scale-free linear field under (GW) and (D); what is excluded is that branch as the origin of the weak scale under that coupling reading. The branch with a level, on which the normal pair and the charged pair are heavy (about $2.5$ to $3.5$ TeV), is the working branch.
synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.technical:
Take the field theory's unit to be $I_{4}$. In the algebra of spacetime and the two rung planes, $I_{4}$ commutes with the rung vectors, so the rung field's complex coefficients are $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$-valued inside the algebra, $c^{2} = Q(c)$ is bilinear over them, and the field carries four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum; on the rung summand the hypercharge rotation is the rung boost $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{tb})$, $b = \sum_{a}v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$, taken at imaginary rapidity $t = \phi I_{4}$. A polynomial (elementary) quantum field is linear: it takes values in all eight real components, not on the quadric $Q = -H^{2}$. The charged pair lies below $456$ GeV (below $383$ GeV when the normal pair is the heavier, as for $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$, $k_{10} \ge r$), the normal pair below $542$ GeV; the stored $450$ to $456$ GeV is the edge with a massless normal pair. That edge is itself excluded (argued): the normal pair is the neutral part of a doublet, so a massless pair would add about half a neutrino species to the invisible width of the $Z$, which the measured width rules out. synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutra.lay: To treat the series' Higgs candidate, the rung field, as a quantum field one has to say what its quantum values are. The series' own imaginary unit, the spacetime volume element, works for it, and with that unit the hypercharge symmetry turns out to be the series' frame boost taken at imaginary speed. A quantum field of the ordinary, well-behaved kind cannot be confined to the curved surface on which the rung field was defined; it has to range over all its directions, and two extra neutral particles appear, the directions off the surface. If the weak scale arises from quantum corrections alone, as an earlier result explored, these two particles must be counted: the charged scalar that result predicted near 450 GeV is then lighter, the new neutral pair lies below about 540 GeV, and the predicted shortfall in the Higgs boson's decays to two photons, about ten per cent, remains for every allowed charged mass. (Since 2 November 2026 that quantum-corrections route is recorded as ruled out under the series' reading of how the Higgs field couples to quarks: the measured two-photon rate lies well above the predicted shortfall, the new neutral pair would make bottom mesons turn into their antiparticles far faster than is observed, and the forces among these particles would grow too strong within a few TeV. The working alternative has the second set of particles at a few TeV.)

proofs.main:
\emph{(1).} Take generators $\gamma_{0}, \ldots, \gamma_{3}$ of spacetime and, for each rung plane $a = 4, 5$, $e_{a}$, $f_{a}$ with $e_{a}^{2} = 1$, $f_{a}^{2} = -1$, all mutually orthogonal, and $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} + f_{a})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} - f_{a})$; then $v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$ and $\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \delta_{ab}$, the stored null pairs. A vector orthogonal to the four $\gamma_{\mu}$ anticommutes with each of them, so it commutes with their product $I_{4}$ (four sign changes); $I_{4}^{2} = -1$. This is the stored property that $I_{4}$ commutes with every mode (\claimref{obj.field-theory.single-algebra-field}), here for the rung modes. Hence $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ acts on $H_{4} \oplus H_{5}$ as a complex structure inside the algebra, and for $c = \sum_{a}(\alpha_{a}v_{a} + \beta_{a}w_{a})$ with $\alpha_{a}, \beta_{a} \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, $c^{2} = \sum_{a,b}\alpha_{a}\beta_{b}\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta = Q(c)$, bilinear over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$: the stored complex-bilinear form, its unit read as $I_{4}$. (In the full algebra $I_{4}$ is not central: it anticommutes with the spacetime vectors, as the field theory uses; on the rung summand it commutes.) Four $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ coefficients give four $I_{4}$-complex modes per momentum, each realised by the polynomial representation of \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(1) with variables indexed by the rung field's modes.

Let $b_{a} = v_{a}w_{a} - \tfrac12 = v_{a}\wedge w_{a}$ and $b = b_{4} + b_{5}$. From $w_{a}v_{a} = 1 - v_{a}w_{a}$ and $v_{a}^{2} = 0$: $v_{a}w_{a}v_{a} = v_{a}$, so $[b, v_{a}] = v_{a}$, and likewise $[b, w_{a}] = -w_{a}$; $b_{4}$ and $b_{5}$ commute (disjoint planes), $b_{a}^{2} = v_{a}w_{a}v_{a}w_{a} - v_{a}w_{a} + \tfrac14 = \tfrac14$, and $(I_{4}b_{a})^{2} = -\tfrac14$. So $e^{tb_{a}} = \cosh\tfrac t2 + 2b_{a}\sinh\tfrac t2$, $e^{\phi I_{4}b_{a}} = \cos\tfrac\phi2 + 2I_{4}b_{a}\sin\tfrac\phi2$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(e^{zb}) = e^{z\,\mathrm{ad}_{b}}$ multiplies $v_{a}$ by $e^{z}$ and $w_{a}$ by $e^{-z}$, for $z = t$ real (the stored $e^{tK}$, $Kv_{a} = v_{a}$, $Kw_{a} = -w_{a}$, \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(4)) and for $z = \phi I_{4}$. On coefficients the latter is $\alpha \mapsto e^{\phi I_{4}}\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto e^{-\phi I_{4}}\beta$, which is $e^{2\phi Y}$ for $Y = \tfrac{1}{2}I_{4}\mathbf{1}$ acting by $\alpha \mapsto Y\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto \bar{Y}\beta$. So $Y = \tfrac12 I_{4}K$ on the rung field: the unitary hypercharge flow is the rung boost at $I_{4}$-imaginary rapidity, which is the reading \claimref{field-theory.boost-modes} gives for any plane's modes (real rapidity scales, imaginary rapidity is the unitary phase). The identification is on rung values only: each $\gamma_{\mu}$ anticommutes with $I_{4}$ and commutes with $b$, so it anticommutes with $I_{4}b$, and $e^{\phi I_{4}b}\gamma_{\mu}e^{-\phi I_{4}b} = e^{2\phi I_{4}b}\gamma_{\mu} \ne \gamma_{\mu}$ for $\phi \notin \pi\mathbb{Z}$: the automorphism moves every spacetime vector and does not commute with the Lorentz rotors, so it is not a spacetime-point transformation, while on the rung summand it is the hypercharge phase. The check verifies all of this in $\Cl(3,5)$ at $e^{t} = 4$ and $(\cos\phi, \sin\phi) = (-\tfrac{7}{25}, \tfrac{24}{25})$, including that $\gamma_{0}$ anticommutes with $v_{a}$ and with $I_{4}b$ and that its image is not $\gamma_{0}$.

\emph{(2).} By \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(1), on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $\sum_{j}\mu_{j}^{2} = \tfrac14(N^{2} - |Q|^{2})$ and $\mu_{Y} = \tfrac12 m$, so $V = F(N, m) + (k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})|Q|^{2} + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2}$ with $F = \tfrac18 g^{2}N^{2} + \tfrac12 g'^{2}(\tfrac12 m - \zeta)^{2} + W(N)$. Write $A = |\alpha|^{2}$, $B = |\beta|^{2}$, $N = \tfrac12(A + B)$, $m = \tfrac12(A - B)$. At $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-\lambda, 0)$: $\partial_{B}V = \tfrac12(F_{N} - F_{m})$, which vanishes by the stored vacuum condition (on the cone it reads $(g^{2} + g'^{2})\lambda^{2} + 4g'^{2}\zeta + 8W' = 0$), so $F_{m} = F_{N} = \tfrac14 g^{2}N^{*} + W'$. The $\alpha$ directions enter $V$ through $A$ (quadratically in $\alpha$) and through $Q = -\lambda\alpha_{1}$ (linearly in $\alpha_{1}$); hence the first derivatives in $\alpha$ vanish, the $\alpha$-$\beta$ second derivatives vanish, $\alpha_{2}$ does not mix with $\alpha_{1}$, and in real coordinates the Hessian on $\alpha_{2}$ is $2\partial_{A}V = F_{N} + F_{m} = \tfrac12 g^{2}N^{*} + 2W' = M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$, the stored charged mass, while on $\alpha_{1}$ it is $M_{W}^{2} + 2W'$ plus the Hessian of $\lambda^{2}\bigl((k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})|\alpha_{1}|^{2} + k_{8}\operatorname{Re}\alpha_{1}^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{1}^{2}\bigr)$, the matrix $2\lambda^{2}\bigl((k_{10} - \tfrac18 g^{2})\mathbf{1} + \bigl(\begin{smallmatrix}k_{8} & k_{9}\\ k_{9} & -k_{8}\end{smallmatrix}\bigr)\bigr)$, with eigenvalues $4N^{*}(k_{10} \pm r) - M_{W}^{2}$. The sum is $2W' + 4N^{*}(k_{10} \pm r)$. The kinetic coefficient of each real coordinate is one ($2N(e) = 1$). The $\beta$ block is the stored one: three directions of the gauge orbit (rank three, the generator $Y - T_{3}$ fixing the point) are massless by invariance, and the radial direction has $m_{h}^{2} = M_{Z}^{2} + 2N^{*}W''$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}(4) at $m^{*} = -N^{*}$, $H = 0$). Since $Q = \alpha^{\mathsf T}\beta$ has differential $\beta^{\mathsf T}d\alpha + \alpha^{\mathsf T}d\beta = -\lambda\,d\alpha_{1}$ at the point, the normal pair is exactly the pair of directions transverse to $L_{0}$. For the pure D-term ($W = 0$, $k = 0$) its mass vanishes: these are D-flat directions.

\emph{The level.} With $k_{8} = k_{9} = 0$ and the term $k_{10}|Q + H^{2}|^{2}$, restrict to $\alpha = (a, 0)$, $\beta = (-\lambda', 0)$ with $a, \lambda'$ real. Since $V$ depends on $a$ only through $a^{2}$ and through $Q = -a\lambda'$, the mixed second derivative in $(a, \lambda')$ vanishes at $a = 0$, so the shift of $\lambda'$ at first order in $H^{2}$ does not enter the $a$-equation at that order. Along real $\alpha_{1} = a$ the part of $V$ without the $k_{10}$ term is quadratic in $a$ at first order, with coefficient half the normal Hessian of (2) at $k_{10} = 0$, that is $W'$; so the $a$-derivative is $2W'a - 2\lambda k_{10}(H^{2} - a\lambda) + O(H^{4})$, which vanishes for $a(2W' + 4N^{*}k_{10}) = 2\lambda k_{10}H^{2}$, that is $a = \rho H^{2}/\lambda$ with $\rho = 1 - 2W'/m_{H}^{2}$, $m_{H}^{2} = 2W' + 4N^{*}k_{10}$, and $Q = -\rho H^{2}$. The check verifies this as the vanishing of the constant and linear coefficients in $H^{2}$ of the exact $\alpha_{1}$-gradient, and that $\rho = 1$ fails when $W' \ne 0$. As $k_{10} \to \infty$ with $m_{h}$, $m_{\pm}$ fixed, $\rho \to 1$ and the normal pair decouples: the constrained field is that limit. For $H \ne 0$ the off-diagonal Hessian entries between the normal and neutral directions are of relative order $H^{2}/N^{*}$ (computed symbolically), about $10^{-88}$ at the weak scale.

\emph{(3).} On the ray $\alpha = 0$, $V = k_{2}|\beta|^{4}$, so the ray is flat exactly when $k_{2} = 0$, which is $a + b - e = 2k_{2} = 0$ in the stored coordinates $a = k_{1} + k_{2} + k_{3}$, $b = k_{1} + k_{2} - k_{3}$, $e = 2(k_{1} - k_{2})$; then $e = 2k_{1}$ and $2a - e = 2k_{3}$. The only term linear in $\alpha$ is $|\beta|^{2}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}Q + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}Q) = -\lambda^{3}(k_{6}\operatorname{Re}\alpha_{1} + k_{7}\operatorname{Im}\alpha_{1})$, a tadpole unless $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$; the $k_{4}, k_{5}$ terms are cubic in $\alpha$ and do not enter the Hessian. As in (2), $\partial_{A}V = k_{3}\lambda^{2}$ gives $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2k_{3}\lambda^{2} = 2(2a - e)N$ on $\alpha_{2}$, and $\alpha_{1}$ adds $4N(k_{10} \pm r)$; the radial direction is the flat one (the scalon) and the gauge orbit has rank three. Every term is homogeneous of degree four, so each mass squared is proportional to $N$. For $k_{4} = k_{5} = 0$: $k_{8}\operatorname{Re}Q^{2} + k_{9}\operatorname{Im}Q^{2} \ge -r|Q|^{2}$, so $V \ge V_{4}(N, m) + (k_{10} - r)|Q|^{2}$ with $V_{4} = aN^{2} + bm^{2} + eNm$; on all of $\mathcal{R}_{\C}$, $N^{2} \ge |Q|^{2} + m^{2} \ge m^{2}$ (\claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}(5)), and $V_{4} \ge 0$ for $|m| \le N$ under the admissibility conditions (\claimref{synthesis.scale-free-rung-potentials-need-the-flat-physical-branch}(3)); so $V \ge 0$ when $k_{10} \ge r$, the ray is a minimum of $V$ on the unit sphere as the imported Fact requires, and $m_{H,A}^{2} \ge m_{\pm}^{2}$. If $k_{10} + r < -(2a - e)/2$ one normal mass squared is negative (the check exhibits $V = -\tfrac{1}{200}$ next to the ray for $k_{3} = \tfrac12$, $k_{10} = -1$).

\emph{(4).} Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass} applies to real scalars with a scale-free quartic polynomial potential and a flat direction at a minimum on the unit sphere; the linear field of (3) is such a theory (eight real scalars), and the cone $L_{0}$ is not a linear space, so the constrained field is outside the Fact's hypotheses except as a limit. Counting real scalars with masses at $\varphi = v$: the three gauge directions are massless in Landau gauge and the scalon is the flat direction, leaving the charged pair (two) and the normal pair (two); vectors and fermions are as in \claimref{synthesis.transmutation-of-the-rung-field-needs-a-charged-pair-near-450-gev}(i), under the same hypothesis (D). This gives the displayed relation, the standard sum rule of the scale-invariant two-doublet model: J. S. Lee and A. Pilaftsis, Phys. Rev. D 86 (2012) 035004 (arXiv:1201.4891), and K. Lane and W. Shepherd, arXiv:1808.07927, Eq. (10), $(\sum M^{4})^{1/4} = 540$ GeV over the heavy states (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(i); their fermion couplings differ from the series' readings, which the sum rule does not use). Solving for $X = 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$, the right side is $8\pi^{2}v^{2}m_{h}^{2} - 6M_{W}^{4} - 3M_{Z}^{4} + 12m_{t}^{4} + \ell$, the expression the stored result calls $2m_{\pm}^{4}$; it increases in $\pi$, $v$, $m_{h}$, $m_{t}$, and the stored check's corner evaluation, repeated here with $\pi \in [\tfrac{333}{106}, \tfrac{355}{113}]$, gives $2 \cdot 450^{4} < X < 2 \cdot 456^{4}$. Then $2m_{\pm}^{4} \le X$ gives $m_{\pm} < 456$; $m_{H}^{4} \le X$ and $X < 542^{4}$ give $m_{H}, m_{A} < 542$ (computed: $X^{1/4}$ lies between $535.8$ and $541.6$ GeV over the box); and $m_{H}, m_{A} \ge m_{\pm}$ give $4m_{\pm}^{4} \le X < 4 \cdot 383^{4}$. Equality $X = 2m_{\pm}^{4}$, the stored bracket, holds only for $m_{H} = m_{A} = 0$. The normal pair is the neutral component of the doublet $\alpha$, so the $Z$ couples to it with doublet strength and $Z \to HA$ is open when $m_{H} + m_{A} < M_{Z}$; a massless pair would add about half a neutrino species to the $Z$'s invisible width, which the measured $N_{\nu} = 2.9840 \pm 0.0082$ excludes (argued; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(ii)); this does not change the bounds above appreciably, since $M_{Z}^{4}/8 \ll X$.

\emph{Reading.} In the scale-free case the bound $m_{H}^{2} < 542^{2}$ GeV$^{2}$ gives $4N(k_{10} + r) + m_{\pm}^{2} < 542^{2}$ GeV$^{2}$, so $k_{10} + r < 542^{2}/(2v^{2}) \approx 2.4$ (computed): the null-lift constraint is not imposed by a large coupling, and the elementary rung field under transmutation is two complete doublets with a neutral pair below $542$ GeV. With a level ($\xi \ne 0$, not scale free) $k_{10}$ is free and the constrained field is a limit of the linear one, but $k_{10} \gg 4\pi$ would put the normal pair's quartic beyond perturbation theory (argued). Transport-convenient throughout: the field, the locus, the unit and the boost are the series'; the spectrum and the scalon sum are standard two-doublet and Gildener-Weinberg computations.

\emph{(5).} With $f(\tau) = \arcsin^{2}\sqrt{\tau} = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 1}(4\tau)^{n}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, whose $n = 1$ term is $\tau$, $A_{0} = (f - \tau)/\tau^{2} = \tfrac12\sum_{n \ge 2}4^{n}\tau^{n - 2}/(n^{2}\binom{2n}{n})$, a series with positive coefficients and leading term $\tfrac13$, increasing on $0 < \tau < 1$. On the flat ray $m_{\pm}^{2} \propto \varphi^{2}$, so the charged pair's term has unit weight, as in the stored result; the normal pair carries no electric charge. The Standard Model amplitude $A_{\mathrm{SM}} = A_{1}(\tau_{W}) + \tfrac43 A_{1/2}(\tau_{t})$ is negative with $|A_{\mathrm{SM}}| > 1 > A_{0}$ (the check brackets it below $-6.4$), so $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} = ((A_{\mathrm{SM}} + A_{0})/A_{\mathrm{SM}})^{2}$ decreases as $A_{0}$ grows, that is as $m_{\pm}$ decreases. At $m_{\pm} = 456$ GeV, with the stored $m_{h}$, $M_{W}$ and pole $m_{t}$, exact interval arithmetic gives $\mu_{\gamma\gamma} < 0.900$; so the bound holds for every $m_{\pm} \in (m_{h}/2, 456]$ GeV. The check also brackets the rate below $0.900$ and decreasing at $400$, $300$, $200$, $100$ and $70$ GeV (computed: about $0.899$, $0.898$, $0.895$, $0.873$, $0.806$; the heavy limit $A_{0} = \tfrac13$ gives $0.900$). Against the Particle Data Group average $1.10 \pm 0.06$ quoted in the stored result, the deficit is about three standard deviations for every charged mass, so freeing the charged mass through the normal pair does not relieve it.

synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-.technical:
Given the massless two-point function, equal at spacelike separation to $-1/(4\pi^{2}Q(\xi))$ and even (standard), Pauli's free-field argument runs on the series' own polarisation sums. The sums of the stored fields have degree $d = 2s$: $1$ for a scalar, $k\gamma_{0} = 2k_{0}\Lambda(k)$ for the spinor, and the photon's bivector sum, a quadratic in $k$ on the null cone. With weights $1$ and $c$ on particle and antiparticle parts and bracket sign $\eta$, the bracket at spacelike $\xi$ is a nonzero multiple of $(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)(1/Q)$, and $P(\partial)(1/Q) \neq 0$; so in a positive-norm space ($c > 0$) the field is local exactly when $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{2s}$.

The tower's CAR has $\eta = +1$ and the palatial CCR $\eta = -1$, so with positive norm the tower carries local spinor fields and the palatial storey local scalar and photon fields, and an elementary local rung scalar of positive norm is palatial. The positive norm is needed: with an indefinite (Krein) form, $c = -1$, the condition becomes $\eta = (-1)^{2s}$ and a CAR scalar is local, as the Faddeev-Popov ghosts of covariant gauge fixing are. For these free fields the result can stand in for the Jost-point import, traded for locality with positive norm; modular covariance is an alternative premise for the same sign.
synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-.lay: Particles that make up matter obey an exclusion rule, while particles of force and the Higgs do not, and which rule a particle obeys is tied to its spin. Here that tie is derived for the series' simplest fields from one requirement, together with the usual rule that quantum states have positive probabilities: measurements at points too far apart for light to connect must not disturb each other. The series stores exclusion-rule modes in one part of its algebra and the other kind in another; the requirement allows half-integer spin only in the first and whole-number spin only in the second, so an elementary Higgs field would have to be built in the second. Without positive probabilities the rule fails, which is why the bookkeeping fields used to fix gauges can break it.

proofs.main:
\emph{Setting and the imported input.} Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with $\gamma_{0}^{2} = 1$, $\gamma_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$ and $Q(\xi) = \xi_{0}^{2} - \xi_{1}^{2} - \xi_{2}^{2} - \xi_{3}^{2}$. The one input from outside the store is the massless two-point function $D_{+}(\xi) = \int d\mu(k)\, e^{-I_{4}k\cdot\xi}$ over the forward null cone with the invariant measure (numbers, the field theory's phases among them, read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$); it is the boundary value $-1/(4\pi^{2}(Q(\xi) - i0\,\xi_{0}))$, so on the open spacelike set $\{Q < 0\}$ it is the real function $-1/(4\pi^{2}Q(\xi))$, even under $\xi \to -\xi$ (standard; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(i); e.g. the free-field chapters of Streater and Wightman or Birrell and Davies). Only $f = 1/Q$ and its evenness enter the argument and the checks; the constant $-1/(4\pi^{2})$ and the powers of $I_{4}$ are overall nonzero factors and are kept symbolic. The method is Pauli's free-field argument (Pauli 1940, standard; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-free-field-spin-statistics-and-guido-longo-theorem}(ii)); the new content is that the series' own polarisation sums and storeys reproduce it.

\emph{The bracket of a free field.} Let a free field have particle part $\int d\mu\, u(k)a(k)e^{-I_{4}k\cdot x}$ and antiparticle part $\int d\mu\, v(k)b^{*}(k)e^{I_{4}k\cdot x}$, with $[a(k), a^{*}(k')]_{\eta} = [b(k), b^{*}(k')]_{\eta} = \delta$ (the bracket $[x, y]_{\eta} = xy + \eta yx$, $\eta = +1$ for the CAR, $-1$ for the CCR), and suppose the antiparticle sum $\sum vv^{*}$ is $c$ times the particle sum $P(k) = \sum uu^{*}$, $c \neq 0$ real, with $c > 0$ when the Fock space has a positive norm, as for the stored spinor field (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2): the anticommutator is $\sum_{j} 2\alpha_{j}\cos(k_{j}\cdot\xi)\Lambda(k_{j})\chi$, the same $\Lambda(k)$ on both exponentials) and the Hermitian photon (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(4)); for a scalar $P = 1$ and positivity of $\langle bb^{*}\rangle$ forces $c > 0$. On an indefinite (Krein) space $\langle bb^{*}\rangle$ may be negative, and then $c < 0$ is allowed. Then the bracket of the field with its adjoint is the c-number
\[
\int d\mu\,P(k)e^{-I_{4}k\cdot\xi} + \eta c\int d\mu\,P(k)e^{I_{4}k\cdot\xi} = P(I_{4}\partial)D_{+}(\xi) + \eta c\,P(-I_{4}\partial)\bigl[D_{+}(-\,\cdot\,)\bigr](\xi),
\]
$\xi = x - y$, where $P$ is any polynomial agreeing with the sum on the cone (two such differ by $Q(k)R(k)$, and $R(I_{4}\partial)\Box D_{+} = 0$ off the cone since $\Box(1/Q) = 0$ there, checked). For $P$ homogeneous of degree $d$, $P(-I_{4}\partial) = (-1)^{d}P(I_{4}\partial)$, and on the spacelike set $D_{+}(-\xi) = D_{+}(\xi)$, so there the bracket is $-\tfrac{I_{4}^{d}}{4\pi^{2}}(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)f$. The script evaluates the two terms separately, the second from the derivatives of $1/Q$ at $-\xi$ with the chain-rule signs, so the parity is computed, not assumed.

\emph{(1).} Scalar: $P = 1$, $d = 0$. Spinor: by Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(1) the one-particle projector is $\Lambda(k) = k\gamma_{0}/(2k_{0})$, the factor $1/(2k_{0})$ belonging to the invariant measure, so $P(k) = k\gamma_{0}$, linear: $P(-k) = -P(k)$. The script checks $\Lambda^{2} = \Lambda$, $k\Lambda = 0$, $P(-k) = -P(k)$ and $P(2k) = 2P(k)$ at five rational null $k$. Photon: by Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(2) the modes at null $k$ are the bivectors $f$ with $kf = 0$; for $\epsilon$ orthogonal to $k$, $k(k \wedge \epsilon) = Q(k)\epsilon - (k\cdot\epsilon)k = 0$, so the modes are $k \wedge \epsilon$ with $\epsilon$ transverse (the script checks two independent transverse $\epsilon$ at each $k$). The polarisation sum on test bivectors is $\sum_{ij}(\delta_{ij} - k_{i}k_{j}/|\mathbf{k}|^{2})\langle A(k \wedge \gamma_{i})\rangle_{0}\langle B(k \wedge \gamma_{j})\rangle_{0}$; the terms of $-g^{\mu\nu}$ beyond the transverse projector are proportional to $k^{\mu}$ or $k^{\nu}$ and vanish under $k \wedge$, so on the cone it equals the quadratic polynomial of (1). The script verifies the equality for all $36$ pairs of basis bivectors at five null $k$, and $P(-k) = P(k)$, $P(2k) = 4P(k)$. So $d = 0, 1, 2 = 2s$ for the three fields.

\emph{(2).} $\partial_{\mu}f = -2\xi_{\mu}/Q^{2}$ and $\partial_{\mu}\partial_{\nu}f = -2g_{\mu\nu}/Q^{2} + 8\xi_{\mu}\xi_{\nu}/Q^{3}$, exact at rational points. For the spinor $P(\partial)f = \partial^{\mu}f\,\gamma_{\mu}\gamma_{0} = -2\xi\gamma_{0}/Q^{2} \neq 0$. For the photon the script computes the coefficients of the quadratic $P(k)[A, B]$ by polarisation and evaluates $P(\partial)f$ for $A = B = \gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}$, nonzero; for the scalar $f \neq 0$. At four rational spacelike points and for $\eta = \pm 1$, $c \in \{1, 2, \tfrac12\}$, the computed bracket vanishes exactly when $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{d}$, and with $c = -1$ added to the sample exactly when $\eta = (-1)^{d}$. Since the bracket is $-\tfrac{I_{4}^{d}}{4\pi^{2}}(1 + \eta c(-1)^{d})P(\partial)f$ on the whole spacelike set and $P(\partial)f$ is a nonzero rational function there, the field is local (its bracket vanishes at every spacelike separation, the locality of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.second-quantisation}(2)) if and only if $1 + \eta c(-1)^{d} = 0$, that is, for $c > 0$, $c = 1$ and $\eta = -(-1)^{d}$, and for $c = -1$, $\eta = (-1)^{d}$. The second case needs a negative-norm antiparticle term: a local anticommuting scalar ($d = 0$, $\eta = +1$, $c = -1$) is the Faddeev-Popov ghost of covariant gauge fixing, which lives on a Krein space (\claimref{synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs-a-krein-form-and-the-tower-supplies-the-ghosts}); so every statement below about which storey carries a local field holds in a positive-norm space. With $\eta = +1$ and $d = 1$ this is the stored anticommutator $\chi(\nabla D)\gamma_{0}$, a derivative of the Pauli-Jordan function.

\emph{(3).} A tower plane is realised in $\Cl(1,1)$ by $v = \tfrac12(e + f)$, $w = \tfrac12(e - f)$, $e^{2} = 1$, $f^{2} = -1$: $Q(v) = Q(w) = 0$ and $vw + wv = 1$ (the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}), while $vw - wv \neq 1$. The palatial pair on polynomials (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra}), $a = d/dz$, $a^{*} = z$, has $[a, a^{*}]z^{n} = z^{n}$ and $\{a, a^{*}\}z^{n} = (2n + 1)z^{n}$, checked for $n \le 5$. So tower modes give $\eta = +1$, palatial modes $\eta = -1$, and by (2), with positive norm, a tower lift is local only for $d$ odd (the spinor) and a palatial lift only for $d$ even (the scalar and the photon). This is the twistor attachment's sentence (Theorem \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment}) that a CAR lift is local exactly when $2s$ is odd, now for these attached free fields from locality with positive norm and the sums, the Jost-point theorem being traded for those premises (it stays the input for interacting fields). By Proposition \claimref{field-theory.no-canonical-commutation-relations-tower} no floor and no bounded element of the CAR limit carries the CCR, so a local elementary scalar of positive norm, in particular a quantised rung field read as elementary, is a palatial field; the tower's rung vectors are odd CAR elements and as the modes of a local scalar field would violate (2). Bosons made of tower fermions are not excluded by this (they are even composites, with the CCR reached only in the limit of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr}).

\emph{Scope.} The result covers the free massless scalar, spinor and Maxwell fields with the stated structure of particle and antiparticle sums; it assumes locality, positive energy and a positive norm, and does not cover interacting fields or the general Wightman setting. For a massive field the same argument needs only that the massive two-point function is real, even and nonzero at spacelike separation (standard; its Bessel-function form is cited from memory and not used). The sign $(-1)^{2s}$ is also the factor by which the boost rotor continued over one modular period ($2\pi$ in imaginary rapidity, Theorem \claimref{synthesis.boost-evolution-on-generators-is-one-unitary-group}(iv)) acts on values; that coincidence is not used here, and a derivation from modular covariance rests on a different premise (\claimref{synthesis.modular-period-on-values-is-the-dual-plane-turn}). Transport-convenient: the sums and storeys are the series' objects; the locality argument itself is standard.
