proofs.main:
\emph{Step 1 (clause (i)).} The rung field is that of \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-on-the-lift-locus}, with the stored slot action. In $\Cl(3,5)$ take $v_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} + f_{a})$, $w_{a} = \tfrac12(e_{a} - f_{a})$ for the rung planes $a = 4, 5$, so $v_{a}^{2} = w_{a}^{2} = 0$, $\{v_{a}, w_{b}\} = \delta_{ab}$, and $I_{4}$ commutes with every $v_{a}$, $w_{a}$ (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(1)). For $x, y$ in $\{v_{4}, v_{5}, w_{4}, w_{5}\}$, $[xy, z] = x\{y, z\} - \{x, z\}y$ for a vector $z$, so $[v_{4}w_{5}, v_{5}] = v_{4}$, $[v_{4}w_{5}, w_{4}] = -w_{5}$, $[v_{5}w_{4}, v_{4}] = v_{5}$, $[v_{5}w_{4}, w_{5}] = -w_{4}$, and $[b_{a}, v_{a}] = v_{a}$, $[b_{a}, w_{a}] = -w_{a}$ (loc. cit. Step 2). Reading the coefficients of $c$ gives: $\tfrac12[I_{4}(v_{4}w_{5} + v_{5}w_{4}), \cdot]$ maps $\alpha \mapsto \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{1}\alpha$, $\beta \mapsto -\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{1}\beta$; $\tfrac12[v_{4}w_{5} - v_{5}w_{4}, \cdot]$ maps both $\alpha$ and $\beta$ by the real matrix $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{2}$; $\tfrac12[I_{4}(b_{4} \mp b_{5}), \cdot]$ maps $\alpha \mapsto \tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\sigma_{3}\alpha$ or $\tfrac{I_{4}}{2}\alpha$ and $\beta$ by the conjugates. These are the stored $T_{1}$, $T_{2}$, $T_{3}$, $Y$ with the unit $I_{4}$. The coefficients are read back by $\alpha_{a} = \{w_{a}, c\}$, $\beta_{a} = \{v_{a}, c\}$, and $Q = c^{2}$ by the Clifford product. The check builds the four generators and the form $Q$ in the GA engine and verifies them against the stored action, and verifies $\nabla V\cdot t\varphi = 0$ for all four. For the coupling: by \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-coupling-to-its-conjugate-is-the-second-family-matrix}, at a point with only rung-$4$ components $M_{d} = \beta Y + \bar{\alpha}\tilde{Y}$ and $M_{u} = \alpha Y + \bar{\beta}\tilde{Y}$; with $Y_{33}$ neglected the third family has $M_{u} = \bar{\beta}_{4}y$, $M_{d} = \bar{\alpha}_{4}y$, whose $SU(2)$-covariant completion in Weyl fields $q$, $u^{c}$, $d^{c}$ is $y\,\epsilon(q, \bar\beta)u^{c} - y\,(q\cdot\bar\alpha)d^{c}$ (under $X \in SU(2)$, $\bar{\beta} \mapsto X\bar{\beta}$, $\bar{\alpha} \mapsto \bar{X}\bar{\alpha}$, and $\epsilon(Xq, X\bar\beta) = \epsilon(q, \bar\beta)$, $(Xq)\cdot(\bar X\bar\alpha) = q\cdot\bar\alpha$); the hypercharges balance, $\tfrac16 + \tfrac12 - \tfrac23 = 0$ and $\tfrac16 - \tfrac12 + \tfrac13 = 0$. The check verifies the invariance $M_{F}(t\varphi) + \tau^{\mathsf T}M_{F} + M_{F}\tau = 0$ for the four generators exactly, and that at $\alpha = 0$, $\beta = (-1, 0)$ only the top pair has mass. Both couplings equal $\tilde{Y}_{33}$, so $y_{1} = y_{2} = m_{t}/v$ at the vacuum.

\emph{Step 2 (clause (ii)).} The gauge loops are taken in Landau gauge with the indefinite form of the Krein premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields} on the gauge field, as in the stored one-loop running; the scalar and Yukawa terms do not use it. For real scalars $\varphi$ with a scale-free quartic $V$, vector masses $M_{V}^{2}(\varphi)_{AB} = g_{A}g_{B}(t_{A}\varphi)\cdot(t_{B}\varphi)$ and Weyl mass matrix $M_{F}(\varphi)$, the one-loop effective potential in Landau gauge is $V + \tfrac{1}{64\pi^{2}}\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4}(\ln M^{2}/\mu^{2} - c)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}(i)), with $\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4} = \operatorname{Tr}V''^{2} + 3\operatorname{Tr}M_{V}^{4} - 2\operatorname{Tr}(M_{F}M_{F}^{\dagger})^{2}$. Its independence of $\mu$ at this order, together with the field's anomalous dimension $\gamma = Y_{2}(S) + 3\sum_{A}g_{A}^{2}t_{A}t_{A}$, $Y_{2}(S)_{ab} = \tfrac12\operatorname{Tr}(Y^{a\dagger}Y^{b} + Y^{b\dagger}Y^{a})$, $Y^{a} = \partial M_{F}/\partial\varphi_{a}$, gives
\[
16\pi^{2}\beta_{V}(\varphi) = \tfrac12\bigl(\operatorname{Tr}V''^{2} + 3\operatorname{Tr}M_{V}^{4} - 2\operatorname{Tr}(M_{F}M_{F}^{\dagger})^{2}\bigr) + \varphi\cdot\gamma\nabla V,
\]
the one-loop part of the general formula \cite{MachacekVaughn1985, LuoWangXiao2003} written as a polynomial (cited from memory). The check confirms the normalisation on one doublet ($V = \lambda|H|^{4}$ gives $24\lambda^{2} - 3\lambda(3g^{2} + g'^{2}) + \tfrac38(2g^{4} + (g^{2} + g'^{2})^{2}) + 12\lambda y_{t}^{2} - 6y_{t}^{4}$) and on $O(N)$, $N = 1, 8$ ($(N + 8)/3$ times $\lambda^{2}$ for $V = \tfrac{\lambda}{24}(\varphi^{2})^{2}$ \cite{KleinertSchulteFrohlinde2001}). Since $\beta_{V}$ is $U(2)$-invariant and quartic it is a combination of the ten invariants; the check computes the fourth-derivative tensor of $V$ by polarisation, $\beta_{V}$ at sampled points and couplings, and compares with $\sum_{i}\dot k_{i}P_{i}(\varphi)$ for the closed forms. The general forms are those of clause (ii) plus, with $\kappa = 12(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2})$ and $\kappa' = 12(k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2})$: $\kappa$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{1}$, $\kappa'$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{2}$, $4(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2}) + 16(k_{4}k_{6} + k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{3}$, $10(k_{4}^{2} - k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} - k_{7}^{2}) + 4(k_{4}k_{6} - k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{8}$, $20(k_{4}k_{5} + k_{6}k_{7}) + 4(k_{4}k_{7} + k_{5}k_{6})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{9}$, $10(k_{4}^{2} + k_{5}^{2} + k_{6}^{2} + k_{7}^{2}) + 4(k_{4}k_{6} + k_{5}k_{7})$ in $16\pi^{2}\dot k_{10}$, and
\begin{align*}
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{4} &= (96k_{1} + 24k_{3} + 32k_{10} + 40k_{8})k_{4} + 40k_{9}k_{5} + (24k_{3} + 16k_{10} + 8k_{8})k_{6} + 8k_{9}k_{7} - wk_{4} + (18y_{1}^{2} + 6y_{2}^{2})k_{4},\\
16\pi^{2}\dot k_{5} &= (96k_{1} + 24k_{3} + 32k_{10} - 40k_{8})k_{5} + 40k_{9}k_{4} + (24k_{3} + 16k_{10} - 8k_{8})k_{7} + 8k_{9}k_{6} - wk_{5} + (18y_{1}^{2} + 6y_{2}^{2})k_{5},
\end{align*}
and $\dot k_{6}$, $\dot k_{7}$ the same with $(k_{1}, k_{4}, k_{5}, y_{1}, y_{2}) \leftrightarrow (k_{2}, k_{6}, k_{7}, y_{2}, y_{1})$. Every term of $\dot k_{4}, \ldots, \dot k_{7}$ contains one of $k_{4}, \ldots, k_{7}$, so the branch $k_{4} = \cdots = k_{7} = 0$ is preserved; it is the branch of the stored physical ray when also $k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$ there is required (\claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(3)). The coupling is invariant under $\alpha \to -\alpha$, $d^{c} \to -d^{c}$, which is why no $k_{4}, \ldots, k_{7}$ is generated; the neglected $Y_{33}$ breaks it at order $y_{t}^{3}y_{b}$.

\emph{Step 3 (dictionary).} With canonical real components $|\beta|^{2} = v^{2}$, so the doublets of the standard normalisation are $\Phi = \beta/\sqrt2$, $\alpha/\sqrt2$ (with the conjugations of Step 1), and $|\Phi_{1}^{\dagger}\Phi_{2}| = \tfrac12|Q|$: $\tfrac{\lambda_{1}}{2}|\Phi_{1}|^{4} = k_{1}A^{2}$ gives $\lambda_{1} = 8k_{1}$, and likewise $\lambda_{2} = 8k_{2}$, $\lambda_{3} = 4k_{3}$, $\lambda_{4} = 4k_{10}$, $\operatorname{Re}\lambda_{5} = 4k_{8}$, $|\operatorname{Im}\lambda_{5}| = 4|k_{9}|$; the top coupling of the canonical doublet is $\sqrt2 y_{2} = y_{t}$. The check substitutes these into the standard one-loop equations of the two-doublet model with a discrete symmetry and type-II couplings (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-general-quartic-running-and-two-doublet-renormalisation-group-equations}(ii): $16\pi^{2}\dot\lambda_{1} = 12\lambda_{1}^{2} + 4\lambda_{3}^{2} + 4\lambda_{3}\lambda_{4} + 2\lambda_{4}^{2} + 2|\lambda_{5}|^{2} + \tfrac34(3g^{4} + g'^{4} + 2g^{2}g'^{2}) - 3\lambda_{1}(3g^{2} + g'^{2}) + 12\lambda_{1}y_{b}^{2} - 12y_{b}^{4}$, and the forms for $\lambda_{2}$ to $\lambda_{5}$) and finds them equal to the closed forms term by term at sampled couplings. The masses of \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(3), $m_{\pm}^{2} = 2k_{3}v^{2}$, $m_{H,A}^{2} = m_{\pm}^{2} + 2v^{2}(k_{10} \pm r)$, are the familiar $\tfrac12\lambda_{3}v^{2}$ and $\tfrac12(\lambda_{3} + \lambda_{4} \pm |\lambda_{5}|)v^{2}$ of a doublet without a vacuum value.

\emph{Step 4 (clause (iii)).} For $V = \tfrac{1}{24}\lambda_{abcd}\varphi_{a}\varphi_{b}\varphi_{c}\varphi_{d}$ the pure-quartic two-loop term of the general formula, $-\tfrac14\sum_{\mathrm{perms}}\lambda_{abef}\lambda_{cegh}\lambda_{dfgh} + \sum_{\mathrm{legs}}\gamma^{(2)}\lambda$ with $\gamma^{(2)}_{ab} = \tfrac{1}{12}\lambda_{acde}\lambda_{bcde}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-general-quartic-running-and-two-doublet-renormalisation-group-equations}(i)), contracted with $\varphi^{4}/24$ is $-\tfrac12V''_{ef}V'''_{egh}V'''_{fgh} + \tfrac{1}{12}(\lambda\lambda)_{ab}\varphi_{a}\partial_{b}V$, since $\lambda_{abef}\varphi_{a}\varphi_{b} = 2V''_{ef}$ and $\lambda_{cegh}\varphi_{c} = V'''_{egh}$. One real scalar gives $-\tfrac14\cdot24 + \tfrac13 = -\tfrac{17}{3}$, and $O(N)$ gives $-(3N + 14)/3$ \cite{KleinertSchulteFrohlinde2001}; the check confirms both for $N = 1$ and $N = 8$, then compares the closed forms of clause (iii) with the field computation at three points; $\dot k_{4}^{(2)}, \ldots, \dot k_{7}^{(2)}$ vanish on the branch. For orientation (computed): at the symmetric point $k_{1} = k_{2} = 0$, $k_{3} = \tfrac65$, $k_{10} = s = 0$ the two-loop term of $\dot k_{3}$ is $-192k_{3}^{3}/(16\pi^{2})^{2}$ against $16k_{3}^{2}/(16\pi^{2})$, a ratio of about $-0.09$.

\emph{Step 5 (clause (iv)).} On the ray $\varphi = (0, 0, 0, 0, -v, 0, 0, 0)$ with $k_{2} = k_{6} = k_{7} = 0$, $\nabla V = 0$ (every term is at least quadratic in $\alpha$ or proportional to $k_{2}$), so $16\pi^{2}\beta_{V} = \tfrac12\mathrm{STr}\,M^{4}$ there and $\beta_{V} = \dot k_{2}v^{4}$. Directly from clause (ii) at $k_{2} = 0$: $2v^{4}(8k_{3}^{2} + 8k_{3}k_{10} + 4k_{10}^{2} + 4s) = 8k_{3}^{2}v^{4} + 8v^{4}((k_{3} + k_{10})^{2} + s) = 2m_{\pm}^{4} + m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$, $2v^{4}G = \tfrac{1}{16}(6g^{4} + 3(g^{2} + g'^{2})^{2})v^{4} = 6M_{W}^{4} + 3M_{Z}^{4}$, and $2v^{4}(-6y_{2}^{4}) = -12m_{t}^{4}$. Along the ray $V_{1\text{-loop}} = (k_{2}(\mu) + B\ln(\rho^{2}/\mu^{2}))\rho^{4}$ up to a constant times $\rho^{4}$, and $\mu$-independence gives $B = \tfrac12\dot k_{2}$; with Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-coleman-weinberg-gildener-weinberg-scalon-mass}(ii), $m_{h}^{2} = 8Bv^{2} = 4v^{2}\dot k_{2}$, which is \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(4) and, at its standard reading, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-two-doublet-scalon-sum-rule-and-lep-neutrino-count}(i). The check verifies the identity at three samples both from the closed form and from the field computation on the ray, and that dropping $m_{H}^{4} + m_{A}^{4}$ breaks it. For the self-coupling, with $L = \ln(\rho^{2}/v^{2})$ and $dL/d\rho = 2/\rho$, $V = B\rho^{4}(L - \tfrac12)$ has $V' = 4B\rho^{3}L$, $V'' = 12B\rho^{2}L + 8B\rho^{2}$, $V''' = 24B\rho L + 40B\rho$, so at $\rho = v$: $V' = 0$, $V'' = 8Bv^{2} = m_{h}^{2}$, $V''' = 40Bv = \tfrac53(3m_{h}^{2}/v)$, the tree value for the same mass being $3m_{h}^{2}/v$ (standard for Gildener-Weinberg potentials). By homogeneity the scalon couples to each heavy pair with $\partial m_{X}^{2}/\partial\rho = 2m_{X}^{2}/v$, the unit weight used in \claimref{synthesis.linear-rung-field-has-a-neutral-normal-pair-in-the-scalon-sum}(5).

\emph{Step 6 (clause (v), computed).} Initial values at $\mu_{0} = m_{t}$ (from memory, $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$): $g = 0.648$, $g' = 0.358$, $g_{3} = 1.164$, $y_{t} = 0.936$, so $y_{1} = y_{2} = 0.662$; the gauge couplings run at one loop with the stored two-doublet coefficients $(\tfrac{21}{5}, -3, -7)$ of \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces} (gauge loops, so under the Krein premise there too), that is $(7, -3, -7)$ for $(g', g, g_{3})$ with $g'$ in the non-GUT normalisation, and $y_{1} = y_{2}$ with $16\pi^{2}\dot y_{2} = y_{2}(y_{1}^{2} + 9y_{2}^{2} - 8g_{3}^{2} - \tfrac94g^{2} - \tfrac{17}{12}g'^{2})$ (the Yukawa part from the general one-loop formula applied to the coupling of Step 1, computed; its $y_{1} = 0$ limit is the standard $\tfrac92y_{t}^{3}$), with the hypercharge term of the $d^{c}$ coupling, $-\tfrac{5}{12}g'^{2}$, averaged in (negligible here). The quartics start at $k_{3} = m_{\pm}^{2}/(2v^{2})$, $k_{10} = (m_{H}^{2} + m_{A}^{2} - 2m_{\pm}^{2})/(4v^{2})$, $|k_{8}| = |m_{H}^{2} - m_{A}^{2}|/(4v^{2})$, $k_{9} = 0$, $k_{1} = k_{2} = 0$. synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs.formal:
Units and signature of the store; $k$ a null vector, $Q(k) = 0$. Polarisation modes $a_\mu = \partial/\partial z_\mu$ on the palatial polynomial representation (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra}) with its positive form $\langle z^n, z^m\rangle = n!\,\delta_{nm}$; ghost modes $b, d$ on two tower planes with the CAR of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit} and the floor's positive trace form.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(A self-adjoint BRST charge needs an indefinite form; proved.)} On a space with a positive-definite form an operator $Q$ with $Q^{*} = Q$ and $Q^2 = 0$ is zero. The tower's trace form ($\langle x^{*}y\rangle_0$, the basis blades orthonormal) and the palatial form are positive definite, so a nonzero nilpotent charge is not self-adjoint for either, and the self-adjoint BRST charge of the Kugo-Ojima framework does not exist on them. Nilpotent charges that are not self-adjoint do exist on positive spaces; that a local covariant vector potential needs an indefinite metric in general is Strocchi's theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iii)), not proved here.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Gupta-Bleuler BRST at a null momentum; proved.)} Let $\eta = (-1)^{n_0} \otimes S$, with $S = 1 - (b^{*} - d^{*})(b - d)$ the inner involution of the ghost floor exchanging $b$ and $d$, and $\langle x, y\rangle_K = \langle x, \eta y\rangle$. Then $a_\mu^{\dagger} = -g_{\mu\mu}z_\mu$ and $b^{\dagger} = d^{*}$, so $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$ for polarisation vectors $u, w$: the one-particle Krein form is the Minkowski metric of the polarisations, the standard Gupta-Bleuler form, invariant under boost rotors (the positive form is not). With $L = \sum_\mu g_{\mu\mu}k^\mu a_\mu$, $Q = L^{\dagger}b + d^{*}L$ satisfies $Q^2 = 0$ and $Q^{\dagger} = Q$.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Positive cohomology; computed up to three quanta.)} $Q$ preserves the total number $T$ (bosons plus ghosts). At ghost number $N_d - N_b = 0$ and $T = 0, 1, 2, 3$ the cohomology of $Q$ has dimensions $1, 2, 3, 4$, those of the symmetric powers of a two-dimensional space, and the Krein form restricted to $\ker Q$ has signature $(\dim H, 0, \dim \operatorname{im} Q)$: positive definite on the cohomology, with radical $\operatorname{im} Q$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(The physical modes are the stored photon modes; proved.)} The one-particle cohomology is $k^{\perp}/\mathrm{span}\{k\}$, and $\epsilon \mapsto k\epsilon$ maps it isomorphically onto the bivectors $\{f : kf = 0\}$, the mode space of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(2).
\item[(v)] \emph{(The constraint charge of the derived algebra on tower ghosts; proved, standard for any Lie algebra.)} For the derived gauge algebra $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} acting on the finite-dimensional matter representation $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors), with ghosts $c^a$ and antighosts $\bar c_a$ the creation and annihilation operators of twelve tower planes, the charge $Q = c^aT_a - \tfrac12 f_{ab}{}^{c}\,c^ac^b\bar c_c$ satisfies $Q^2 = 0$; without the cubic ghost term $Q^2 \neq 0$, and changing one structure constant gives $Q^2 \neq 0$.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Reading.} A self-adjoint BRST charge for the series' gauge fields needs an indefinite form, which the store's representations lack; the Gupta-Bleuler form of the polarisations supplies it in a Lorentz-invariant way, and under the premise that gauge fields carry this indefinite form, Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, the covariant route works at the free level with positive physical states. An indefinite form is already present at the one-particle level of the attachment: the conformal-group-invariant twistor form of signature $(2,2)$, whose positive polarisations alone carry states (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}); this is a parallel, not the form used here. The ghosts are tower modes, as the Grassmann variables of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.path-integral-inside-tower} are rungs; they are scalar CAR modes, which the spin-statistics clause of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} excludes as local fields with positive weights, and which are local only with antiparticle weight $-1$, that is in the indefinite form (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}); they appear only in zero-norm quartets. The sign of the one-loop beta coefficients of the non-abelian factors is computed in a result (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}).
synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs.technical:
The store quantises the photon in Coulomb gauge on a positive polynomial representation, and the tower's floors carry a positive trace form. The covariant route to non-abelian gauge fields in the Kugo-Ojima form needs a nilpotent self-adjoint BRST charge, and on a positive-definite space $\langle Qx, Qx\rangle = \langle x, Q^2x\rangle = 0$ forces $Q = 0$. So, assuming the store's positive forms, that route cannot be taken on the store's representations as they stand; it needs an indefinite (Krein) form. Nilpotent charges that are not self-adjoint exist on positive spaces, so this is a statement about self-adjoint charges; the general need for an indefinite metric for a local covariant vector potential is Strocchi's theorem (\claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}), not proved here.

The Minkowski metric of the polarisations offers one, the standard Gupta-Bleuler form. Give the polynomial representation the form twisted by $(-1)^{n_0}$ and the ghost floor the twist by the involution exchanging its two modes: the polarisation modes then obey $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$, which is boost-invariant, while the positive form singles out a frame. The free BRST charge at a null momentum, $Q = L^{\dagger}b + d^{*}L$ with $L = k\cdot a$, is nilpotent because $k$ is null and the ghosts anticommute, and self-adjoint for the Krein form. Its cohomology at ghost number zero, computed exactly with up to three quanta for two null momenta, is the symmetric algebra of a two-dimensional space with a positive-definite form: the transverse polarisations, which $\epsilon \mapsto k\epsilon$ identifies with the stored photon's bivector modes $\{f : kf = 0\}$.

For the derived gauge algebra, twelve tower planes carry the ghosts and antighosts, and the constraint charge $c^aT_a - \tfrac12 f_{ab}{}^{c}c^ac^b\bar c_c$ on the matter representation $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$ squares to zero exactly, the cubic ghost term being forced by non-commutativity; this holds for any Lie algebra and is standard. The interacting field-level charge (with the covariant derivative of the ghost acting on the gauge field) and confinement are not computed here; the sign of the beta coefficients is computed in \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}.
synthesis.self-adjoint-brst-charge-needs.lay: Quantising force fields like the gluons in a way that respects relativity needs a way of removing their unphysical parts. The standard way introduces fictitious particles (ghosts) and an accounting operator that, in its usual form, only works if some states are allowed negative norm. The series' quantum spaces all have positive norms, and a short argument shows that this usual form of the accounting cannot exist on them. The standard remedy, an indefinite measure built from the spacetime metric of the force field's polarisations, works with ghosts taken from the tower's fermion modes: for a single light-like momentum the surviving states are the two transverse polarisations, the same states the series already uses for the photon, and for the series' gauge group the ghosts' accounting closes exactly. The indefinite measure is a premise for the series, not something it derives, and the series' covariant treatment of force fields holds under it.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} If $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle$ is positive definite, $Q^{*} = Q$ and $Q^2 = 0$, then $\langle Qx, Qx\rangle = \langle x, Q^2x\rangle = 0$ for every $x$, so $Qx = 0$. On a floor of the tower (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}) the form $\langle x^{*}y\rangle_0$, with $*$ the reversion followed by a sign for each negative-square generator, makes the basis blades orthonormal: the check confirms $\langle b^{*}c\rangle_0 = \delta_{bc}$ over all blades of floors with one and two planes, and the computation for a general blade is the same product of signs, each factor $e^{*}e = e^2 = 1$ or $f^{*}f = -f^2 = 1$. On the palatial polynomial representation of Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-statistics-no-go-palatial-algebra} the form $\langle z^n, z^m\rangle = n!\,\delta_{nm}$ is diagonal with positive entries. So a nonzero nilpotent charge is not self-adjoint for either form, and the self-adjoint charge of the Kugo-Ojima framework, whose physical states are $\ker Q/\operatorname{im}Q$ with $Q^{\dagger} = Q$, does not exist on them. Nilpotent charges that are not self-adjoint exist on positive spaces (their cohomology is computed with $Q$ and $Q^{*}$), so nothing here excludes covariant gauge fixing in every form; the general statement that a local covariant vector potential obeying Maxwell's equations needs an indefinite metric is Strocchi's theorem (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iii)); the check exhibits this for the charge of (ii), which is nilpotent and nonzero and fails $PQ = Q^{\mathsf T}P$ for the positive Gram matrix $P$.

\emph{(ii).} With $a_\mu = \partial/\partial z_\mu$ and positive adjoint $a_\mu^{*} = z_\mu$, the operator $(-1)^{n_0}$ is an involution that anticommutes with $z_0$ and commutes with $z_i$, so the Krein adjoint $a_\mu^{\dagger} = \eta a_\mu^{*}\eta$ is $-z_0$ for $\mu = 0$ and $z_i$ for $\mu = i$, that is $-g_{\mu\mu}z_\mu$. Hence $[a_\mu, a_\nu^{\dagger}] = -g_{\mu\nu}$, and for $a(u) = \sum_\mu g_{\mu\mu}u^\mu a_\mu$ one gets $[a(u), a(w)^{\dagger}] = -u\cdot w$, the Minkowski metric of the polarisations with a sign: the standard Gupta-Bleuler form, the same in any formalism. A boost rotor $R$ preserves $u\cdot w$, so this one-particle form is boost-invariant; the check confirms it for $R = \tfrac54 + \tfrac34\gamma_0\gamma_1$ ($R\tilde R = 1$) and shows the Euclidean form $\sum_\mu u^\mu w^\mu$ changes. On the ghost floor, $S = 1 - (b^{*} - d^{*})(b - d)$ is an element of the floor with $S^2 = 1$, $S^{*} = S$ and $SbS = d$ (checked), so $b^{\dagger} = Sb^{*}S = d^{*}$ and $(d^{*})^{\dagger} = b$. Bosons and ghosts commute. For $L = \sum_\mu g_{\mu\mu}k^\mu a_\mu$, $L^{\dagger} = -\sum_\mu k^\mu z_\mu$ and $[L, L^{\dagger}] = -Q(k) = 0$. Then
\[
Q^2 = L^{\dagger}L\,(bd^{*} + d^{*}b) + (L^{\dagger})^2b^2 + d^{*2}L^2 + [L, L^{\dagger}]\,d^{*}b = 0,
\]
since $b$ and $d^{*}$ anticommute, $b^2 = d^{*2} = 0$ and $k$ is null; and $Q^{\dagger} = b^{\dagger}L + L^{\dagger}d = d^{*}L + L^{\dagger}b = Q$, the bosonic and ghost factors commuting. The check confirms $Q^2 = 0$, $KQ = Q^{\mathsf T}K$ and $K = K^{\mathsf T}$ for the Krein Gram matrix $K = P\eta$ on the space with $T \le 3$ (which $Q$ preserves; in the truncation the factor that lowers $T$ is applied first), for $k = \gamma_0 + \gamma_3$ and $k = 5\gamma_0 + 3\gamma_1 + 4\gamma_2$.

\emph{(iii).} $Q$ commutes with $T = \deg + N_b + N_d$ and raises the ghost number $N_d - N_b$ by one. For each $T \le 3$ the check computes exactly the ranks of $Q$ from ghost number $-1$ to $0$ and from $0$ to $1$, so the dimension of the cohomology at ghost number zero, and the signature of the Krein form on $\ker Q$; the results are $\dim H = 1, 2, 3, 4$ and signature $(\dim H, 0, \dim\operatorname{im}Q)$ for both momenta. Since $Q$ is self-adjoint and nilpotent, $\operatorname{im}Q \subset \ker Q$ is orthogonal to $\ker Q$, so the form descends to the cohomology, where it is positive definite by the signature. The pattern $T + 1$ is the dimension of the degree-$T$ symmetric power of a two-dimensional space; that it continues for every $T$ is the Kugo-Ojima quartet mechanism (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(ii)), not computed here.

\emph{(iv).} At $T = 1$ and ghost number zero the space is spanned by the linear monomials $\epsilon\cdot z$; $Q(\epsilon\cdot z) = d^{*}L(\epsilon\cdot z)$ vanishes exactly when $k\cdot\epsilon = 0$, and the image of $Q$ from ghost number $-1$ is $L^{\dagger}$ applied to the ghost state, the monomial along $k$. So the one-particle cohomology is $k^{\perp}/\mathrm{span}\{k\}$, two-dimensional. For $\epsilon \in k^{\perp}$, $k\epsilon = k\wedge\epsilon$ is a bivector and $k(k\epsilon) = Q(k)\epsilon = 0$; $k\wedge\epsilon = 0$ exactly when $\epsilon$ is a multiple of $k$. So $\epsilon \mapsto k\epsilon$ induces an injective map from $k^{\perp}/\mathrm{span}\{k\}$ into $\{f : kf = 0\}$, which is two-dimensional (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.fock-space-maxwell-modes}(2), recomputed in the check as the kernel of $f \mapsto kf$ on the six bivectors), hence onto. The check confirms rank $2$ of the image and the dimension $2$ for three null momenta.

\emph{(v).} Write $T_a$ for the twelve anti-Hermitian generators of $\mathfrak{su}(2) \oplus \mathfrak{su}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{u}(1)$ on $\C^{2} \otimes \C^{3}$, the algebra of Theorem \claimref{standard-model.gauge-algebra-minimal-massive-composite} (a basis with Gaussian-rational entries; the structure constants $[T_a, T_b] = f_{ab}{}^{c}T_c$ are then rational and are computed exactly). Take $c^a = v_a$, $\bar c_a = w_a$ on twelve tower planes, so $\{c^a, \bar c_b\} = \delta^a_b$ and the $c$'s anticommute. With $Q = c^aT_a + G$, $G = -\tfrac12 f_{ab}{}^{c}c^ac^b\bar c_c$,
\[
Q^2 = \tfrac12 c^ac^b\,[T_a, T_b] + T_d\,\{c^d, G\} + G^2 ,
\]
since the matter factors commute with the ghosts. Moving $c^d$ through $c^ac^b$ costs no sign, so $\{c^d, c^ac^b\bar c_c\} = c^ac^b\{c^d, \bar c_c\} = \delta^d_c\,c^ac^b$ and $\{c^d, G\} = -\tfrac12 f_{ab}{}^{d}c^ac^b$. The first two terms therefore cancel exactly when $[T_a, T_b] = f_{ab}{}^{c}T_c$, and $G^2 = 0$ exactly when the $f$ satisfy the Jacobi identity (the standard computation of the BRST charge of a constraint algebra, valid for any Lie algebra and finite-dimensional representation; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(i)). The check does not rely on this expansion: it computes $Q^2$ as a matrix of elements of the twelve-plane floor, finding it zero; dropping $G$ leaves $\tfrac12 c^ac^bf_{ab}{}^{c}T_c \neq 0$, and changing one structure constant of $\mathfrak{su}(3)$ by one makes $Q^2 \neq 0$.

\emph{Reading.} By (i) the store's representations carry no self-adjoint BRST charge as they stand, and by (ii) to (iv) the Gupta-Bleuler form of the polarisations supplies the missing indefinite form in a boost-invariant way, with physical states that are positive and coincide at one particle with the stored photon modes; under the premise that gauge fields carry this indefinite form, Premise \claimref{synthesis.krein-form-premise-indefinite-inner-product-for-gauge-fields}, the covariant route works at the free level. An indefinite form already appears at the one-particle level of the attachment, the twistor form of signature $(2,2)$ whose positive polarisations alone carry states (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.positive-structure-is-twistor-form-at-imaginary-time}); that is a parallel, not the form used here, and nothing is computed from it. The ghosts in (ii) and (v) are tower modes, as the Grassmann variables of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.path-integral-inside-tower} are rungs, and they are spin-zero CAR modes; Proposition \claimref{field-theory.twistor-attachment} makes a CAR lift local only for odd $2s$ when the weights are positive, and the spacelike bracket of a spin-zero CAR field vanishes only at antiparticle weight $-1$, that is in the indefinite form (\claimref{synthesis.locality-of-the-attached-free-fields-fixes-their-statistics}); they appear only in the zero-norm quartets of (iii). The adjoint representation of the derived algebra is real, so the gauge fields need no complex unit beyond the field's $I_4$ (argued). Not computed: the field-level charge of the interacting theory, the alternative physical (Coulomb) gauge for non-abelian fields with its Gribov ambiguity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-brst-kugo-ojima-strocchi-and-gribov}(iv)), and confinement; the sign of the one-loop beta coefficients is computed in a result (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-running-coefficients-from-spacetime-algebra-spin-traces}).

synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-mass.formal:
Units $\hbar = c = 1$; $\Cl(1,3)$ with $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$; spinors acted on by left multiplication, the field theory's unit the right unit $\psi \mapsto \psi I_{4}$ (numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$); matrix forms are parenthetical readings. Let $N$ be a globally hyperbolic region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) with a time function $t$, $\mathcal{H}$ the solutions of the Dirac equation of mass $m \ge 0$ with the conserved current product $(\psi|\phi)$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimock-dirac-car-algebra-on-a-gravitational-field}), and $F \ge 0$ a weight in $t$ for which $\langle\psi|\phi\rangle_{F} = \int_{N}F\,\bar\psi\phi\,\mathrm{dvol}$ is bounded on $\mathcal{H}$, with $\bar\psi\phi$ read as $\langle e_{0}\tilde\psi\phi\rangle_{0}$ plus its unit part. Let $A_{F}$ be the self-adjoint operator with $(\psi|A_{F}\phi) = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle_{F}$, $\Pi_{F}$ the projection onto its kernel, and $\omega_{F}$ the gauge-invariant quasi-free state with one-particle projection $Q_{F} = \chi_{(0,\infty)}(A_{F})$: the Fewster-Lang weighted spin-product state (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fewster-lang-spin-product-states-of-the-dirac-field}), the finite-time form of the fermionic projector state. Let $\Gamma\psi = I_{4}\psi I_{4}$ (the matrix $\gamma_{5}$).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Chirality.)} $\Gamma$ is an involution commuting with the unit, minus the grade involution on the algebra, anticommuting with the left action of vectors and commuting with that of bivectors; the spin product is odd and the current even under it. Hence for $m = 0$, $\Gamma A_{F}\Gamma = -A_{F}$ and $Q_{F} + \Gamma Q_{F}\Gamma = 1 - \Pi_{F}$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Massless no-go.)} If $m = 0$ and $A_{F}$ is injective, $\omega_{F}$ is Hadamard on no open subset of $N$: Hadamard would give $C^{+} = C^{-}$ (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b)).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Homogeneous collars.)} On a flat slab, and for $m = 0$ on a spatially flat Robertson-Walker collar $\hb(b) = b/a(\eta)$ in conformal time (with the flat weight $Fa$), each momentum-helicity block is the two-level system $H = Ms_{3} + ks_{1}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard}, the spin-product density is $\partial H/\partial M = s_{3}$, $A_{F}$ restricted to a block is the weighted mean $\int Fa\,\tilde Us_{3}U\,d\eta$ of the turned density ($U = e^{-IH\eta}$), and $\omega_{F}$ is the pure state with Bloch vector $\hat A$. For constant $M$, with $\hat F(\lambda) = \int Fe^{I_{4}\lambda t}dt$ and $\omega^{2} = k^{2} + M^{2}$: $A\cdot\hat h = (M/\omega)\hat F(0)$, $|A|^{2} = (M/\omega)^{2}\hat F(0)^{2} + (k/\omega)^{2}|\hat F(2\omega)|^{2}$ and $1 - 2|\beta_{k}|^{2} = M\hat F(0)/(\omega|A|)$ against the vacuum. For $m = 0$, $A \perp \hat h = s_{1}$ for every weight, so $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = \tfrac12$ over the conformal vacuum wherever $\widehat{Fa}(2k) \ne 0$; for every nonzero compactly supported weight this is every momentum off a null set, $A_{F}$ is injective and (ii) applies; the energy density over the conformal vacuum diverges.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Massive slab.)} For the sharp slab of length $T$, along $\omega T = (n + \tfrac12)\pi$, $|\beta_{k}|^{2} \to \tfrac12(1 - MT(1 + M^{2}T^{2})^{-1/2})$ ($\tfrac15$ at $MT = \tfrac34$), so the state is not Hadamard; for smooth compactly supported weights $|\beta_{k}|^{2} \le k^{2}|\hat F(2\omega)|^{2}/(4M^{2}\hat F(0)^{2})$ at large $k$, rapidly decreasing, and these states are Hadamard (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fewster-lang-spin-product-states-of-the-dirac-field}, \cite[Thms 3.4, 3.5]{FewsterLang2015}, proved there for ultrastatic slabs with compact spatial sections; carried to the flat slab mode by mode, argued).
\item[(v)] \emph{(The deposit.)} So the selection by the Dirac field's own spin product gives no Hadamard state for the massless Dirac field on any collar of the descent with injective $A_{F}$ (on the radiation-type collar, for every compactly supported weight), and for massive fields only with a smooth weight, which the form does not fix: it does not supply the occupation profile that the premise (HD) leaves free (Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise}). The massless no-go holds with torsion as well: with $\Omega$ independent of $\hb$ (the definition's Einstein-Cartan choice) the connection term of the Dirac operator is a vector plus a trivector, both odd, so $\Gamma$ still anticommutes with it. The twistor form, by contrast, selects the attachment's vacuum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z}), the conformal vacuum on a Weyl-flat collar, which is Hadamard there.
\end{enumerate}
Status: (i) proved; (ii) proved given the Fact and the invariance of wave-front sets under bundle isomorphisms (cited from memory); (iii) proved and computed, the energy-density statement argued; (iv) computed, its Hadamard conclusions imported from Fewster and Lang; (v) argued. Standard: the mode form and the massive conclusions. Transport-absent.
synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-mass.technical:
The premise (HD) leaves free which state the descent deposits; only its short-distance tail is fixed. One way the series might fix it without new input is through the Dirac field's own indefinite form, the spin product $\bar\psi\phi$ integrated over a collar of the descent. Split against the positive conserved current, this form singles out a state: the positive part of the operator it defines is the filled one-particle space. This is the weighted spin-product state of Fewster and Lang, the finite-time form of the fermionic projector state of Finster and Reintjes and the Dirac analogue of the Sorkin-Johnston state; Fewster and Lang showed, for massive fields on static slabs with compact spatial sections, that the sharp collar gives a state that is not Hadamard and that smoothing the collar's edges in time gives Hadamard states.

The result settles the massless case, which is the case of the radiation-type collar. The chirality, which in the spacetime algebra is left multiplication by $I_{4}$ composed with the unit (minus the grade involution), preserves the massless field equation and the current but reverses the spin product, because the spin product carries one factor $e_{0}$ and the current two. So the chirality exchanges the positive and negative parts of the spin-product operator: the selected state and its chirality image fill complementary spaces. A Hadamard state cannot do this, because the chirality is a smooth pointwise map and would carry the positive-frequency singularity onto the negative-frequency one. Mode by mode on a Weyl-flat Robertson-Walker collar this is visible directly: each momentum block is a two-level system, the spin-product density is $s_{3}$, the operator is the weighted average of $s_{3}$ turned about the energy axis, and for zero mass every turned copy is perpendicular to the energy axis, so the selected state is at right angles to the conformal vacuum in every block, an occupation of one half at every momentum, whatever the weight. For massive fields the same formula reproduces the Fewster-Lang mixing angle; the sharp collar leaves an occupation that does not fall off, smooth weights give a rapidly falling one.

So the Dirac field's own indefinite form does not supply the deposit that (HD) assumes: for massless fields it never gives a Hadamard state, and for massive fields it does so only after a smoothing that the form does not choose. The twistor form on the conformal spinors does better: its positive part is the attachment's vacuum, the conformal vacuum on a Weyl-flat collar, which is Hadamard. (HD) remains a premise.
synthesis.spin-product-state-of-the-mass.lay: Quantum fields need a well-behaved state, one that looks like empty space at very short distances. The series' account of the earliest universe leaves its fields in some state but does not say which, so it is assumed to be well behaved. One natural way to pick a state using only the electron field's own structure is to split its solutions with a mixed-sign quantity built from the field, the one that gives an electron its mass term, averaged over a slice of time. This result shows that for massless particles, which is how all particles behave at the universe's start, that split always picks a badly behaved state: the quantity changes sign under the swap of left- and right-handed particles, which forces the chosen state to be half filled at every energy. For massive particles it works only if the time slice is given soft edges, a choice the method does not make. A different mixed-sign quantity, from the series' twistor picture, does pick a well-behaved state.

proofs.main:
\emph{Conventions.} Units $\hbar = c = 1$; $\Cl(1,3)$ with $e_{0}^{2} = 1$, $e_{i}^{2} = -1$, $I_{4} = e_{0}e_{1}e_{2}e_{3}$. Spinors are acted on by left multiplication, and the field theory's unit is the right unit $\psi \mapsto \psi I_{4}$ (the store's convention for Dirac lines). Matrix forms are parenthetical readings. The real part of the Dirac adjoint pairing is $s(\psi, \phi) = \langle e_{0}\tilde\psi\phi\rangle_{0}$ (the reading of $\mathrm{Re}\,\bar\psi\phi$) and the real part of the current pairing is $h(\psi, \phi) = \langle e_{0}\tilde\psi e_{0}\phi\rangle_{0}$ (the reading of $\mathrm{Re}\,\psi^{\dagger}\phi$); the complex forms are recovered from the real parts with the right unit. The check verifies on all $16 \times 16$ pairs of basis blades of $\Cl(1,3)$, used as the module (complete by bilinearity, and inherited by every left ideal closed under the maps below), that $h$ is symmetric and positive on the basis and that every vector $e_{\mu}$ acting on the left is symmetric for $s$ (the Dirac adjoint property $\bar\gamma_{\mu} = \gamma_{\mu}$).

\emph{Set-up.} Let $N$ be a globally hyperbolic region of a gravitational field $(\hb, \Omega)$ (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) with a time function $t$, and let $\mathcal{H}$ be the space of solutions of the Dirac equation of mass $m \ge 0$ with the conserved current product $(\psi|\phi)$, the one-particle space of the CAR algebra (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-dimock-dirac-car-algebra-on-a-gravitational-field}). For a weight $F \ge 0$, a function of $t$, put $\langle\psi|\phi\rangle_{F} = \int_{N}F\,\bar\psi\phi\,\mathrm{dvol}$ and suppose it bounded on $\mathcal{H}$ (it is on the collars of (iii), (iv) and on the ultrastatic slabs of \cite{FewsterLang2015}); $A_{F}$ is the bounded self-adjoint operator with $(\psi|A_{F}\phi) = \langle\psi|\phi\rangle_{F}$, $Q_{F} = \chi_{(0,\infty)}(A_{F})$ and $\Pi_{F}$ the projection onto $\ker A_{F}$. The spin-product state $\omega_{F}$ is the gauge-invariant quasi-free state whose two-point function $\omega_{F}(\Psi(f)\bar\Psi(h))$ is the pairing of $Sh$ with $Q_{F}Sf$ ($S$ the causal propagator) and whose other ordering carries $1 - Q_{F}$. This is the weighted spin-product state of Fewster and Lang (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-fewster-lang-spin-product-states-of-the-dirac-field}; \cite{FewsterLang2015}, Sec. 3), the finite-time form of the fermionic projector state of Finster and Reintjes, whose construction on a whole spacetime uses a family of masses and does not exist at $m = 0$ ($F$ the characteristic function of the collar gives their unsoftened state, $F$ smooth with compact support their softened ones); it is the Dirac analogue of the Sorkin-Johnston state.

\emph{(i) Chirality.} Let $\Gamma\psi = I_{4}\psi I_{4}$, left multiplication by $I_{4}$ (the matrix $\gamma_{0}\gamma_{1}\gamma_{2}\gamma_{3}$) composed with the unit, the right multiplication by $I_{4}$: the matrix $\gamma_{5}$. Left and right multiplication commute, so $\Gamma^{2}\psi = I_{4}^{2}\psi I_{4}^{2} = \psi$ and $\Gamma$ commutes with the right unit; on the whole algebra $\Gamma$ is minus the grade involution (checked), since $I_{4}$ commutes with even and anticommutes with odd elements. Because $I_{4}$ anticommutes with every vector and commutes with every bivector, $\Gamma(e_{\mu}\psi) = -e_{\mu}\Gamma\psi$ and $\Gamma(B\psi) = B\Gamma\psi$ for bivectors $B$ (checked on all basis elements). With torsion ($\Omega$ independent of $\hb$, the definition's Einstein-Cartan choice) the connection term of the Dirac operator, $\hb(\partial_{a})$ acting with $\Omega(a)$, is a vector plus a trivector, both odd, so $\Gamma$ anticommutes with it too and (i), (ii) hold on every gravitational field of the definition. The Dirac operator on $(\hb, \Omega)$ is the left action of the vector derivative $\hb(\partial)$ plus the connection, a bivector acting on the left, so $\Gamma$ anticommutes with it; the massless equation is therefore $\Gamma$-invariant, while the massive one, whose mass term is the right unit times $m$ against a left vector, is not (checked: $\Gamma$ does not commute with left $e_{0}$). Under $\Gamma$ on both arguments, $s$ changes sign and $h$ is unchanged (checked on all pairs): in $s$ one factor $e_{0}$ meets the grade involution, in $h$ two do. So for $m = 0$, $\Gamma$ is a unitary involution of $\mathcal{H}$ with $\Gamma A_{F}\Gamma = -A_{F}$. Hence $\Gamma$ maps the spectral subspace of $A_{F}$ for $(0, \infty)$ onto that for $(-\infty, 0)$ and preserves $\ker A_{F}$, which is the identity $Q_{F} + \Gamma Q_{F}\Gamma = 1 - \Pi_{F}$. (Proved.)

\emph{(ii) No massless spin-product state is Hadamard.} Let $m = 0$ and $\Pi_{F} = 0$. The causal propagator obeys $S\Gamma = -\Gamma S$ on test sections: with $D$ the massless Dirac operator, $D\Gamma = -\Gamma D$, so $\Gamma S_{\mathrm{ret}}\Gamma$ is a retarded fundamental solution of $-D$ and equals $-S_{\mathrm{ret}}$ by uniqueness, and likewise for the advanced one. So $(Sh|\Gamma Q_{F}\Gamma Sf) = (S\Gamma h|Q_{F}S\Gamma f)$, the two signs cancelling: the two-point function of $\Gamma Q_{F}\Gamma = 1 - Q_{F}$ is that of $Q_{F}$ with both arguments transformed by the smooth bundle isomorphism $\Gamma$ over the identity map. Hence $\mathcal{G}^{(-)}_{\omega_{F}}$ is $\mathcal{G}^{(+)}_{\omega_{F}}$ composed with $\Gamma \times \Gamma$, and a bundle isomorphism over the identity of the base does not change a wave-front set (standard, cited from memory as \cite[Thm.~8.2.4]{Hormander1983} for the pullback by the identity map, the fibre maps being smooth and invertible). If $\omega_{F}$ were Hadamard on an open set $O \subset N$, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b) would give $\mathrm{WF}'(\mathcal{G}^{(+)}) = C^{+}$ and $\mathrm{WF}'(\mathcal{G}^{(-)}) = C^{-}$ over $O \times O$, so $C^{+} = C^{-}$ there; but these sets are disjoint and nonempty (each contains $(x, \xi; x, \xi)$ with $\xi$ null and future-, respectively past-directed). So $\omega_{F}$ is Hadamard on no open subset of $N$. (Proved, given the Fact and the cited invariance.) Without $\Pi_{F} = 0$ the same argument shows that a Hadamard $\omega_{F}$ would need the kernel projection $\Pi_{F}$ to carry the whole singularity of the causal propagator.

\emph{(iii) Homogeneous collars.} On a flat slab, and for $m = 0$ on a spatially flat Robertson-Walker collar $\hb(b) = b/a(\eta)$ in conformal time, the field splits into momentum-helicity blocks. Each block is the stored two-level system $Iu' = Hu$, $H = Ms_{3} + ks_{1}$, $M = ma$, in the Pauli algebra with the unit $I = s_{1}s_{2}s_{3}$ (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.massive-dirac-instantaneous-vacuum-and-non-smooth-descents-are-not-hadamard}, formal statement), with the current product the Hermitian product of two-component spinors over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I\}$, adjoint the reversion. The mass term of the Dirac Hamiltonian is $m\bar\psi\psi$, so the spin-product density of a block is $\partial H/\partial M = s_{3}$ (Hellmann-Feynman reading; checked: $H$ is linear in $M$ with that slope). For $m = 0$ on the Robertson-Walker collar, $\psi = a^{-3/2}\chi$ with $\chi$ a flat massless solution and the current product preserved (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-conformal-covariance-of-massless-fields-and-local-conformal-flatness}(b); Theorem \claimref{synthesis.deposit-over-the-conformal-vacuum-is-hadamard-exactly-when-every-occupation-moment-is-finite}), and $\bar\psi\phi\,\mathrm{dvol} = a^{-3}\bar\chi\chi'\,a^{4}\,d\eta\,d^{3}x$ (exponent $-\tfrac32 - \tfrac32 + 4 = 1$, checked), so the collar's weight is the flat weight $Fa$. With $U(\eta) = e^{-IH\eta}$ for constant $H$,
\[
A_{F}\big|_{\mathrm{block}} \;=\; \int F(\eta)a(\eta)\,\tilde U(\eta)\,s_{3}\,U(\eta)\,d\eta,
\]
a vector of the Pauli algebra (the operator $\vec A\cdot\vec\sigma$), whose square is the scalar $|A|^{2}$; its positive spectral projection is $\tfrac12(1 + \hat A)$, the pure state with Bloch vector $\hat A = A/|A|$. The conformal vacuum (on the slab, the vacuum) is the positive-frequency projection $\tfrac12(1 + \hat h)$, $\hat h = (ks_{1} + Ms_{3})/\omega$, $\omega = (k^{2} + M^{2})^{1/2}$, and the Bogoliubov coefficient between the two pure states is $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = \tfrac12(1 - \hat A\cdot\hat h)$ as in that theorem. The rotor $U$ turns $s_{3}$ about $\hat h$ through the angle $2\omega\eta$: the part $(s_{3}\cdot\hat h)\hat h = (M/\omega)\hat h$ is fixed and the perpendicular part, of length $k/\omega$, turns (checked with exact rational rotors $c - I\hat h s$, $c^{2} + s^{2} = 1$, on Pythagorean $(k, M, \omega)$ and weighted sums of up to seven turns). With $\hat F(\lambda) = \int F e^{I_{4}\lambda t}dt$ for the flat weight,
\[
A\cdot\hat h = \frac{M}{\omega}\hat F(0), \qquad |A|^{2} = \Xi^{2} = \frac{M^{2}}{\omega^{2}}\hat F(0)^{2} + \frac{k^{2}}{\omega^{2}}|\hat F(2\omega)|^{2}, \qquad 1 - 2|\beta_{k}|^{2} = \frac{M\hat F(0)}{\omega\,\Xi},
\]
which is the mixing angle $\cos 2\theta = \hat F(0)m/(\lambda\Xi)$ of \cite{FewsterLang2015} (standard, recomputed here; the check verifies the two identities exactly for discrete weights $\sum_{j}w_{j}\delta(\eta - \eta_{j})$, to which the integral is linear). For $m = 0$: $\hat h = s_{1}$, and $\tilde U s_{3}U = \cos(2k\eta)s_{3} + \sin(2k\eta)s_{2}$ has no $s_{1}$ part, so $A \perp \hat h$ for every weight: wherever $\widehat{Fa}(2k) \ne 0$ the spin-product state's Bloch vector is perpendicular to the conformal vacuum's and $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = \tfrac12$ (checked, including weights $F a$ with $a = \eta$). The block chirality is $s_{1}$ (it commutes with $H = ks_{1}$ and anticommutes with $s_{3}$, checked), $s_{1}As_{1} = -A$ and $Q + s_{1}Qs_{1} = 1$ (checked), the block form of (i). If $F$ has compact support in $\eta$ and is not zero, $\widehat{Fa}$ is entire and $\widehat{Fa}(0) = \int Fa > 0$, so its zeros are isolated and the blocks with $A = 0$ lie on finitely many spheres in every bounded set of momenta, a null set: $\Pi_{F} = 0$, and (ii) applies. Directly: the energy of a block above the vacuum is $\omega(1 - \hat A\cdot\hat h) = 2\omega|\beta_{k}|^{2} = k$, so the expected energy density over the conformal vacuum is $a^{-4}$ times a multiple of $\int k\,d^{3}k$, divergent at every point, which no Hadamard state has (argued; this is the route of the massive-Dirac theorem). (Proved; the energy statement argued.)

\emph{(iv) Massive flat slab.} For the characteristic function of $(-T/2, T/2)$, $\hat F(0) = T$ and $\hat F(2\omega) = \sin(\omega T)/\omega$. On the momenta with $\omega T = (n + \tfrac12)\pi$, $(1 - 2|\beta_{k}|^{2})^{2} = M^{2}T^{2}\omega^{2}/(M^{2}T^{2}\omega^{2} + k^{2})$, which decreases to $M^{2}T^{2}/(M^{2}T^{2} + 1)$ as $k \to \infty$; at $MT = \tfrac34$ the limit is $\tfrac{9}{25}$ and $|\beta_{k}|^{2} \to \tfrac15$, and for $k \ge 3M$ already $|\beta_{k}|^{2} \ge \tfrac12(1 - 2^{-1/2})$ (checked exactly on the rational expression). The same lower bound holds on intervals of momenta around these points of fixed width in $\omega$, so the relative energy density diverges and the unsoftened state is not Hadamard, in agreement with \cite[Thm.~3.4]{FewsterLang2015}, which is proved for ultrastatic slabs with compact spatial sections; on the flat slab the mode-wise statement is the one computed here (computed and argued; standard). For a weight $F$ smooth with compact support, $1 - (1 + x)^{-1/2} \le x/2$ for $0 \le x \le 3$, from the polynomial identity $(1 + x)(1 - \tfrac{x}{2})^{2} = 1 - \tfrac34x^{2} + \tfrac14x^{3}$ (checked), gives, with $x = (1 - 2|\beta_{k}|^{2})^{-2} - 1 = k^{2}|\hat F(2\omega)|^{2}/(M^{2}\hat F(0)^{2})$, the bound $|\beta_{k}|^{2} = \tfrac12(1 - (1 + x)^{-1/2}) \le x/4 = k^{2}|\hat F(2\omega)|^{2}/(4M^{2}\hat F(0)^{2})$ once $x \le 3$, which holds at large $k$; $\hat F$ decreases faster than any power, so $|\beta_{k}|^{2}$ does, and the softened states are Hadamard by \cite[Thm.~3.5]{FewsterLang2015} (imported, not re-proved; proved there for compact spatial sections and carried to the flat slab mode by mode, argued; the bound is the mode-wise reason). At $m = 0$ the bound is void ($\hat F(0)M = 0$), as (iii) requires.

\emph{(v) The deposit.} (HD) (Premise \claimref{synthesis.hadamard-deposit-premise}) asks that the deposit be Hadamard on some Cauchy collar of the descent, with the occupation profile over an admissible reference vacuum free. The spin-product prescription is the one selection built only from the Dirac field's own indefinite form, its conserved current and a collar; by (ii) and (iii) it gives, for the massless Dirac field, a state that is Hadamard on no open subset of any collar for which $A_{F}$ is injective, every compactly supported weight on the radiation-type collar included, with occupation $\tfrac12$ above the conformal vacuum; by (iv) for massive fields it gives (HD) only for smooth weights, a choice the form does not make. So it does not supply the occupation profile, and (HD) is not derived by it (argued, from (ii) to (iv)). The contrast: the twistor form on the conformal spinors is graded by $Z = e_{0}\nu$ against the Hilbert form, and its positive part selects the attachment's Fock vacuum (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.attachment-conformal-energy-is-generated-by-z}), on a Weyl-flat collar the conformal vacuum, which is Hadamard there; so of the two indefinite forms on massless Dirac spinors, the conformal one selects a Hadamard state and the spacetime one does not.

\emph{Status.} (i) proved; (ii) proved given Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-microlocal-hadamard-condition}(b) and the invariance of wave-front sets under bundle isomorphisms (cited from memory); (iii) proved and computed, the energy-density reading argued; (iv) computed, the Hadamard conclusions those of \cite{FewsterLang2015} (Thms 3.4, 3.5); (v) argued. Standard: the per-mode form of the fermionic projector state and the massive conclusions (Fewster and Lang). New: the chirality identity (i), the massless no-go (ii) and (iii) on every collar and for every weight (Fewster and Lang treat $m > 0$ only), the geometric reading of the state as the normalised weighted mean of the turned spin-product density $s_{3}$, and the consequence (v) for (HD). Transport-absent: nothing in the result uses the transport; the spacetime algebra form (the chirality as left times right $I_{4}$, minus the grade involution) is convenient.

synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-cha.formal:
Let $H_{4} = \sum_{b}K(n_{a} + n_{c}) - G\,P^{*}P$, $P = \sum_{b}w_{a}w_{c}$, be the pairing element of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2) on a floor with $n_{b}$ blocks, $K \ge 0$, $G > 0$, acting on the Fock space of its $2n_{b}$ tower modes (the tower planes generate the CAR, Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Closed spectrum.)} $H_{4}$ conserves $N_{a}$ and $N_{c}$. In the sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$ its eigenvalues are exactly the numbers $K(2p + s_{a} + s_{c}) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$, where $s_{a}$ blocks hold $a$ alone, $s_{c}$ blocks hold $c$ alone, $p = N_{a} - s_{a} = N_{c} - s_{c}$ pairs occupy the remaining $\Omega = n_{b} - s_{a} - s_{c}$ blocks, $j_{z} = p - \Omega/2$, and $j \in \{\Omega/2, \Omega/2 - 1, \dots\}$ with $j \ge |j_{z}|$. The stored pair band $2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1)$ is $s_{a} = s_{c} = 0$, $j = n_{b}/2$, and is the lowest level of the sector $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Gap at fixed numbers.)} For $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$ with $0 < n < n_{b}$, the next level lies exactly $Gn_{b}$ above the band level, for every $K$ and $n$: breaking one pair, or lowering the quasi-spin by one, costs $Gn_{b}$, and no level lies between. This level is the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold; the uniform scalar channel $P + P^{*}$ moves only along the band and does not reach it.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Twice the quasiparticle energy.)} Above the threshold $G > 2K/n_{b}$ the one-shell mean-field energy $n_{b}(K - E) + \Delta^{2}/G$, $E^{2} = K^{2} + \Delta^{2}$, is stationary and convex exactly at $E = Gn_{b}/2$, the gap equation, so the exact gap of (ii) is $Gn_{b} = 2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}}$ with $\Delta$ the mean-field fermion mass: the pair-breaking threshold sits at twice the quasiparticle energy, at least $2\Delta$, and at exactly $2\Delta$ when $K = 0$, the floor analogue of Nambu's relation $m_{\sigma} = 2m$.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Reading the rung field as such a composite.)} If the rung field's neutral mode is read as a tower composite of one fermion species of mean-field mass $m_{f} = \Delta$, lying at or above the pair-breaking threshold, then $m_{h} \ge 2m_{f}$ at this level. With the measured $m_{h}$ this needs $m_{f} < 63$ GeV, and with the tree value $m_{h} = M_{Z}$ of the D-term action (Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}) $m_{f} < 46$ GeV; both exclude the top quark as sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell), since $2m_{t}$ exceeds both. Composites of several species, or mixing between condensates, are not excluded.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-cha.technical:
The stored composite scalars of the tower are built at mean field. Beyond mean field the pairing element on a floor is the degenerate pairing model, whose exact spectrum is the quasi-spin spectrum: in each sector of fixed numbers $N_{a}, N_{c}$ the levels are $K(2p + s) - G(j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$, with $s$ singly occupied blocks, $p$ pairs on the others, quasi-spin $j$ and projection $j_{z}$. At equal numbers the band of the stored result is the lowest level and the next lies exactly $Gn_{b}$ above it: the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold, which the uniform scalar channel does not reach on a floor.

The mean-field gap equation puts the quasiparticle energy at $E = Gn_{b}/2$, so the exact gap is $2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}}$, at least twice the fermion mass $\Delta$: by analogy, the floor form of Nambu's relation $m_{\sigma} = 2m$. If the Higgs boson is read as a composite of one species lying at or above this threshold, that species must be lighter than $m_{h}/2$, about $63$ GeV, or $M_{Z}/2$ at the tree level of the D-term action, which excludes the top quark as sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell). Light composites from several condensates, as in two-condensate models of top and bottom pairing, are not covered.
synthesis.tower-pairing-gap-at-fixed-cha.lay:
In this framework a scalar particle can arise as a bound pair of fermions, but so far only in an averaged approximation. This result solves the underlying model exactly on finite pieces of it. The lowest way to disturb the paired state without changing the particle numbers is to break one pair, and that costs exactly twice the energy of one dressed fermion, as the averaged treatment predicts.

By analogy with the known relation for such models, a composite scalar of this kind would weigh at least twice its constituents. If the Higgs boson were such a pair of a single kind of fermion, those fermions would have to be lighter than half its mass, about 63 GeV. The top quark is far heavier, so in this simple setting the Higgs cannot be a pair of top quarks alone, in line with the known difficulty of top-quark condensation; pairs mixing several kinds of fermion are not ruled out.

proofs.main:
\emph{(i).} The element is that of Proposition \claimref{field-theory.composite-scalars-mean-field-level}(2), on the Fock space of the floor's tower modes, which generate the CAR (Fact \claimref{field-theory.imported-tower-limit}). $H_{4}$ is a sum of number operators and of $P^{*}P = \sum_{b,b'}v_{c}(b)v_{a}(b)w_{a}(b')w_{c}(b')$ (with $v$ creating, as in the stored check), which moves a complete pair from block $b'$ to block $b$; so it conserves $N_{a}$ and $N_{c}$, and it annihilates any state in which block $b'$ holds $a$ or $c$ alone, while such a block cannot receive a pair. A block holding one particle alone is therefore inert for the pairing term and contributes $K$. On the remaining $\Omega$ blocks, each empty or paired, the operators $P$, $P^{*}$ and $p - \Omega/2$ close on $\mathfrak{su}(2)$: with $J_{+} = P^{*}$, $J_{-} = P$ restricted to these blocks and $J_{z} = p - \Omega/2$, each block is a quasi-spin $\tfrac12$ (Proposition \claimref{field-theory.how-close-tower-comes-ccr} is the same algebra on a whole floor), and $P^{*}P = J_{+}J_{-} = J^{2} - J_{z}^{2} + J_{z} = (j + j_{z})(j - j_{z} + 1)$ on total quasi-spin $j$, with $j_{z}$ the eigenvalue of $J_{z}$. The total quasi-spin of $\Omega$ spins $\tfrac12$ takes the values $\Omega/2, \Omega/2 - 1, \dots$, and the kinetic term is $K$ times the particle number $2p + s_{a} + s_{c}$. This is the quasi-spin (seniority) solution of the degenerate pairing model (Kerman, 1961; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(i)). The check does not rely on it: it builds $H_{4}$ on the full Fock space of the $n_{b} = 2, 3$ floors with GA's exterior model of the CAR (creation by wedge, annihilation by contraction), and in every sector $(N_{a}, N_{c})$, at eight couples $(K, G)$ including $K = 0$ and couplings on both sides of the threshold, verifies exactly that the product of $H_{4} - E$ over the predicted values vanishes on the sector (every eigenvalue is predicted) and that the product over all but one predicted value does not (every predicted value occurs), and that the lowest predicted value at $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$ is the stored band value. For $G > 0$ the energy decreases with $j$ at fixed $j_{z}$, so the band ($j = n_{b}/2$, no inert block) is the lowest level of its sector; a blocked pair of blocks lowers the available quasi-spin by one, as does a lower $j$, and higher seniorities cost more.

\emph{(ii).} At $N_{a} = N_{c} = n$, $0 < n < n_{b}$, the band level is $2Kn - Gn(n_{b} - n + 1)$. The next candidates have the same particle number and quasi-spin lowered by one: either $s_{a} = s_{c} = 1$ with $n - 1$ pairs on $n_{b} - 2$ blocks at top quasi-spin, or no inert block and $j = n_{b}/2 - 1$; both give $2Kn - G(n - 1)(n_{b} - n)$. The difference is $G[n(n_{b} - n + 1) - (n - 1)(n_{b} - n)] = Gn_{b}$, independent of $n$ and $K$. By (i) no other value lies between (the check confirms the two lowest predicted values differ by exactly $Gn_{b}$ in every such sector and that both occur).

\emph{(iii).} The one-shell mean-field energy of the stored result is $f(x) = n_{b}(K - \sqrt{K^{2} + x}) + x/G$ with $x = \Delta^{2}$; $f'(x) = -n_{b}/(2\sqrt{K^{2} + x}) + 1/G$ vanishes exactly at $\sqrt{K^{2} + x} = Gn_{b}/2$, which is positive-$x$ exactly when $G > 2K/n_{b}$ (the stored threshold), and $f''(x) = n_{b}/(4(K^{2} + x)^{3/2}) > 0$. So the mean-field quasiparticle energy is $E = Gn_{b}/2$ and $Gn_{b} = 2E = 2\sqrt{K^{2} + \Delta^{2}} \ge 2\Delta$, with equality exactly at $K = 0$, $\Delta$ being the mean-field fermion mass. Checked exactly at four above-threshold samples with rational $E$ and $\Delta$, one with $K = 0$. On a single shell the uniform scalar channel $P + P^{*}$ moves only along the band, so the level at $2E$ is the pair-breaking (two-quasiparticle) threshold and is not reached by the composite-scalar operator on a floor. Its relation to the amplitude mode of the relativistic model, where many shells are present and the bound state sits at $2m$ (Nambu and Jona-Lasinio; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(ii)), is an analogy (argued): the threshold is the floor's counterpart of the energy at which that mode sits, not the mode itself.

\emph{(iv).} Under the reading stated, with the neutral mode at or above the pair-breaking threshold, $m_{h} \ge 2E \ge 2m_{f}$, $m_{f} = \Delta$ the constituent's mean-field mass. The stored $m_{h} = 125.20$ GeV gives $m_{f} \le 62.6$ GeV and the stored $M_{Z} = 91.188$ GeV, the tree value of $m_{h}$ in Theorem \claimref{synthesis.rung-field-d-term-action-and-tree-masses-on-the-lift-locus}, gives $m_{f} \le 45.6$ GeV; the stored $m_{t} = 172.57$ GeV exceeds both bounds (checked exactly), so the top quark is excluded as the sole constituent at this level (one species, single shell). For comparison (outside; Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-quasi-spin-pairing-and-top-condensation}(iii), arXiv 1906.09579, which cites the large-$N_{c}$ result): in the minimal top-condensation model the composite Higgs has $m_{\chi} = 2m_{t}$ at large $N_{c}$ and about $\sqrt{2}\,m_{t}$ with gauge and Higgs corrections, both too large. The same paper obtains its own light composite Higgs, about $125$ GeV, from two condensates (mostly bottom-antibottom with a top admixture, through axial $U(1)$ breaking), which is the several-species case left open here. The floor result supplies the analogue of the first relation inside the series. Limits of the reading: the rung field is a doublet with a charged pair, the composite here a single complex scalar of one shell; colour, gauge corrections and the running between the cutoff and the weak scale are absent; the bound concerns a composite of one species, and a composite of several species, or mixing between condensates, is not excluded by this computation.

synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.formal:
Work in $\Cl(1,3)$ with the vectors $\gamma_{\mu}$ as Dirac matrices, the unit of the Feynman rules the right unit $x \mapsto xI_{4}$, a coefficient outside the Clifford product (Proposition \claimref{synthesis.one-loop-qed-in-the-spacetime-algebra}(5); numbers read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$), and the chirality $\gamma_{5}$ acting as $x \mapsto I_{4}xI_{4}$, $I_{4}$ inside the product on the left and that unit on the right, so $\mathrm{Tr}\,X = 4\langle X\rangle_{0}$. Write $S(p) = (p + M)/(Q(p) - M^{2})$. For momenta $k_{1}$, $k_{2}$, $q = k_{1} + k_{2}$ let
\[
D_{1}(\ell) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(\ell)\gamma^{\nu}S(\ell - k_{1})\gamma^{\rho}S(\ell - q)], \quad D_{2}(\ell) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(\ell)\gamma^{\rho}S(\ell - k_{2})\gamma^{\nu}S(\ell - q)],
\]
$P_{1}$, $P_{2}$ the same with $\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}$ replaced by $\gamma_{5}$, and regulate with the Pauli-Villars fields of Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-one-loop-integrals-and-pauli-villars-regulators}(iii) on the fermion loop, weights $c_{i}$ with $\sum_{i}c_{i} = 0$ ($c_{0} = 1$, $M_{0} = m$), $T^{\mu\nu\rho} = \sum_{i}c_{i}\int\frac{d^{4}\ell}{(2\pi)^{4}}(D_{1} + D_{2})|_{M = M_{i}}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] (Trace.) $\mathrm{Tr}(\gamma_{5}abcd) = 4\langle I_{4}abcd\rangle_{0}\,I_{4} = -4\lambda I_{4}$, where $a\wedge b\wedge c\wedge d = \lambda I_{4}$; it is real up to the unit and totally antisymmetric.
\item[(ii)] (Vector Ward identities.) For every $\ell$ and mass, $k_{1\nu}(D_{1} + D_{2})(\ell) = B(\ell - k_{1}) - B(\ell)$ with $B(p) = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}\gamma_{5}S(p)\gamma^{\rho}S(p - k_{2})]$, and likewise for $k_{2\rho}$. The pseudoscalar part of the numerator of $B$ does not depend on the mass and is odd about the centre of the loop, and $\sum_{i}c_{i}/((Q(\ell) - M_{i}^{2})(Q(\ell - k) - M_{i}^{2})) = O(|\ell|^{-6})$ exactly when $\sum_{i}c_{i} = 0$; so the regulated shift difference integrates to zero and $k_{1\nu}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = k_{2\rho}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = 0$.
\item[(iii)] (Axial divergence.) For every $\ell$, $q_{\mu}(D_{1} + D_{2}) = -2M(P_{1} + P_{2})$ plus four two-point terms of the kind in (ii), which integrate to zero under the regulators. The numerator of $P_{1}$ and of $P_{2}$ over its three denominators is $M \cdot 4\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}\,I_{4}$, independent of $\ell$. With the imported integral $\int\frac{d^{4}\ell}{(2\pi)^{4}}(\ell^{2} - \Delta)^{-3} = -I_{4}/(32\pi^{2}\Delta)$ and $M_{i} \to \infty$ for $i \geq 1$, at $m = 0$
\[
q_{\mu}T^{\mu\nu\rho} = \frac{1}{2\pi^{2}}\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0},
\]
which depends on the regulators only through $\sum_{i \geq 1}c_{i} = -1$. In the index reading the right side is $\pm\tfrac{1}{2\pi^{2}}\epsilon^{\nu\rho\alpha\beta}k_{1\alpha}k_{2\beta}$, the sign fixed by the orientation convention of $\epsilon$.
\item[(iv)] (Field form.) For polarisations $a_{1}$, $a_{2}$, $\langle I_{4}a_{1}k_{1}a_{2}k_{2}\rangle_{0} = \langle I_{4}f_{1}f_{2}\rangle_{0}$ with the plane-wave field-strength bivectors $f_{j} = a_{j} \wedge k_{j}$, symmetric in the two photons; it is the bilinear form of $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0}$, and for $F = E + I_{4}B$ ($E$, $B$ relative vectors) $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -2E\cdot B$.
\item[(v)] (Chiral fields.) With $P_{L,R} = \tfrac12(1 \mp \gamma_{5})$, $\mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}P_{L}a\gamma^{\nu}P_{L}b\gamma^{\rho}P_{L}c] = \mathrm{Tr}[\gamma^{\mu}a\gamma^{\nu}b\gamma^{\rho}cP_{R}]$, half the vector trace plus half the $\gamma_{5}$ trace, so a Weyl loop carries half the Dirac axial term with the sign of its chirality. For left-handed Weyl fields in a representation of a gauge algebra the anomalous part of the three-current triangle is proportional to the symmetric tensor $d(X, Y, Z) = \mathrm{tr}(X\{Y, Z\})$. The projector identity is proved; the reduction to $d$ is argued (Bose symmetrisation, standard).
\item[(vi)] (One generation.) For the left-handed content $(1,1)_{0} \oplus (1,\bar 3)_{-2/3} \oplus (2,3)_{1/6} \oplus (2,1)_{-1/2} \oplus (1,1)_{1} \oplus (1,\bar 3)_{1/3}$ of Theorem \claimref{synthesis.anomaly-freedom-forces-slot-content} ($m = 1$), $d$ vanishes on the whole complexified gauge algebra $\mathfrak{sl}(3) \oplus \mathfrak{sl}(2) \oplus \C$ (numbers and the module's complex structure are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, the module read on the tower's floors, where $I_{4}$ commutes with the tower vectors) and $\mathrm{tr}\,X = 0$ for every $X$ (for the hypercharge this is $\mathrm{tr}\,Y = 0$, the imported mixed gravitational coefficient: a trace count, not a computed gauge-gravitational triangle); the cancellation is between fields (the quark doublet alone gives $\mathrm{tr}\,Y^{3} = \tfrac{1}{36}$) and holds generation by generation, for any number of generations.
\end{enumerate}
synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.technical: In the spacetime algebra the Dirac matrices are the vectors, the trace is four times the scalar part, and the chirality acts as $x \mapsto I_{4}xI_{4}$, the left $I_{4}$ inside the product and the unit, the right $I_{4}$, standing outside it, as the stored one-loop result requires on massive lines. Then the trace of the chirality element with four vectors is four times the pseudoscalar coefficient of their product. For the triangle with one axial and two vector vertices, regulated by Pauli-Villars fermions with weights summing to zero, contracting a vector vertex with its momentum turns the integrand into a difference of two-point terms shifted by that momentum, and since the regulators make those terms fall off fast enough the difference integrates to zero: both vector currents are conserved. Contracting the axial vertex gives the mass term $-2M$ times the pseudoscalar triangle plus terms that integrate to zero. For each regulator the pseudoscalar triangle's numerator is $M$ times a constant, $4\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}\,I_{4}$, with no loop-momentum dependence, so the regulator term tends to a finite limit as its mass grows: the axial divergence of the massless loop is $(1/(2\pi^{2}))\langle I_{4}\gamma^{\nu}k_{1}\gamma^{\rho}k_{2}\rangle_{0}$, depending on the regulators only through the sum of their weights. Contracted with polarisations this is the bilinear form of $\langle I_{4}F^{2}\rangle_{0} = -2E\cdot B$, the pseudoscalar part of the square of the field bivector. A chiral vertex collapses its projectors to one, so a Weyl loop carries half the Dirac anomaly with its chirality's sign, and a content of Weyl fields is anomalous through the symmetric tensor $\mathrm{tr}(X\{Y, Z\})$ (the standard reduction, argued here); for one stored generation that tensor vanishes on the whole gauge algebra, generation by generation, and the trace $\mathrm{tr}\,Y$ that enters the imported mixed gravitational condition is zero (a trace count, not a computed triangle). These are standard results (Adler; Bell and Jackiw, Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-adler-bell-jackiw-axial-anomaly}); what is new is their form in the spacetime algebra. Every covariant extension conserving both vector currents gives the same axial divergence (\claimref{synthesis.one-loop-vacuum-polarisation-extends-without-a-regulator-and-ward-preserving-extensions-differ-only-by-the-renormalisation-constants}(iii), given the imported existence of such extensions), so the value does not depend on the Pauli-Villars scheme.
synthesis.triangle-anomaly-in-the-spacet.lay: Some symmetries of classical fields fail once quantum effects are included; the classic case is the axial anomaly of a charged particle in an electromagnetic field, found in 1969. This result recomputes that anomaly in the series' own algebra of spacetime, using a standard method of taming the infinities. The anomaly comes out as the part of the squared electromagnetic field that measures how electric and magnetic fields line up, with the textbook strength. For a theory to be consistent, such anomalies must cancel between all the particles that feel a force; the result checks that they cancel within one generation of the series' particles, so the cancellation does not depend on how many generations there are.
